item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Kyle Tucker didn't start on Sunday, one day after fouling a ball off his right knee, but the Dodgers right fielder insisted that he felt fine. This was more of a chance to pair a rest day for Tucker with Monday's scheduled off day for the team.
"[The off day] wasn't planned. I just felt that after he took one off the knee, this would have been 10 in a row for him," manager Dave Roberts said Sunday. "He's playing well, played a lot. It's a chance to give him two days, then six in a row to finish the season."
The injury was in a much higher spot on his leg than the right shin fracture that cost him two months on the injured list during the 2024 season while with the Houston Astros.
Tucker did pinch-hit in the eighth inning on Sunday, and he's second on the Dodgers in games played (148), starts (141), and plate appearances (602), trailing only Freddie Freeman in all three categories. Tucker is playing the best baseball of his season at the moment with five home runs in his last 10 starts, hitting .417/.500/.972 since September 9.
Notes
Speaking of playing in the outfield on Tuesday, the Dodgers will likely activate center fielder Andy Pages off the injured list to play in the series opener against the San Diego Padres, after he missed the last 27 games after a fastball broke his left hand on August 21.
Pages at the end of this season will have two years, 155 days of major league service time and will be eligible for salary arbitration for the first time as a Super Two player, among the top 70 percent in service time among major leaguers with two years but not yet three years of service time. MLB Trade Rumors last week projected the cutoff for Super Two players this offseason to be two years, 134 days.
Longtime Dodgers third base coach Joey Amalfitano and knuckleballer Charlie Hough were honored on the field at Dodger Stadium prior to Sunday's game as the 2026 winners of the the Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award. This is the fifth year of the award, timed close to Lasorda's birthday, which is Tuesday.

item.title: [MLB.com] Top 9 things at stake in the final week

item.content:encoded:
The final week of the 2026 regular season has arrived and there is still much to be determined.
While six teams have clinched playoff spots and a few others are close, multiple playoff positions are still up for grabs. And from an individual perspective, there are awards that could be determined in the coming days.
Here’s what is at stake in the final week of the season.
Who will win the AL West and Central?
There’s no telling who will win these two divisions in the American League. The Rays have just about wrapped up the AL East, but the White Sox and Guardians are still battling for the AL Central, while the Rangers and Astros are battling for the West.
This is where things stand. The Rangers lead the Astros by one game in the AL West but Houston won the pivotal tiebreaker against Texas. That means if the two clubs end the season with the same record, the division would go to the Astros.
In the AL Central, the Guardians hold a one-game lead over the White Sox, but Chicago holds the tiebreaker advantage. Any tie between the two clubs means the White Sox would win the division.
Who gets the last AL Wild Card spot?
The AL West and Central battles are directly linked to what’s happening for the final Wild Card spot. It’s very likely that one of those four aforementioned teams will grab the last AL Wild Card spot, unless the Blue Jays have something to say about it. Right now, the White Sox have a fairly comfortable three-game lead over the Blue Jays and Astros.
Could Yordan still win the Triple Crown?
For a while, Yordan Alvarez looked like he might win the MLB Triple Crown, leading the Majors in average, home runs and RBIs. Now, the lefty slugger and presumptive AL MVP winner might merely finish first or second in average, home runs and RBIs. Heading into the final week, Alvarez has a slight edge in average (.313) over Chandler Simpson (.309) and is second in home runs (40) behind Junior Caminero (41) and second in RBIs (99) behind Pete Alonso (105). Alvarez could still snag the AL Triple Crown, but it’ll take a monstrous final week.
Simpson’s unique season and quest for an unusual batting title
Back to Simpson for a second, though. The Rays outfielder is having an excellent season, hitting for average, swiping bases and playing solid outfield defense. What he hasn’t done, though, is hit a single home run. The last hitter to win a batting title without hitting a home run was Rod Carew in 1972. Even if he doesn’t win, he could be the first qualified hitter to bat .300 without a home run since Luis Castillo in 1999.
Will Misiorowski win the ERA title?
It's been a remarkable season for Jacob Misiorowski, who has a 1.86 ERA and 247 strikeouts after Sunday's outing against the Orioles. Assuming he's in line for one more start next weekend -- even if it's abbreviated like his three-inning outing on Sunday -- Misiorowski is in line to join some impressive company. If he can hold his ERA edge over Cam Schlittler's 1.94 mark, he'd join 2021 Corbin Burnes (2.43 ERA in 2021) as the only Brewers to win an ERA title.
If Misiorowski keeps his ERA under two and gets to 250 strikeouts, there's some other fun company he'll join. He'd be just the 13th pitcher (15th instance) since earned runs became official in 1913 to finish a season with a sub-2 ERA and 250-plus strikeouts. The last to do so was Jacob deGrom in 2018.
Will Schwarber or PCA lead the Majors in home runs?
Kyle Schwarber led the National League with 56 home runs last year. As hard as it is to believe, though, Schwarber has never led the Majors in home runs. That could change this year, as the Phillies’ slugger is tied for the MLB lead with 45 homers. The last Phillie to pull that off was Ryan Howard in 2008, when he hit 48 homers and helped lead Philly to a World Series title.
Schwarber, though, has Pete Crow-Armstrong tied with him at the top. The surefire NL MVP has completely taken off this season with 45 homers, 38 stolen bases (more on this shortly), a .949 OPS and his usual excellent center field defense, which has led to an MLB-best 10.5 WAR, per FanGraphs. If PCA surpasses Schwarber, he’d be the first Cub to lead the NL in homers since Sammy Sosa’s 49 homers in 2002 and the first to lead the Majors in long balls since Sosa hit 50 in 2000.
Does PCA get to 40-40?
Crow-Armstrong is making all sorts of history this season. Reaching 10 WAR puts PCA in rarified territory and it seems very likely that the Cubs’ superstar center fielder will be a unanimous MVP winner, something no Cub has ever achieved. Crow-Armstrong is also a mere two stolen bases away from a 40-40 season, something no Cub has done and only six other MLB players have achieved.
Burleson vying to join impressive Cardinals history
Alec Burleson leads the Majors with 111 RBIs, putting him in line for some impressive Cardinals history. He’s looking to become the first Cardinal to lead the National League since Albert Pujols in 2010 and the first to lead the Majors in the category since Joe Torre drove in 137 runs in 1971. His stiffest competition is Cincinnati’s Sal Stewart, who sits at 110 RBIs entering the final week.
How does Verlander's final start go?
Justin Verlander returned to the Tigers for the 2026 season, which will be his final before retiring. Unfortunately, he only made one start in April and hasn't pitched since that point. The good news is he's lined up to pitch on Saturday at Detroit's Comerica Park, which will surely be a feel good moment and send off for the likely future Hall of Famer. Verlander can also add a few more strikeouts to his career total of 3,554.

item.title: [Cubbies Crib] Rule changes in last MLB CBA have helped Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong chase history
item.dc:creator: Jake Misener
item.description: Pete Crow-Armstrong is putting the finishing touches on a season for the ages - one that may very well go down as the best in the 150-year history of the Chicago Cubs. item.content:encoded:
Pete Crow-Armstrong is putting the finishing touches on a season for the ages - one that may very well go down as the best in the 150-year history of the Chicago Cubs. One last feather in his cap would be achieving a 40/40 season. To do that, he'll need two stolen bases over the next week to join one of baseball's most exclusive clubs.
He's already set a career-high with 38 bags, to go along with 45 home runs, 30 doubles and 107 runs batted in, but the 40/40 club would be the cherry on top. It feels like some context is important, though, because I feel like his bid for history is flying a bit under the radar outside Chicago - and rule changes made during the last MLB CBA talks could be to blame.
As Bob Nightengale of USA Today pointed out in his weekend column, just four players accomplished a 40/40 season prior to 2023: Jose Canseco, Barry Bonds, Alex Rodriguez and Alfonso Soriano. But since then, Ronald Acuna Jr. and Shohei Ohtani have both done it, and PCA could be the third with a strong final week.
Pete Crow-Armstrong on the brink of joining baseball's 40/40 club
That shouldn't take away from the accomplishments of Ohtani, Acuna Jr. or Crow-Armstrong. But we also shouldn't ignore the impact the rule changes have had on the game (which are exactly what the league hoped for when it made them). For context, in 2022, there were 2,486 stolen bases across Major League Baseball. The 2026 regular season isn't even over yet and we're already over 3,000.
PCA pseudo-joined that group of aforementioned stars with a double in the early innings Sunday, becoming just the sixth player in MLB history with 30+ doubles, 35+ stolen bases and 40+ homers in a season (the others being Ohtani, Acuna Jr., Soriano, Rodriguez and Canseco). As he closes in on 40/40 and the first MVP award of his career, rule change or not, Crow-Armstrong has shown his breakout 2025 was no fluke and he's ready to lead the charge into the next era of Chicago Cubs baseball.

item.title: [Currently.com] Phillies’ Zack Wheeler Embraces Final Starts, ‘Winding Down’ Ahead Of Retirement
item.dc:creator: Peter Chawaga; Contributor

item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies are entering the final weeks of the regular season with their margin for error narrowing. Their bullpen has remained a major concern, putting even more pressure on a starting rotation that has already dealt with injuries and inconsistency as October approaches.
Until emerging star Jesus Luzardo can return from the injured list, questions about the bridge between the team's rotation and elite closer Jhoan Duran will continue to grow. The Phillies continue to rely on questionable bridge relievers, like Alex McFarlane, Jonathan Bowlan and Tim Mayza.
"Until then, the bridge from Zack Wheeler and Cristopher Sanchez to Duran is murkier than ever," Matt Gelb wrote for The Athletic. "McFarlane, a veteran of 15 big-league games, is vital to everything. So is Bowlan's health. Mayza has gained importance. So has Chase Shugart, used mostly as a long reliever all season."
Among the starts, that uncertainty makes Wheeler's role particularly important as the veteran right-hander approaches a crossroads in his career.
Philadelphia Phillies Superstar Zack Wheeler Reflects On Final Remaining Starts
Amid an impressive return from surgery and with only one year remaining on his contract, Wheeler acknowledged that he is nearing the end of his playing days.
Wheeler is pitching at a high level again after a blood clot near his right shoulder led to surgery for venous thoracic outlet syndrome, forcing him to miss the remainder of that season.
He returned in April and has since reestablished himself as arguably the Phillies' most important rotation anchor. On September 16, Wheeler threw seven scoreless innings against the Washington Nationals, allowing four hits and one walk while striking out five. The performance lowered his ERA to 2.99 through 26 starts.
But even while competing at that level, Wheeler has begun looking at some of his remaining road trips differently. During a trip this season to the Boston Red Sox's Fenway Park, for instance, Wheeler drank in the historic surroundings as he acknowledged he could be preparing for his final start in that ballpark.
"Part of that's me probably winding down my career," Wheeler explained, according to The Philadelphia Inquirer's Scott Lauber. "I've only got one more year on this contract. I don't know if I'm going to play after that. But just going into those stadiums that maybe I won't go back to — Anaheim, Detroit, Boston — we're not going to play those teams there next year. So, kind of just soaking that in and enjoying it a little bit more this year than most years."
Philadelphia Phillies Relying On Zack Wheeler As Career Nears End
The timing of Wheeler's comments is notable for a Phillies team that needs its starting pitchers to carry an increasingly heavy load.
Wheeler's recent rebound has provided some stability. He followed a difficult stretch in August with four consecutive starts of at least six innings while allowing one run or fewer, including his seven-inning shutout of Washington.
Now, the Phillies need that version of Wheeler to continue into October.
For Wheeler, however, the remaining starts also carry a personal significance. Whether his current contract represents the final chapter remains undecided, but he has clearly begun appreciating the possibility that some of these ballparks and moments could be among his last.
This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] 5 Free Agents Mets Should Pursue to Help Build a 2027 Contender (Including Tarik Skubal)
item.dc:creator: Mike Phillips; Unknown

item.content:encoded:
The Mets have just nine games left in the season, and all of the attention is already shifting to the 2027 campaign. There are a lot of questions that the Mets have to answer this winter, and seeing the fans' over-the-top reaction to Pete Alonso's return this week shows how much work the front office needs to do to win back the trust of its fan base.
The free agent market is a bit thin this year, but it does have a few players who could help the Mets bolster their roster, particularly in the pitching department. That tally doesn't include Bo Bichette, whose opt-out decision will also play a significant role in how much money President of Baseball Operations David Stearns has to work with in free agency.
That said, let's dive into five potential free agents that the Mets should pursue this winter.
1. LHP Tarik Skubal
We took a deeper dive into the Tarik Skubal fit for the Mets last week, but it is fair to wonder if the fans' vitriolic display at Citi Field this week may inspire Steve Cohen to go for the top pitcher on the board as a make-good to them.
There are certainly injury risks with Skubal, but there isn't a better pitcher on the board, and his arrival would push the rest of the current rotation into more appropriate roles, starting with Nolan McLean as one of the best No. 2's in baseball.
2. LHP Robbie Ray
Skubal alone would bolster the Mets' rotation but Stearns should also look to add a veteran for the middle of the rotation who can give them quality innings. Enter Robbie Ray, a former Cy Young winner who is 13-8 with a 3.60 ERA in 30 appearances (including 29 starts) between the Giants and Padres.
The Mets would get a veteran lefty who has thrown at least 162.2 innings in four of the past six seasons, with the only exceptions being the 2022 and 2023 campaigns when he missed significant time rehabbing from Tommy John surgery. Putting Ray as the Mets' third starter would allow Stearns to bump Christian Scott down to the No. 4 spot and have healthy competition for the fifth between Sean Manaea, Jonah Tong, Zac Thornton and a slew of other depth options.
3. 1B/3B Alec Bohm
First base is one of the bigger questions on the Mets' roster, and they can't go into next season hoping that the combination of Jared Young, Mark Vientos, Brett Baty and Jorge Polanco can solve it. One good fit here could be Alec Bohm, who is hitting .251 with 15 home runs, 84 RBIs and a .707 OPS in 534 at-bats for the Phillies.
If the Mets feel like Young can be part of a first base platoon, then Bohm would make sense as a partner since he is very strong against lefties, batting .293 with seven homers, 36 RBIs and an .828 OPS against them in 179 at-bats. Veteran Paul Goldschmidt could also fill a platoon role with Young, but the Mets would be better served going with someone in his prime as opposed to a Goldschmidt-type towards the end of his career.
Bohm's ability to play both infield corners could also be helpful in the event Bichette opts out.
4. OF Ramon Laureano
The Mets' decision to move on from Tyrone Taylor (via trade) and Luis Robert Jr. (via waivers) has left them with an all-left-handed-hitting outfield of Juan Soto, A.J. Ewing and Carson Benge. While all three are capable starters, it would make sense to add a veteran option who can hit right-handed since Nick Morabito appears to need more minor league seasoning to be ready for that fourth outfielder role.
A good buy-low fit here could be Ramón Laureano, who has missed most of the season after undergoing surgery to repair a torn labrum in his right hip in May. Laureano can play both outfield corners and is just a year removed from a solid 2025 campaign where he hit .281 with 24 homers, 76 RBIs and an .855 OPS, so adding him on a one-year prove-it deal could give the Mets more flexibility to protect Juan Soto's health with DH days or sit one of Ewing or Benge against tough lefties.
5. RHP Evan Phillips
The Mets bullpen's strong performance post-deadline has lessened their need to go big-game hunting at the back end of the unit, but they still need to add a proven setup reliever to their mix. One name who could offer good value is Evan Phillips, who has pitched to a 3.68 ERA and 1.23 WHIP in 27 appearances for the Dodgers this season.
Phillips missed time with injuries this year but does have closing experience with Los Angeles, which could be valuable if Devin Williams struggles in his second year with the Mets. The injury issues Phillips had may drive his price down to a one- or two-year contract, which would be right up Stearns' wheelhouse and make him a good complement to the likes of Williams, Kodai Senga, Reed Garrett and Daniel Duarte in the relief mix.

Mike Phillips is a contributor to the Mets On SI site. Mike has been covering the Mets since 2011 for various websites, including Metstradamus and Kiners Korner. Mike has a Masters Degree from Iona University in Sports Communications and Media and also has experience covering the NFL and college basketball on FanSided. Mike also hosts his own New York sports based podcast. You can follow Mike on Twitter/X and Instagram: @MPhillips331.

item.content:encoded:
These MLB sluggers are chasing an ugly record. Will history be made this week?
Philadelphia Phillies DH Kyle Schwarber and Chicago White Sox shortstop Colson Montgomery are nearing some dubious baseball history.
Schwarber and Montgomery each have 216 strikeouts entering the final week of the season, endangering Mark Reynolds’ all-time record of 223 strikeouts set in 2009.
Yet, it hardly bothers them.
“Guys who strike out a lot," Montgomery told reporters, “you see them, but what do they also do? They hit a lot of homers and drive a lot of guys in.”
Montgomery has 31 homers and 87 RBIs. Schwarber has 45 homers and 95 RBIs.
It's Montgomery's first 200-strikeout season but the third for Schwarber – who broke his career high of 215, set in 2023.
Both sluggers' teams have everything to play for in the days to come with the Phillies fighting for positioning in the NL wild card and the White Sox trading blows with the Cleveland Guardians for the AL Central crown, meaning they'll both see a regular number of at-bats.

item.content:encoded:
San Diego Padres youngster Ethan Salas stole the show on Saturday exactly like Manny Machado did over a decade ago.
Salas came up to the plate as a pinch hitter in a tie game against the Miami Marlins at Petco Park in San Diego, Calif. The 20-year-old had a man on third with one out in the bottom of the 10th inning.
All Salas needed was a deep fly ball to drive in the game-winning run, with Jake Cronenworth standing 90 feet away. He did even better by hitting an 0-2 pitch up the middle for a walk-off RBI single.
IT'S TARPS OFF FOR ETHAN SALAS pic.twitter.com/KYoyQJaBY3
— San Diego Padres (@Padres) September 20, 2026
Ethan Salas is the youngest player with a walk-off hit since Manny Machado did in 2012 at 20 years and 69 days old
The youngest player with a pinch-hit walk-off hit in at least the last 50 years. pic.twitter.com/3C42sAUoAb
The Padres are right in the thick of a competitive NL Wild Card race with the Chicago Cubs and the Philadelphia Phillies. San Diego was outside the postseason picture a couple of weeks ago, but has since won 13 of its last 15 games to maintain a stranglehold on one of the NL Wild Card spots.
Saturday’s contest was only Salas’ 11th in the majors. He went 0-for-14 in his first six MLB games but has gone 4-for-12 since then — including a clutch hit to secure a Padres win.

item.title: [Diario Libre] Junior Caminero no alcanza a Yordan Álvarez con el guante
item.dc:creator: Nathanael P; Eacute; Rez Ner; Oacute
item.description: Yordan Álvarez edificó con los porcentajes un muro que parece impenetrable para merecerse el premio al Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana. En la semana final de la fase regular saca 34 puntos sobre Junior Caminero en promedio de bateo (.313-.277), uno de los renglones que encabeza detrás de la Triple Corona. item.content:encoded:
Yordan Álvarez edificó con los porcentajes un muro que parece impenetrable para merecerse el premio al Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana. En la semana final de la fase regular saca 34 puntos sobre Junior Caminero en promedio de bateo (.313-.277), uno de los renglones que encabeza detrás de la Triple Corona.
Pero donde se separa del resto por cuerpo entero es en la principal referencia ofensiva de hoy, el OPS. Es el único en toda la MLB que supera los 1.000 (1.027), 135 puntos sobre el .892 del de los Rays. La superioridad es apreciable en la frecuencia de embasarse (.430-.363) y de extrabases (.597-.515).
Ante esa respetable ventaja porcentual, que hace que en Las Vegas den como un hecho su MVP, clasifique Houston o no, los partidarios de Caminero argumentan el aporte defensivo que hace el dominicano al salir a diario al terreno.
En la ecuación que arroja el WAR de FanGraphs y Baseball-Reference, el ajuste posicional le da a Caminero +2.5 carreras como antesalista y Álvarez -17.5 como un bateador designado que no aporta con el guante.
Antes de salir al terreno, el quisqueyano sale delante, pero el de Las Tunas remonta con el madero hasta liderar en esa casilla.
Lo que dice la Sabermetría
Hay métricas que dejan bien parado a "La Máxima" como 3B, otras no. Baseball Info Solutions dice que ha salvado 4 carreras defensivas, un salto impresionante con relación a las -5 de 2025.
Sin embargo, Savant "opina" todo lo contrario. En OAA saca -12 out por encima del promedio, es decir, la cantidad de outs que hace con relación al antesalista average.
El cálculo se apoya en cámaras e inteligencia artificial que miden desde la velocidad de salida del batazo, el ángulo del roletazo, la distancia recorrida hacia la bola y la fuerza/precisión del disparo a la base.
En carreras prevenidas, medido por Statscat, queda con -9. Es líder en errores entre los defensores de la esquina caliente (19) en la Americana.
A pesar de que Álvarez, quien ha jugado 24 partidos en el prado izquierdo (con -5 DRS) y 129 como designado, queda con -1.7 WAR defensivos al sumar las 6.7 ofensivas totaliza 6.3, líder de todo el béisbol. Caminero, con 0.7 defensivas, tiene 5.7 en total.
De las 25.6 WAR de los jugadores de posición de los Rays, Caminero lidera el aporte con 5.7 (22.2 %). En cambio, Álvarez es responsable de 6.3 de las 19 de los Astros o el 33.1 %.
Dicho esto, el cubano ha sido más determinante para Houston que Caminero para Tampa, a pesar del abismo competitivo entre ese salvaje Este y el mediocre Oeste.

[중앙이코노미뉴스 조용우] 샌프란시스코 자이언츠 이정후가 3경기 연속 안타를 기록했으며, 애틀랜타 브레이브스 김하성은 5경기 연속 안타를 치지 못했다.
이정후는 21일 미국 캘리포니아주 로스앤젤레스 유니클로필드 앳 다저스타디움에서 열린 LA 다저스와의 방문 경기에 2번 타자 우익수로 출전해 2타수 1안타 1볼넷을 골랐다. 그는 1회 외야 뜬공, 3회 볼넷을 기록한 뒤 6회 우전 안타를 쳤고, 7회말 수비 때 교체됐다. 이정후의 시즌 타율은 0.276이다. 샌프란시스코는 이날 다저스에 1-3으로 패했다.
김하성은 같은 날 휴스턴 애스트로스와의 방문 경기에 9번 타자 유격수로 나서 삼진 2개와 땅볼, 뜬공으로 타격을 마쳤다. 김하성이 침묵했지만, 애틀랜타는 휴스턴을 4-2로 제압했다. 이 승리로 애틀랜타는 3년 만에 내셔널리그(NL) 동부지구 1위를 확정했다.

item.content:encoded:
人気ランキング
コラム一覧
8-1とリードする場面で迎えた8回に今季25号となる推定飛距離440フィート（134m）の特大ダメ押し弾を放ち、チームの9-1の大勝に貢献した。また、9回の守備ではジャンピングキャッチに加え、スライディングキャッチも披露するなど、攻守において存在感を発揮した。
◆試合結果
カ　ブ　ス｜1 0 4 0 3 0 0 1 0｜9
レ　ッ　ズ｜0 0 0 1 0 0 0 0 0｜1
メジャーリーグ中継2026
試合後、現地メディア『CBSスポーツ』は電子版に「カブスのセイヤ・スズキが日曜に今季25号弾を放つ」と題した記事を掲載し、「スズキは4打数無安打1三振として8回の最後の打席を迎えると、その打席で今季25号となる本塁打を放った」とこの試合における和製スラッガーの打席を振り返った。
そして、「これはこの実力派外野手にとって今月初の一発であり、シーズン通算本塁打数は、昨季レギュラーシーズン151試合で記録した32本に次ぐ、自身のMLBキャリアで2番目に多い数字となった」と伝えた。
続けて記事では、今季の鈴木について、「ワールド・ベースボール・クラシックで負った右膝の捻挫により、2026年シーズンは開幕に出遅れこそしたものの、この32歳の強打者は、今季も打撃面で素晴らしいシーズンを送っている」としている。
一方、『FOXスポーツ』は試合後、電子版に「クロウ＝アームストロングが45号本塁打を放ち、カブスがレッズを9-1で下してプレーオフ進出へ一歩前進」と題した記事を掲載。
その上で、「シカゴ（87勝69敗）はマジックナンバーを1に減らしており、同日遅れて行われる試合でダイヤモンドバックスがヤンキースに敗れれば、プレーオフ進出が確定する」と伝えた。
なお、件の試合はダイヤモンドバックスが勝利したため、カブスのプレーオフ進出決定は、現地21日以降へ持ち越しとなっている。
また記事では、パドレスと87勝69敗で並びながら、タイブレーカーによりワイルドカード1位に立つカブスが、「この順位を維持すれば、ワイルドカード・シリーズでのホーム開催権を獲得できる」と指摘。
さらに「ダイヤモンドバックス、パドレス、フィリーズとの直接対決の成績では、カブスが優位に立っている」と、ナショナル・リーグの第4シード獲得へ向け、ノースサイダーズが優位に立っていることを伝えている。

item.content:encoded:
The Colorado Rockies are 57–99.
Purple Row After Dark: If the Rockies could steal one player
An absurd rule for absurd times: if the worst team in baseball could steal one player from a playoff club, who should the Rockies take?
One more loss will give them their fourth consecutive 100-loss season, and they are almost certainly going to finish with the worst record in baseball.
These are absurd times for the Rockies, so I have devised an appropriately absurd rule to help them out.
The team with the worst record in baseball gets to steal one player from a playoff team.
There are, naturally, some restrictions. We’re freezing the playoff field as it stood before games on Sunday, September 20. The player has to come from one of those 12 teams, cannot be a pending free agent, and you cannot take the player who leads his team in FanGraphs WAR. The Rockies also inherit the player’s existing contract.
No, one player is not suddenly turning the Rockies into a contender. But could one poached superstar at least keep this thing from becoming five consecutive 100-loss seasons?
Here’s the board:
| Team | Off limits: fWAR leader | Highest available fWAR | Other players worth considering |
| Rays | Junior Caminero (5.2) | Drew Rasmussen (4.7) | Jonathan Aranda (3) |
| Guardians | Parker Messick (4.6) | Steven Kwan (3.4) | Gavin Williams (3.4), Brayan Rocchio (3.3), José Ramírez (2.2) |
| Rangers | Ezequiel Duran (4.6) | Jacob deGrom (4.2) | Josh Jung (2.9), Wyatt Langford (2.8) |
| Yankees | Cam Schlittler (6.1) | Ben Rice (4) | Cody Bellinger (3.9), Aaron Judge (2) |
| Red Sox | Willson Contreras (4.1) | Payton Tolle (4) | Ceddanne Rafaela (3.9), Ranger Suárez (3.7) |
| White Sox | Miguel Vargas (5) | Chase Meidroth (4) | Tristan Peters (3.9), Sean Burke (3.1) |
| Brewers | Jacob Misiorowski (6.3) | Brice Turang (5.4) | Jackson Chourio (4), Jake Bauers (3.6) |
| Dodgers | Shohei Ohtani (6.7) | Yoshinobu Yamamoto (4.7) | Max Muncy (4.3), Andy Pages (3.9) |
| Braves | Chris Sale (5.7) | Michael Harris II (4) | Matt Olson (4), Drake Baldwin (3.1) |
| Cubs | Pete Crow-Armstrong (10.2) | Alex Bregman (5) | Dansby Swanson (3.6) |
| Padres | Fernando Tatis Jr. (5) | Jackson Merrill (4) | Ty France (3.8), Mason Miller (3.7) |
| Phillies | Cristopher Sánchez (5.8) | Jesús Luzardo (5.6) | Zack Wheeler (3.5), Bryce Harper (3.4) |
For me, the choice comes down to Brice Turang, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Aaron Judge.
Turang is probably the sensible choice.
At 5.4 fWAR, he would easily lead the Rockies, giving them a legitimate top-end player while immediately solving second base for the foreseeable future. He’s 26, hitting .266/.367/.441 with an .808 OPS, and brings value on both sides of the ball with elite range, strong baserunning and a 95th-percentile walk rate.
It would be a very easy way to make the roster better.
But the Rockies really need starting pitching.
Enter Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
He’s 14–8 with a 2.51 ERA, 178 strikeouts and a 0.87 WHIP over 179 innings. His Statcast profile is just as impressive: 100th-percentile pitching run value, 99th-percentile fastball run value, 95th-percentile offspeed run value and a 91st-percentile xERA.
Pitchers are risky, and Yamamoto comes with a lot of money attached. But it’s hard to argue with either the profile or the results, and the addition of the Penner family makes absorbing that contract a lot easier to imagine.
Speaking of high-priced items...
Aaron Judge.
Judge being available is basically a loophole created by our own stupid rule. Injuries have limited him to just 285 plate appearances, which is why he sits at only 2 fWAR, but he’s still hitting .241/.360/.511 with 15 home runs.
And the underlying numbers are still very much Judge: a .396 xwOBA, .569 xSLG, 94.0 mph average exit velocity and a 57.5% hard-hit rate.
It is very hard to look at that and say, “No thanks.”
After all, Aaron Judge is the type of hitter that, if he were playing 81 games a year at Coors Field, I might take out a small loan for season tickets.
So who are you stealing?

item.content:encoded:
CLEVELAND -- - Gavin Williams threw seven shutout innings, Jo Adell had an RBI infield single and the Cleveland Guardians beat the Athletics 1-0 Sunday to remain atop the AL Central.
Steven Kwan added three hits for Cleveland, which posted its seventh series sweep of the season and third at home.
The Guardians (81-75) are one game in front of the Chicago White Sox, who defeated Detroit 8-1. They finish the season on the road with series against Boston and Kansas City.
Williams (14-8) gave up three hits and struck out nine to move into the American League lead with 244 strikeouts. Toronto's Dylan Cease is in second with 239. It is the 13th time in 31 starts this season that the right-hander has had at least nine strikeouts.
Cade Smith worked 1 1/3 innings for his 39th save in 44 opportunities.
The Athletics were swept for the second straight series and lost all six games on their road trip.
José Ramírez led off the fourth with a double down the right-field line, advanced to third on Chase DeLauter's fly out to left and scored on Jo Adell's infield single. Pitcher Jack Perkins (3-12) fielded the soft grounder on the grass in front of the mound, but his throw hit Adell in the back as he was in the basepath.
Athletics manager Mark Kotsay was ejected for the third time this season for agruing the call.
Perkins went six innings and allowed one run on four hits.
The Athletics' best chance came in the eighth inning when they had runners on second and third with one out. Hunter Gaddis struck out pinch-hitter Carlos Cortes and Smith whiffed Henry Bolte.
Up next
Athletics: Return home to face the Los Angeles Angels on Tuesday. LHP Brady Brasso (1-3, 4.50 ERA) will take the mound.
Guardians: LHP Parker Messic (12-9, 2.57 ERA) goes on Tuesday to start a three-game series at Boston.
------

item.title: [UNANIMO Deportes] Nolan Arenado lidera remontada de Diamondbacks ante Yankees - UNANIMO Deportes
item.dc:creator: Juan David Perez
item.description: Los Arizona Diamondbacks volvieron a demostrar que saben reaccionar cuando están contra las cuerdas. Este domingo, una noche inspirada de Nolan Arenado, quien conectó su tercer grand slam de la temporada, fue clave para que Arizona remontara y derrotara 8-4 a los New York Yankees. - LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡José Ramírez llega a las 1,000 carreras impulsadas! - LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Atlanta Braves aseguran su boleto a los playoffs! - LEER MÁS SOBRE: New York Yankees 9- 2 Diamondbacks: Resultados y crónica
item.content:encoded:
Los Arizona Diamondbacks volvieron a demostrar que saben reaccionar cuando están contra las cuerdas. Este domingo, una noche inspirada de Nolan Arenado, quien conectó su tercer grand slam de la temporada, fue clave para que Arizona remontara y derrotara 8-4 a los New York Yankees.
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡José Ramírez llega a las 1,000 carreras impulsadas!
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Atlanta Braves aseguran su boleto a los playoffs!
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: New York Yankees 9- 2 Diamondbacks: Resultados y crónica
La jugada que terminó por cambiar el rumbo del encuentro llegó en la quinta entrada. Los Diamondbacks habían conseguido llenar las bases frente al abridor de Nueva York, Will Warren, quien dejó el montículo para darle paso al relevista Brent Headrick.
El pitcher logró retirar a Geraldo Perdomo con un ponche para conseguir el segundo out, pero después vino el descontrol. Headrick otorgó una base por bolas a Corbin Carroll, situación que permitió que Arizona sumara una carrera y dejara las bases listas para Arenado.
Con cuenta de 2-1, el tercera base no perdonó. Arenado encontró el lanzamiento y mandó la pelota por encima de la barda para completar el grand slam y darle la vuelta al partido. Fue el noveno cuadrangular con las bases llenas de su carrera, además de que alcanzó al cubano Yordan Álvarez, de los Houston Astros, como líder de las Grandes Ligas en grand slams durante esta temporada.
Pero el poder ofensivo de Arizona no se limitó a Arenado. Perdomo también tuvo una tarde productiva al conectar un sencillo productor en la primera entrada y posteriormente un triple que llevó otra carrera al plato durante el séptimo episodio.
Los Yankees, por su parte, habían respondido con fuerza en el tercer inning. Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. y Spencer Jones conectaron cuadrangulares consecutivos dentro de esa entrada frente al abridor de Arizona, Corbin Burnes, para mantener con vida a Nueva York.
Sin embargo, la ofensiva neoyorquina se apagó después de ese episodio. El bullpen de Arizona tomó el control y, encabezado por Justin Martínez, consiguió limitar a los Yankees a solamente tres imparables durante las últimas 6 entradas. Martínez se apuntó la victoria, la tercera de su temporada, con marca de 3-0.
Suscríbete al Newsletter de Unanimo y recibe gratis las últimas noticias. Dale click aquí
Arenado héroe de Arizona
Con este triunfo, los Diamondbacks llegaron a 47 victorias conseguidas después de comenzar perdiendo, la cifra más alta de las Grandes Ligas. Arizona continúa además en la pelea con los Philadelphia Phillies por el último boleto de comodín de la Liga Nacional, aunque todavía se encuentra cuatro juegos por detrás cuando restan seis encuentros.
Del otro lado, los Yankees aún conservan posibilidades matemáticas de pelear por el Este de la Liga Americana, aunque necesitan cerrar la temporada con victorias y esperar resultados favorables. Nueva York comenzará el martes una serie de cuatro partidos ante los Tampa Bay Rays, actuales líderes divisionales, en territorio neoyorquino.
Por ahora, Arizona celebra una remontada más en una temporada en la que ha convertido los partidos complicados en una de sus principales características. Y esta vez, el golpe decisivo tuvo nombre y apellido: Nolan Arenado.

item.description: Estados Unidos.- Los mexicanos José Ignacio Rodríguez, Brandon Valenzuela y Alejandro Osuna tuvieron destacada participación en la jornada de este domingo 20 de septiembre de 2026 en las Grandes Ligas, durante el juego que ganaron los Azulejos de Toronto por 7-2 a los Rangers de Texas. El “Tiburón” Rodríguez, pitcher de los Blue Jays de Toronto originario de Oaxaca, lanzó la séptima entrada en blanco dos días después de su debut en Major League Baseball (MLB), mientras que el oriundo de Los Moch
item.content:encoded:
Estados Unidos.- Los mexicanos José Ignacio Rodríguez, Brandon Valenzuela y Alejandro Osuna tuvieron destacada participación en la jornada de este domingo 20 de septiembre de 2026 en las Grandes Ligas, durante el juego que ganaron los Azulejos de Toronto por 7-2 a los Rangers de Texas.
El “Tiburón” Rodríguez, pitcher de los Blue Jays de Toronto originario de Oaxaca, lanzó la séptima entrada en blanco dos días después de su debut en Major League Baseball (MLB), mientras que el oriundo de Los Mochis, Alex Osuna, pegó 2 hits en 4 turnos por parte de los Rangers de Texas, en tanto que Brandon Valenzuela se fue de 3-1 también como parte de los canadienses.
Buen relevo del “Tibu” Rodríguez con los Toronto Blue Jays
Después de debutar el pasado 18 de septiembre con una entrada y tercios en blanco, con un hit y dos ponches ante los Rangers, José Ignacio Rodríguez volvió a la acción este domingo en el estadio Globe Life Field en territorio texano.
Sugerimos: ¡Debut mexicano! José Rodríguez se estrena con Azulejos de Toronto en Grandes Ligas
El “Tibu” ingresó al montículo en el séptimo inning y trabajó una entrada completa de un imparable y un chocolate, para mantener su efectividad en 0.00. Rodríguez inició su labor con un hit en contra de parte de Evan Carter. Enseguida, Wyatt Langford elevó de out al izquierdo, Corey Seager entregó el segundo tercio con fly al derecho y finalmente Josh Lung fue ponchado tirándole a una recta de 97 millas por hora.
Alex Osuna se fue de 4-2 por los Rangers de Texas
En el mismo enfrentamiento en Glob Life Field que registró asistencia de 33 mil 694 aficionados, el nativo de Los Mochis, Alejandro “Cuate” Osuna, bateó de 4-2 como quinto tolete de los Rangers de Texas.
Te podría interesar: “Se siente muy bonito”: Alex Osuna al cumplir su sueño de jugar en el Clásico Mundial de Beisbol
Osuna Quintero, de 23 años de edad, conectó su primer imparable del juego en el segundo inning ante los envíos de Spencer Miles, esto hacia el jardín central, mientras que, en la octava, el toletero zurdo volvió a pegar hit, esto ante Tyler Rogers hacia el prado izquierdo.
Brandon Valenzuela se fue de 3-1 en el triunfo de los Azulejos
El receptor originario de Hermosillo, Sonora, Brandon Valenzuela, también tuvo buena jornada este domingo al conectar un imparable en tres turnos, como octavo bat de los Azulejos de Toronto.
El bateador zurdo de 25 años de edad disparó sencillo en la sexta entrada ante el también zurdo Robert García, en un domingo de 3-1 con una base por bolas negociada.

item.content:encoded:
Misiorowski allowed a hit and struck out four without walking a batter over three shutout innings in a no-decision versus the Orioles on Sunday. Per Adam McCalvy of MLB.com, this was an intentionally planned short outing for Misiorowski to keep his innings in check ahead of the postseason.
McCalvy adds that Misiorowski is expected to see more regular usage in his last projected start of the regular season at home versus the Cardinals, which will line him up to take the mound during the ALDS. Since the All-Star break, Misiorowski has allowed just 16 runs (15 earned) over 58.1 innings, adding an 80:15 K:BB in that span. For the year, he's at a 1.86 ERA, 0.80 WHIP and 247:42 K:BB through 169.1 innings over 29 starts. The good news for fantasy managers is that Misiorowski is expected to have one more start even if the Brewers clinch everything they can before it's his turn to pitch again.

item.content:encoded:
Twins Video
Box Score:
Starting Pitcher: Dean Kremer: 6 IP, 1 H, 0 ER, 3 BB, 8 K (96 Pitches, 60 Strikes, 62.5%)
Home Runs: Alan Roden (1)
Top 3 WPA: Kremer (0.28), Josh Bell (0.18), Roden (0.13)
Win Probability Chart (Via BaseballSavant):

The Twins are in full "let's see what we have for next year" mode. Sunday found them finishing up a series against a team that is always planning for next year (though rarely making decisions that support that vision): the L.A. Angels.
That meant Walker Jenkins hitting leadoff, the return of Alan Roden, and Ben Ross playing shortstop. Dean Kremer took the mound for the Twins, opposing Ryan Johnson—who, like many Angels pitchers, has had an encouraging second half.
The Twins had a hard time squaring up Johnson, who has a funky, quick delivery with lots of side-to-side movement. There was a lot of weak contact on the ground until the third inning, when with one out, Jenkins legged out an infield single and Brooks Lee followed with a hard single to right. Josh Bell looped in a single to score Jenkins, and Roden delivered yet another single to score Lee. That made it 2-0 Twins.
Kremer wasn't at his sharpest early, with his velocity down a bit and looking a little off in terms of command. But he bore down when he had to, getting the light-hitting Angels to chase and taking advantage of the fact they burned all their challenges by the second inning. They didn't collect their first hit until the fourth, when Vaughn Grissom singled, but he was quickly erased on a double-play grounder from catcher Moisés Ballesteros.
Lee and Bell peppered Johnson with a couple more singles in the fifth, resulting in another RBI for Bell and chasing Johnson from the game. Kremer found his rhythm as the outing progressed, still staying out of the middle of the zone but throwing a few more strikes. He managed eight strikeouts through six innings, with a lot of whiffs on his four-seamer, despite touching 94 MPH just once.
The top of the sixth was very on brand for the Angels. With two outs, Emmanuel Rodríguez doubled off Jose Siri's glove. It was a play that would have been lauded as really nice had Siri made the catch, but in reality, he had plenty of time and barely had to jump. Regardless, Rodríguez deserved the break; he has really struggled lately. Ross singled him home, then tried to steal second. For some reason, Ross decided not to slide, which turned from a poor to a perfect choice when the ball scooted into center field. He coasted into third, then realized the Angels were picking up the ball with little urgency, turned on the jets, and scored.
The valiant visitors would add on in the seventh. Lee and Bell produced their third hits of the game, both singles. Roden then pulverized a first-pitch slider from lefty Sammy Peralta for a three-run homer. It's notable that Roden looked overmatched against Peralta in the fifth, eventually grounding out weakly, which shows a good ability to adjust on the fly.
Bailey Ober was brought out for the seventh, with the Twins juggling their starting rotation for the last week of the year. He hit 91 MPH and carved up the Angels lineup for the final three innings, allowing only a single (that was really a misplay by Ross at shortstop).
Stuff I'm Tracking:
- I'm going to miss the old version of the Angels, who were always all-in on the current season but made terrible baseball ops decisions, had a terrible culture, and apparently didn't even utilize pitch-tracking data until they revamped their pitching department this August. You just knew trading with them was playing chess while (former owner) Arte Moreno insisted his club play checkers. I still wouldn't have traded Kaelen Culpepper (plus more, reportedly) for Zach Neto, though.
- Royce Lewis looks cooked. No idea what the plan is for him next year. He did loop in a meaningless single in the seventh after striking out swinging his first three at-bats.
- Roden quietly has a .278/.349/.375 slash despite inconsistent playing time, this being his first game since August 26. You do root for a guy like him who hasn't done anything wrong; he's just been a victim of poor roster construction with all the left-handed outfielders on this team who need at-bats.
- Rodríguez is in the meat grinder, constantly behind in counts, and when he swings early, it's in play and an easy out. He did break an 0-17 with the double off Siri's glove in center.
- Is there a better pitcher in the league with a big lead than Ober? When he doesn't have to be perfect (and when he doesn't have to pace himself toward six innings), he looks great.
What’s Next: The Twins head to San Francisco to take on the floundering Giants. Ober was the scheduled starter, but with him pitching in relief, it may be Zebby Matthews taking the turn. Whoever it is will face Landen Roupp (9-14, 4.01 ERA), a solid but unspectacular righty who will be making his 30th start of the year. The Giants have been beset by injuries, and Luis Arraez is still second on the team in bWAR even though he was traded at the deadline. Crazy how a team that thought of itself as a contender is this bereft of talent, despite Rafael Devers quietly having his best overall year. (He's out for the rest of the year with a core muscle injury, leaving the Giants' own core rather damaged.)
Postgame Interviews: Coming Soon

item.dc:creator: Chris Lewis

item.content:encoded:
In the ninth inning against the Colorado Rockies, Seattle Mariners closer Andrés Muñoz left the game due to a knee injury. After the contest, the Mariners announced that their closer would undergo imaging tomorrow. Apparently, this has been an issue previously for Muñoz. Whether this could explain some of his struggles in 2026 remains to receive an explanation.
In 2026, Muñoz has a 4.11 ERA and 28 saves in 57 innings of play. He also has 10 blown saves on the year, the highest of his career. While 3.06 fielding independent pitching indicates a player who should rebound nicely in the future, the Mariners needed more from their star reliever this season. The bullpen, which used to be regarded as a strength for the Mariners, now need a massive makeover heading into this offseason. There simply are not enough reliable options, especially if Muñoz's knee injury lingers into next season.
Seattle Mariners fans are used to bullpen injuries especially when you consider how much time Matt Brash has missed over the last several years. However, a loss of Muñoz for any extended period of time next year could make the bullpen a frontline issue for this offseason.
Seattle Mariners Andrés Muñoz Dealing with Knee Injury
The Seattle Mariners still have yet to be officially eliminated from the playoffs, but the odds are extremely against them doing so. A loss to the Rockies on Sunday would've ended their hopes of making the postseason. Regardless, even with the Houston Astros and Texas Rangers enduring losses on Sunday, the Mariners only have a 0.2% of making the playoffs per Fangraphs. If Muñoz expects to miss extended time because of an injury, its hard to believe the Mariners realistically have any chance of making the postseason.
For now, the Mariners should have their eyes set for 2027, and the health of Muñoz should easily take priority over the rest of this season. In fact, it will only help Seattle make determinations on which relievers they will want to keep next year. Many of the players enter their first year of arbitration. With how the unit has performed in 2026, its unlikely that Seattle Mariners ownership will want to pay a significant amount for a mediocre bullpen.
The Failure to Acquire Jhoan Duran Continues to Haunt the Seattle Mariners
When the Seattle Mariners failed to acquire Jhoan Duran at the 2025 MLB Trade Deadline, the results that followed continue to plague them. They desperately needed Duran in the 2025 postseason especially against the Toronto Blue Jays. This season, he could've supported Muñoz in a high leverage role, allowing more opportunities for Muñoz to pitch in other innings outside of the ninth. Since the Philadelphia Phillies acquired Duran, he has compiled 3.6 wins above replacement, greatly higher than the entire Mariners bullpen in that period of time.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Seattle Mariners Andrés Muñoz Receives Concerning Update Before MLB Offseason appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [日刊スポーツ] 吉田正尚のレッドソックスがPS進出 史上４球団目、借金14から奇跡的快進撃 - ＭＬＢ : 日刊スポーツ
item.description: レッドソックスはレイズに敗戦したが、アストロズがブレーブスに2－4で敗戦したため、2年連続でワイルドカードでのポストシーズン（PS）進出を決めた。84勝72敗でア・リーグ東地区3位。ワイルドカードではヤンキースに続きア・リーグで2番目の進出決定となった。 6月24日時点で32勝46敗で借金14の低迷から奇跡的な快進撃を果たした。4月25日にはアレックス・コーラ監督と複数のコーチが解任。好調だった吉田正尚外野手（33）は左太もも裏の肉離れで8月16日から負傷者リスト入りした。だが傘下マイナーから抜擢（ばってき）されたチャド・トレーシー暫定監督が見事にチームを立て直した。MLB公式サイトのサラ・ラングス記者によると、借金14からPS進出を果たしたのは、1914年のブレーブス、74年のパイレーツ、05年のアストロズに続き史上4球団目だという。 トレーシー監督は現地メディアの取材に「目指す位置までこられたことはもちろんうれしいし、苦しい道のりを乗り越えてきただけに、さらに感無量。本当に長い道のりだったが、選手たちは負けずに突き進んだ」と話した。

item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman shared a graphic selfie Sunday after suffering a frightening facial injury from a foul ball during an MLB game.
Bregman was struck during the fourth inning of Chicago's 9-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Teammate Michael Busch fouled a pitch from Luis Mey, and the ball bounced into Bregman while he stood near the on-deck circle.
Bregman immediately left the game with blood visible on his face. He later underwent hospital testing after the ball struck him near his cheekbone.
The selfie, which he shared on his Instagram, showed significant swelling around Bregman's eye, along with facial cuts and a nosebleed. Especially the area below his eye had turned slightly black. He also included a message for supporters: "Thanks for all the messages, y'all. I'll be back 🙏."
Cubs manager Craig Counsell described the incident as a "terrible, terrible accident." He said the team's priority was getting positive medical results after Bregman was taken to the hospital.
The injury came during an important stretch for Chicago. The Cubs entered Sunday chasing a postseason berth and remained positioned for a National League wild-card spot.
Cubs must manage Alex Bregman's absence carefully
Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman (3) walks off the field after getting hit by a foul ball in the fourth inning in the game against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
Bregman had already contributed during Sunday's game before leaving. He delivered an RBI single in the first inning, helping Chicago build an early lead.
After Bregman exited, Matt Shaw replaced him as a pinch-hitter. Pedro Ramirez shifted to third base while Shaw moved to second.
The Cubs continued producing offensively without their veteran third baseman. Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 45th home run, while Michael Conforto and Seiya Suzuki also homered.
Chicago now faces a balance between its postseason push and Bregman's recovery. His defensive stability and veteran experience remain valuable during the final week.
Counsell said Bregman's general well-being came before baseball considerations. "I want to get a good report first," the manager said.
Bregman's message offered some optimism, but his return timeline remains unclear. The Cubs will need to await further medical updates before determining his availability.

item.content:encoded:
According to a prominent Canadian sports writer, Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is “embarrassed” by his poor season.
The six-time MLB All-Star is batting just .262 for the Blue Jays with an OPS of .694 and an OPS+ of 92, indicating his bat has been 8% below league average. He has only hit 9 home runs this season, including just 1 home run at Rogers Centre.
Considering Guerrero makes $40.2 million this season, the first year of a 14-year, $500 million contract, it has been downright shocking, to say the least, to see how poorly he has performed at the plate this year for Toronto, which is likely to miss the postseason after making it all the way to the World Series last year, in what can only be described as a massive fall from grace.
Vladimir Guerrero Jr. ‘Embarrassed’ by Poor Performance
According to Steve Simmons of the Toronto Sun, Guerrero has told those close to him that he is “embarrassed” by his play this season.
“Those who know Guerrero best say he is terribly embarrassed by his lack of production and he has grown tired of all the meetings, the coaching, the daily work, the noise that has not resulted in anything resembling success during this wayward season,” Simmons wrote.
Simmons also provided another interesting note, pointing out that in the event of an MLB lockout — which seems likely at this point — Guerrero will not be able to work with the Blue Jays coaches after December 1 to help get his swing back on track this offseason.
“What complicates the off-season for Guerrero and the Jays is the possibility of a lockout on Dec. 1. If that happens, and the Jays have plans to work with Guerrero to get his swing back, there can be no contact between the player and the team after that date,” Simmons wrote.
Blue Jays Likely to Miss Playoffs
With just six games left this season, the Blue Jays have a 77-79 record, and making the postseason is going to be next to impossible, as the team is currently 3 GB of the Chicago White Sox in the hunt for the third and final American League Wild Card spot.
That’s actually 4 GB, though, because the White Sox hold the tiebreaker over Toronto, so the odds of the Blue Jays making it to the postseason bracket are extremely slim right now.
The only hope Toronto has is that they win their last six games of the season to get to 83-79 and hope that Chicago goes 2-4 in their last six games to finish at 82-80.
Or, the Cleveland Guardians can go 2-4 over their final six games to also finish at 83-79, as Toronto at least has the tiebreaker over Cleveland.
With that in mind, math is not on the Blue Jays’ side right now, as time is running out this season and there simply aren’t enough games left for Toronto to get into the postseason bracket.
And fairly or unfairly, since it is a team sport, Guerrero’s bad season with the bat is a big reason why the team isn’t going anywhere this year.

item.title: [MLB.com] Alvarez calls players' meeting to rally Astros after tough series vs. Braves
item.dc:creator: Brian McTaggart
item.description: HOUSTON -- The frustration oozed out of Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez with every word he spoke to reporters in a hushed clubhouse on Sunday afternoon. It was only moments before that the stoic Alvarez did something he hasn’t done much in his career, speaking up in a players’ meeting following a sweep at the hands of the Braves. “Basically for us, it was three slaps in the face they gave us right in front of our fans, especially,” Alvarez said through an interpreter. “Just use tomorrow to take it
item.content:encoded:
HOUSTON -- The frustration oozed out of Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez with every word he spoke to reporters in a hushed clubhouse on Sunday afternoon. It was only moments before that the stoic Alvarez did something he hasn’t done much in his career, speaking up in a players’ meeting following a sweep at the hands of the Braves.
“Basically for us, it was three slaps in the face they gave us right in front of our fans, especially,” Alvarez said through an interpreter. “Just use tomorrow to take it as a reset day and rest, and then the only thing left is to go out there and win the six games we have left.”
Six games on the road -- two against the Mariners in Seattle and four against the A’s in West Sacramento -- are the only games still guaranteed on the Astros’ schedule this season, but they’re hoping for more. Sunday afternoon’s 4-2 loss to the Braves at Daikin Park was Houston’s 10th in its past 14 games, dropping the Astros to 77-79.
“We have six chances to go out there and make the playoffs,” said Alvarez, who is chasing an American League MVP and Triple Crown entering the regular season’s final week.
“Listen, we’ve got to use tomorrow to really gather our thoughts and get a good plan together for the next week,” manager Joe Espada said. “No doubt about it that we need to bounce back and really dig deep and fight, because this series was not what we were expecting.”
Sunday’s script was reminiscent of Saturday’s 6-3 loss, when Braves slugger Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a go-ahead three-run homer in the seventh. The Astros’ led, 1-0, through five innings on Sunday before Bryan King allowed all four batters he faced to reach, capped by MIke Yastrzemski’s three-run homer in the sixth that made it 4-1.
The Astros went 0-for-3 with the bases loaded and did little to back starting pitcher Hunter Brown, who struck out 10 batters in five scoreless innings. Brown also walked three batters and was pulled after throwing 98 pitches, but Houston’s battered bullpen couldn’t hold the lead for the second game in a row.
“We can still make a big push here,” Brown said. “We’re right in it. We’re not dead yet. That’s what we’re going to do, give it our all these last six games and find out where we are after that.”
Alvarez refused to divulge what was said in his speech or who else spoke up, but outfielder Taylor Trammell said his message carried weight.
“He doesn’t talk much and when he speaks, there’s a presence,” Trammell said. “This was not a ‘hoorah’ or anything like that. It’s just like, ‘Hey guys, Easy. Just be easy with it,’ and hearing it from him, it means something. You see the way he’s played all year and you can’t tell me there hasn’t been any nicks or bangs for him. And he’s going out there every single day and being the best hitter in the game right now. That’s what he’s doing. And so when he says something and he talks, you listen.”
Veteran first baseman Christian Walker said Alvarez’s speech stressed a sense of urgency facing the Astros, who were knocked out of first place on Saturday for the first time since late July. Houston missed the postseason by one game last year, ending its run of eight consecutive playoff appearances.
Alvarez challenged his teammates to get back to October.
“Everybody is going to receive things differently, but younger guys who haven’t been to the postseason, it feels like there’s a lot of pressure right now, and there is,” Walker said. “And that’s a good thing, because we played ourselves into a spot to be competitive. I think any time a vet can address the team, especially somebody like Yordan, if nothing else, for everybody to feel the calmness he brings to the table. That can be helpful.”
The Mariners (73-83), whose slim playoff hopes are still alive, would love nothing more to spoil it for the Astros, who are 2-9 against Seattle. Houston ends the season playing in a Minor League ballpark in West Sacramento that can be about as unpredictable as it gets and wants to leave nothing to chance.
“These next two teams have nothing to lose,” Walker said. “Their goal is to knock us out. I’ve been on teams where we’ve been in that position before and it can be a dangerous spot. I think it’s a good reminder to come into these cities with a fire and a sense of urgency, and prepare to come in and win some baseball games.”

item.content:encoded:
Cristopher Sánchez consigue su 18ma victoria, líder de MLB; Juan Soto se va de 4-1
El dominicano Cristopher Sánchez consiguió su 18.ª victoria, la mayor cantidad en las Grandes Ligas, para guiar la victoria el domingo 7-2 de los Filis de Filadelfia ante los Mets de Nueva York.
Los Filis (86-70), que rescataron un empate en la serie de cuatro juegos, llegaron al domingo en el tercer puesto de comodín de la Liga Nacional, a un juego de los Cachorros de Chicago y Padres de San Diego y con una ventaja de cuatro juegos sobre los Diamondbacks de Arizona.
Sánchez permitió seis hits —incluido el jonrón de Bo Bichette en la sexta entrada— y ponchó a seis en 6 1/3 innings, con lo que rompió el empate con Sonny Gray, de los Medias Rojas de Boston, por el liderato de victorias en las Grandes Ligas.
El último lanzador de los Filis en liderar las mayores en victorias fue Steve Carlton, con 23 en 1982.
Justin Crawford conectó un triple de tres carreras y el venezolano Luis Arráez terminó con dos carreras impulsadas. Alec Bohm y Trea Turner aportaron cada uno un hit productor. Kyle Schwarber igualó su máximo de carrera con cuatro bases por bolas.
El novato Jonah Tong (2-2) permitió cuatro carreras y ponchó a cinco en 4 2/3 innings por los coleros Mets, que terminaron 36-45 en casa —su peor registro en Citi Field desde 2013, que fue de 33-48.
Los Mets atrajeron a 2.712.120 aficionados esta temporada, una caída de 5.870 aficionados por juego respecto a la temporada pasada —el descenso más pronunciado en las Grandes Ligas.
El dominicano Juan Soto bateó de 4-1.

item.title: [roundtable.io] Yankees' Paul Goldschmidt Has Gone From Disposable to Indispensable
item.dc:creator: Matthew Schmidt
item.description: New York Yankees first baseman Paul Goldschmidt has flipped the script. The addition of Luis Garcia Jr. had completely clouded Goldschmidt's role, and it appeared that the impending returns of Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton would make the former NL MVP rather disposable. item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees first baseman Paul Goldschmidt has flipped the script.
The addition of Luis Garcia Jr. had completely clouded Goldschmidt's role, and it appeared that the impending returns of Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton would make the former NL MVP rather disposable.
My, how things have changed.
Yes, Goldschmidt's at-bats have still been somewhat sparse since the arrival of Garcia at the MLB trade deadline, but with Judge and Stanton now both potentially out for the playoffs (or at least the Wild Card Series), Goldschmidt's value just increased exponentially.
Suddenly, Goldschmidt is now one of the Yankees' very best options against left-handed pitching, and he may get some starts in the playoffs now that Judge and Stanton are both on the shelf.
Goldschmidt has always mashed southpaws, owning a lifetime 1.006 OPS against them. This year, he is slashing .309/.404/.592 versus lefties, making him a must on New York's playoff squad.
It should also be noted that after a miserable month of July and after barely playing in August, Goldschmidt has gone 6-for-18 at the plate this month, so he is starting to rediscover his stroke as October draws near.
And with the Boston Red Sox — New York's likely Wild Card opponent — being loaded with left-handers, Goldschmidt will likely get significant playing time early on in the postseason.
In that scenario, Ben Rice would serve as the DH — a role that almost certainly would have gone to Stanton had he been available — and Goldschmidt will play over at first base. Garcia would then come off the bench as a pinch hitter against righties.
Goldschmidt's overall numbers this season look solid, as he is slashing .253/.316/.455 with 18 home runs and 50 RBI across 370 trips to the dish. Not bad for a 39-year-old.
Goldschmidt's production has nose dived since then, but he appears to be kicking it back into gear just in time for the playoffs.
And now that Judge and Stanton are both on the shelf, you can expect Goldschmidt to play a pivotal role.

item.title: [sentinelandenterprise.com] Mike Yastrzemski’s home run for Braves sends Red Sox to postseason
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Starr
item.description: The Red Sox were unable to punch their own ticket to the postseason Sunday, as they fell to the Tampa Bay Rays, 5-1, at Tropicana Field. Fortunately, one of their former pitchers, the grandson of one of the greatest players to ever don a Red Sox uniform and Boston’s original major league team did it for them. item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox were unable to punch their own ticket to the postseason Sunday, as they fell to the Tampa Bay Rays, 5-1, at Tropicana Field.
Fortunately, one of their former pitchers, the grandson of one of the greatest players to ever don a Red Sox uniform and Boston’s original major league team did it for them.
With a 4-2 defeat of the Houston Astros late Sunday afternoon, the Atlanta Braves propelled the Red Sox to October.
Left-hander Martin Pérez, who pitched for the 2020-21 Red Sox, started for the Braves and held the Astros to one run, a solo homer by Jose Altuve, over 4 1/3 innings.
But the biggest Boston-connected contribution came from Mike Yastrzemski, grandson of Red Sox icon Carl Yastrzemski and a former Red Sox late-round draft pick out of St. John’s Prep in Danvers, Ma. The younger Yaz’s three-run homer in the sixth gave the Braves an enduring lead, and the Red Sox an in.
His momentous home run also coincided with the 59th anniversary of his grandfather hitting his 41st home run and scoring the go-ahead run to keep the 1967 “Impossible Dream” Red Sox in a first-place tie with the Minnesota Twins in a tight American League pennant race.
The final piece of this New England-centric puzzle was a game-ending strikeout of Astros shortstop Jeremy Pena. The Braves originally drafted him in the 39th round of the 2015 MLB Draft out of Providence’s Classic High School, before the Astros took him in the third round in 2018, out of the University of Maine.
The Red Sox watched the Braves from the visitors’ clubhouse at Tropicana Field, then donned “Clinched” t-shirts and goggles, and went back out to the field to celebrate and give the attendants time to seal the clubhouse in plastic wrap and wheel in the champagne and beer.
Long before the Red Sox played their inaugural season as one of the American League’s eight charter clubs in 1901, Boston had the Braves. The Braves were originally the Red Stockings, their name from their 1871 inception until 1876, when they were renamed the Red Caps until 1882.
The 1914 Boston Braves were the first team in MLB history to reach the postseason after being 14 games under .500 at some point in the season. It was a feat only matched by the 1974 Pittsburgh Pirates and 2005 Astros.
Until Sunday, when the Braves helped the Red Sox become the fourth team to do so.

item.title: [heavy.com] Why Brewers Pulled Jacob Misiorowski After Pitching 3 Innings
item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen
item.description: Jacob Misiorowski must’ve wanted to watch the Sunday Night Football matchup between the Kansas City Chiefs and Indianapolis Colts. Because after pitching three innings on Sunday Night Baseball for the Milwaukee Brewers, he was pulled from the game. For those not paying more attention, it certainly could cause alarm. The Brewers are just a week away from the end of the regular season. They’re trying to wrap up the top record in the National League. And now Misiorowski is out? Well, don’t be alarm
item.content:encoded:
Jacob Misiorowski must’ve wanted to watch the Sunday Night Football matchup between the Kansas City Chiefs and Indianapolis Colts.
Because after pitching three innings on Sunday Night Baseball for the Milwaukee Brewers, he was pulled from the game.
For those not paying more attention, it certainly could cause alarm.
The Brewers are just a week away from the end of the regular season. They’re trying to wrap up the top record in the National League. And now Misiorowski is out?
Well, don’t be alarmed.
Why Did Brewers Pull Jacob Misiorowski?
The Brewers were always planning on doing this.
They wanted to give Misiorowksi one easy start at this point in the season. He’ll have one more regular season outing after this one, and they’ll ramp him back up there.
Pulling him early on Sunday gives him a bit of rest relative to a full outing.
This is how the Brewers’ beat writer for MLB.com explained it on X:
It’s Antonio Senzatela taking over for the Brewers in the fourth inning.
Misiorowski: Three innings, one hit, no walks, four strikeouts on 44 pitches. The plan was to back him off for this one, then stretch him back out for his next one as a final tune-up for the postseason.
— Adam McCalvy (@AdamMcCalvy) September 21, 2026
Misiorowski was shown on the national broadcast on Peacock smiling with his teammates in the dugout. He clearly wasn’t bothered by the early hook, particularly when he knew it was the plan all along.
Jacob Misiorowski Stats
For what it’s worth, ‘The Miz’ was dominant in his short outing.
He went 3.0 innings and faced just 10 batters. The Orioles had one hit off of him.
Misiorowski didn’t give up a run, and he struck out four hitters without walking any.
He threw 44 pitches, 29 of them for strikes.
The Brewers turned to Antonio Senzatela early out of the bullpen to start the parade of arms that would get to the end of Sunday night.
Based on general pitching schedules, Misiorowski should get his final outing of the regular season at home.
Milwaukee first goes to Philadelphia for a three-game series against the Phillies from Tuesday to Thursday.
After that, they return home and host the St. Louis Cardinals for three games to conclude the regular season.
The Brewers are closing in on a first-round bye, which would mean Misiorowski would get another block of rest after his final regular season outing. Teams have just started to figure out how to handle that since it’s been introduced in the recent past.
For Milwaukee, they’ll get to line up Misiorowski for their playoff opener, whenever that is. And because he was pulled early in this one, he’ll be just a little fresher.

item.content:encoded:
Este domingo, las Grandes Ligas vivió uno de los momentos más dramáticos en los últimos tiempos. Durante el juego entre los Chicago Cubs y Cincinnati Reds, Alex Bregman tuvo un iniesperado accidente mientras estaba esperando su tirno al bat.
El famoso pelotero estadounidense se encontraba en la zona de calentamiento para batear, cuando Michael Busch estaba en el plato e intentó batear una bola, misma que salió a la zona de foul donde se encontraba Bregman y lo agarró desprevenido. El jugador de Cubs recibió un fuerte impacto en el rostro.
RECOMENDAMOS: ¡Casi lo parten! Aaron Rodgers sufre BRUTAL golpe en derrota de Steelers ante Patriots en la NFL
¿Qué le pasó a Alex Bregman?
Después del penoso accidente que sufrió Alex Bregman, se dio a conocer que el jugador de los Cachorros fue trasladado al hospital, pero no hay muchos detalles de cuál es su estado de salud.
El propio manager de los Cubs, Craig Counsell, aseguró que sabe lo mínimo. El entrenador dejó claro que solo sabía de las heridas que tenía en el rostro, incluso llegó a pensar que le habían roto la nariz.
“Tenía una cortada debajo del ojo. Le sangraba un poco la nariz. Está bastante hinchado. Fue debajo del ojo. Sinceramente, pensé que le había pegado en la nariz. Pensé que se había fracturado la nariz, pero sabía que la pelota le había dado en alguna parte del rostro”.
Por su parte, Alex Bregman mostró en sus redes sociales cómo le quedó el rostro después del tremendo pelotazo que le dieron este domingo.
PUEDE INTERESAR: Isaac del Toro finalizó sexto en prueba contrarreloj del Mundial de Ciclismo 2026
¿Quién es Alex Bregman?
Alexander David Bregman, conocido en las Grandes Ligas como Alex Bregman, se ha consolidado como una de las figuras más completas de la tercera base en la última década de las Major League Baseball (MLB).
El beisbolista se ha caracterizado por su paciencia en el plato, excelente disciplina de bateo y una defensa impecable en la esquina caliente, el infielder estadounidense ha sido una pieza fundamental en la época dorada de los Houston Astros antes de continuar su trayectoria profesional.
Los equipos de Alex Bregman:
- Houston Astros (2016–2024)
- Boston Red Sox (2025)
- Chicago Cubs (2026–presente)

item.content:encoded:
What, no italics? That's right, I'm abandoning the usual boilerplate intro for this final edition of the two-start pitcher rankings to issue a grave warning ...
Don't count on any of these guys actually making two starts.
They appear to be in line to -- and some indeed will -- but the second start would come on the final day of the season. With no tomorrow, a team can throw caution to the wind and pretty much use whomever it wants. I'm not saying it'll start someone on short rest, but a bullpen game or a spot starter? Why not?
And actually, I think the pitchers most in danger of losing their second start are the ones on the teams with a tomorrow -- i.e., the ones resetting their rotation for the playoffs. If they've already secured their spot prior to the final day of the season and one of their top hurlers is scheduled to go, they'll almost assuredly opt for someone else.
To reiterate, you should be skeptical of any pitcher listed here actually making two starts, but especially Zack Wheeler, Max Fried and Kevin Gausman. Maybe Cristian Javier, Nick Martinez and Robbie Ray as well. You're probably going to ask about Payton Tolle because you're likely to see two baseball indicators next to his name on your lineup page, signaling two starts, but I'm so confident he won't actually make that second start that I've left him out of these rankings altogether. Of course, you'll probably still want to use him with one start because he's that good.
That should the litmus test. If you wouldn't be comfortable getting just one start from any of these pitchers, you're better off not using him at all. For now, though, here's how the two-start pitcher slate stacks up for Fantasy Week 27 (Sept. 21-27). All information is up to date as of Sunday evening.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers placed pitcher Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list on Sunday, which means he could miss his final regular-season turn in the rotation next week.
Skubal's next start is scheduled for Friday against the San Francisco Giants, which could fall within the three-to-seven days that players are allowed to be away from the team while on the bereavement list. But Dodgers manager Dave Roberts appeared to believe that Skubal will be back by Friday, telling reporters he would miss "a couple days."
"Some personal stuff going on, but he's fine," Roberts said, via MLB.com's Sonja Chen.
Skubal pitched in Saturday's 10-4 win over the Giants, allowing four runs and eight hits over five innings. He walked two batters with three strikeouts, tying his lowest total of the season. Saturday's game was the first time Skubal gave up more than three runs in his nine starts with the Dodgers. according to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.
Tarik Skubal pitched five innings and allowed four runs but is grateful for the offensive support.
“Yeah, no doubt. Obviously, I wasn't very good today, but the offense and defense and bullpen picked me up big time, and that's what good teams do,” Skubal said. “You know, they… pic.twitter.com/4TUdrQqgH8
"Obviously, I wasn't very good today, but the offense and defense and bullpen picked me up big time, and that's what good teams do," Skubal said after the game.
In his nine starts with the Dodgers since being acquired from the Detroit Tigers before the MLB trade deadline, Skubal has a 2.95 ERA and 4-2 record with 60 strikeouts in 55 innings.
The Dodgers took a 2-0 lead on a first-inning RBI double by Max Muncy and Mookie Betts hitting a run-scoring single in the second. But San Francisco tied the score in the third on a 2-run homer from Victor Bericoto, hitting a fastball left in the very middle of the strike zone by Skubal.
The two teams then traded runs during the third through fifth innings, resulting in a 4-4 tie, before the Dodgers pulled away on a 2-run hit by Tommy Edman and RBI single from Miguel Rojas. In the following inning, the Dodgers added three more runs with Will Smith driving in a run and Josue De Paula hitting a 2-run single.
To fill Skubal's spot on the active roster, Emmet Sheehan was recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City. He pitched 5 1/3 scoreless innings with one hit allowed and nine strikeouts, taking over for opener Jack Dreyer in the Dodgers' 3-1 win. In his previous two starts before being optioned, Sheehan allowed one run over 11 2/3 innings with 15 strikeouts.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — The Yankees' chances of winning the AL East title were reduced to nearly zero on Sunday . . . not that they were all that good to begin with.
The Tampa Bay Rays entered Sunday with a magic number of four to eliminate the Yankees from contention for first place. That became three when the Rays beat the Red Sox, and it dropped to two when the Yankees lost to the Arizona Diamondbacks, 8-4.
The Rays (95-60) lead the Yankees (89-66) by six games with seven to play. The two teams will play four games in the Bronx this week, including a split doubleheader on Tuesday. If the Rays win that first game — or any game in the series — the race is over. The Yankees must win all four games to stay alive, and a sweep also would give them the tiebreaker in the season series, 7-6.
The Yankees are scheduled to start lefthanders Carlos Rodon (6-3, 2.95 ERA) and Max Fried (5-4, 2.63) on Tuesday against the Rays, who will counter with righthanders Nick Martinez (15-4, 2.94) and Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72). Gerrit Cole and Cam Schlittler are slated to pitch Wednesday and Thursday for the Yankees.
The Yankees did reduce their magic number to clinch the first wild card — and home-field advantage in the Wild Card Round — to one over the Red Sox, whom they seem likely to play in that round for the second straight season.
The Yankees managed only three hits in the final 6 1/3 innings after hitting three no-doubt home runs off Corbin Burnes in the third inning — 388 feet to left by Heliot Ramos (107.6-mph exit velocity), 424 to left by George Lombard Jr. (108.7) and 448 to center by Spencer Jones (109.8) — for a 4-1 lead, but Arizona's Nolan Arenado capped a five-run fifth with a two-out grand slam off Brent Headrick.
Yankees starter Will Warren retired Tim Tawa to begin the fifth, but Lars Nootbaar doubled, Ketel Marte singled and Gabriel Moreno walked to load the bases. Headrick replaced Warren and struck out Geraldo Perdomo for the second out, but he walked Corbin Carroll to force in a run. One pitch after Arenado's bid for a grand slam went just foul, he gave the Diamondbacks a 6-4 lead with a blast to leftfield.
Perdomo had a run-scoring single in the first and an RBI triple in the seventh as Arizona recorded its MLB-best 47th comeback victory of the season.

item.dc:creator: Michael McDermott
item.description: The Atlanta Braves will celebrate their third National League East division title with Matt Olson as their first baseman.
