Obviously, we got out to such a good start. It’s a great group here; we can do some special things.” The 2025 season served as a harsh reminder for Olson and the Brave
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves will celebrate their third National League East division title with Matt Olson as their first baseman. The Braves All-Star spoke to Wiley Ballard of BravesVision about their season during the celebration.
“Last year left a sour taste in our mouth,” said Olson. “I felt the focus from first day of Spring Training. Obviously, we got out to such a good start. It’s a great group here; we can do some special things.”
The 2025 season served as a harsh reminder for Olson and the Braves. They endured a frustrating season, but that served as motivation behind their strong 2026 season. They’ll celebrate a division title with a week left in the regular season.
“Happy to be in this moment. It’s always the best when you’re celebrating such a long season and coming together to win a division.”
In 2026, Olson has enjoyed his typical strong year. He’s slashing .253/.324/.506 with 40 home runs and a 123 wRC+. He’s on track to post his fourth season of at least 4.0 fWAR since 2021.
Olson was named a National League All-Star in 2026. It marked the fourth All-Star selection of his great career.
Matt Olson on Walt Weiss’ Impact as Braves Manager
The topic shifted to the impact that new manager Walt Weiss had on the club. Weiss was hired as the manager after World Series-winning manager Brian Snitker stepped down from the job.
Matt Olson spoke about the impact that the new manager has brought to the team.
“He was probably our No. 1 person,” said Olson. “Between Walt and a lot of the new staff that we brought in, it’s been hyperfocus from the beginning.
“To have the focus, Walt talking about it, having that aggression in spring, I felt it all year.
“Obviously, you’re going to have some moments throughout the course of the season. It feels like we had a couple bad series, we go to a big series and we rise up to the occasion. Just proud of these guys.”
Weiss will be on a short list of favorites to win the National League’s Manager of the Year for the 2026 season. The other top candidate should be Milwaukee Brewers skipper Pat Murphy, who has won the last two awards.
What’s Next for the Braves?
The Braves will have an off day before they return to Truist Park. They’ll host the Cincinnati Reds for three games, then travel to Miami to finish out their season.
Atlanta will still push for a Wild Card round bye, but they are also four games back of the Los Angeles Dodgers. Most likely, they will play in the Wild Card Series against the Wild Card team with the worst record. Currently, that team is the Philadelphia Phillies.
In that scenario, it would be the fifth series between the two National League East clubs. The Braves won the regular-season series, nine games to four.

item.content:encoded:
Yordan Alvarez Gives Bold Quote, Calls Team Meeting as Astros Fall in MLB Playoff Standings
Yordan Alvarez was not pleased after the Houston Astros were swept by the Atlanta Braves over the weekend, leaving them a game behind the Texas Rangers in the AL West with just six games remaining.
The superstar slugger told reporters he called a team meeting following Sunday's 4-2 loss:
Alvarez, 29, has more than done his part this season, hitting .313 with 40 homers, 99 RBI, 98 runs and a 1.027 OPS. He's likely going to be the AL MVP, though it likely won't mean nearly as much if the Astros—who have lost 10 of their last 14 games—fail to reach the postseason.
They will have two games remaining against the Seattle Mariners and four against the Athletics to salvage the season. The Rangers will finish with three games against the New York Mets and three games against the Minnesota Twins.

item.content:encoded:
AI 핵심 요약
beta
- 이정후는 21일 다저스전서 1안타 1볼넷을 기록했다
- 이정후는 3경기 연속 안타로 타격감을 끌어올렸다
- 김하성은 침묵했고 애틀랜타는 지구 1위를 확정했다
!AI가 자동 생성한 요약으로 정확하지 않을 수 있어요.
[서울=뉴스핌] 박상욱 기자 = 이정후(샌프란시스코 자이언츠)가 LA 다저스를 상대로 3경기 연속 안타 행진을 이어갔다. 이정후는 21일(한국시간) 미국 캘리포니아주 로스앤젤레스의 다저스타디움에서 열린 다저스와의 방문 경기에 2번 타자 우익수로 선발 출전해 2타수 1안타 1볼넷을 기록했다.
이번 다저스 원정 3연전에서 이정후는 매경기 안타를 터뜨리며 타격감을 끌어올렸다. 지난 19일 경기에서 홈런과 타점을 올렸고, 전날 경기에서는 2루타를 포함한 멀티히트를 작성했다. 이날 역시 첫 타석에서 유격수 뜬공으로 물러났으나, 3회초 두 번째 타석에서 볼넷을 골라 출루했다.
안타는 팀이 1-0으로 앞선 6회초 세 번째 타석에서 나왔다. 다저스 투수 에밋 시한과 풀카운트 접전 끝에 시속 92.9마일 포심 패스트볼을 받아쳐 우익수 앞 안타로 연결했다. 후속 타자 불발로 득점으로 이어지지는 않았다. 이정후는 7회말 수비를 앞두고 드류 길버트와 교체되며 경기를 마쳤다. 이정후의 시즌 타율은 0.276이 됐고, 샌프란시스코는 1-3으로 역전패했다.
올 시즌 이정후는 월별 타격 성적에서 부침이 심했다. 지난 6월 한 달간 타율 0.340을 치며 내셔널리그 타격왕 경쟁을 벌였고 시즌 타율을 0.319까지 끌어올렸다. 샌프란시스코 구단 역사상 규정 타석을 채우고 3할 타율을 기록한 좌타자는 2004년 배리 본즈가 마지막이었기에 기대감이 컸다.
하지만 7월 타율이 0.244로 주춤하더니 8월에도 0.245에 머물렀다. 9월 들어서는 타율이 1할대까지 떨어지며 3할 타율 무산의 아픔을 겪었다. 비록 시즌 막판 부침을 겪었으나 이번 다저스 원정 3연전에서 10타수 4안타 1볼넷을 기록하며 반등의 발판을 마련했다.
애틀랜타 브레이브스의 김하성은 휴스턴 애스트로스와의 원정 경기에 9번 타자 유격수로 출전해 삼진 2개, 땅볼, 뜬공으로 침묵하며 5경기 연속 안타를 생산하지 못했다. 이날 휴스턴을 4-2로 제압한 애틀랜타는 3년 만에 내셔널리그 동부지구 1위를 확정했다. 내셔널리그에서는 애틀랜타, 밀워키 브루어스(중부지구), LA 다저스(서부지구)가 지구 우승을 확정 지었다. 아메리칸리그에서는 보스턴 레드삭스가 와일드카드로 포스트시즌 진출을 결정했다.
psoq1337@newspim.com

item.dc:creator: Jesse Borek

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX -- The sound off the bat got an eruption of sound from the Chase Field crowd. But as the ball off the bat of Nolan Arenado traveled toward the left-foul pole, it began to hook. It ultimately slid foul, almost a go-ahead grand slam in the bottom of the fifth that would have kept the D-backs’ postseason chances alive.
One pitch later, Arenado hammered the next one fair into the left-field seats. Pendulum, swung.
It marked Arenado’s ninth career grand slam and third this year, tying Paul Goldschmidt (2013) and Eugenio Suárez (2025) for the most in a single season in franchise history. It was the turning point in the club’s 8-4 victory over the Yankees on Sunday during the 2026 regular-season home finale, marking their 47th comeback win of the year, the most in the Majors.
But with the Cubs (87-69), Padres (87-69) and Phillies (86-70) all winning on Sunday as well, the D-backs remain four games out of the third and final National League Wild Card spot with just six games to play. To paraphrase Yankees Hall of Famer Yogi Berra and one of his “Yogi-isms”:
“It’s getting late early.”
While the D-backs will conclude the regular season with a three-game series against San Diego next week, they trail the Padres by five games. That means Arizona will need to make up two games in the standings by the time it arrives at Petco Park next Friday to give themselves a chance at October baseball.
Regardless of what the next week holds for the 2026 D-backs as they embark on the road, what can’t be denied is that by virtue of their 45-37 record at Chase Field, they turned in the most successful season at home since 2017 (53-29).

item.content:encoded:
Card collectors gather for trading card show at Independence Mall
WILMINGTON, NC (WWAY) — Trading card fanatics packed Independence Mall during the weekend to buy, trade, and sell trading cards.
Dozens of card collectors turned out over the weekend for a “TCG and Sports Card Show” at Independence Mall, where attendees could buy, trade and sell a wide variety of cards.
Some collectors arrived with briefcases, hoping to find the perfect addition to their collections. Cards ranged from Pokémon and baseball to hockey.
Friends Mitchell Smith and Britt Wilson shared some of their favorite cards.
“I’m a Duke fan, as you can tell. I like Cooper Flagg, so I have a Cooper Flagg autograph right now,” Smith said. “My favorite card in my collection is probably a Paul Skenes autograph,” said Wilson
Carolina Sports Promotions, which hosted the event, will return for the next card show at American Legion Post 10.

item.content:encoded:
Mariners update status of Andrés Muñoz after closer exits with injury
The Seattle Mariners have a new injury concern with two-time All-Star closer Andrés Muñoz after Sunday's 2-1 win over the Colorado Rockies.
(Dustin Bradford/Getty Images)
The Seattle Mariners have a new injury concern with two-time All-Star closer Andrés Muñoz after Sunday’s 2-1 win over the Colorado Rockies.
Muñoz exited the game after facing three batters, as the hard-throwing right-hander seemed to be favoring his left knee as he finished throwing the final pitch of a one-out walk to Colorado first baseman TJ Rumfield in the bottom of the ninth inning.
A trainer and manager Dan Wilson came out of the dugout to check on Muñoz, and after a short discussion opted to call for Eduard Bazardo out of the bullpen. Bazardo struck two batters out around a two-out walk to record his first career save.
After the game, Wilson told reporters that Muñoz “felt something in his knee” and that the Mariners will know more after imaging is done Monday.
“I think it’s been an issue here and there, but something that just popped up big time today,” Wilson said of the knee concern with Muñoz.
Muñoz, who allowed a home run to Rockies All-Star Hunter Goodman that accounted for Colorado’s sole run Sunday, has had an uneven 2026 season. He owns a 4.24 ERA, 1.22 WHIP and .216 opponent batting average in 61 appearances (57 1/3 innings), and has converted 28 of 38 save opportunities.
The Mariners are off Monday, then begin their final homestand with the opener of a two-game set against the Houston Astros at 6:40 p.m. Tuesday at T-Mobile Park. Houston (77-79) is a game behind the Texas Rangers (78-78) for first place in the AL West. The M’s are on the brink of elimination from playoff contention at five game back of Texas.

item.content:encoded:
The final road game of the 2026 regular season is upon us, as the Yankees will conclude it with a seven-game homestand before likely hosting the Red Sox for the Wild Card Series. If the season ends there, this is the end of the line for the gray uniforms for 2026, but obviously, we all hope we’ll see them next in Tampa (and more) in early October.
Looking to end a road slate that has been very generous to the Yankees on a high note is Will Warren, who’s finishing his sophomore season strong after his great start to the campaign unraveled into a bit of a mess over the summer. Rotation reinforcements that threatened to throw him in the bullpen never came with the recurring injuries, so he’ll finish 2026 with 30 starts for the second straight season. This is No. 29, as he enters with a 3.89 ERA (108 ERA+) and 4.07 FIP in 148 innings. No matter what happens from here, Warren has had a successful year in solidifying himself as a true MLB-caliber rotation arm.
Opposing him will be a former Cy Young winner trying to round into form off Tommy John surgery in Corbin Burnes, whom Yankees fans remember well from his lone season in Baltimore in 2024. Returning from a 16-month absence on September 8 to help with the playoff push, Burnes has allowed five runs across 7.2 innings with six strikeouts to two walks against the Royals and Marlins. He isn’t totally built up, having thrown 75 pitches in his last start, so expect him to settle around 80-85 today. He’s always befuddled the Yankees, pitching to a 1.93 ERA across 23.1 innings in his career, but he doesn’t have a win in any of those four starts.
Ben Rice will once again lead off, followed by Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, and Luis García Jr. We’ve seen better ABs and swings from George Lombard Jr. lately, who’ll bat fifth. Spencer Jones is back after a one-day absence due to a sore foot and will bat in front of Anthony Volpe, Austin Wells, and José Caballero.
Lars Nootbaar will also be a repeat leadoff hitter for the D-backs, followed by Ketel Marte, Gabriel Moreno, and Geraldo Perdomo. Corbin Carroll is batting fifth, Nolan Arenado will bat sixth, and former Blue Jay Jesús Sánchez bats seventh ahead of last night’s hero Pavin Smith and Tim Tawa.
How to watch
Location: Chase Field, Phoenix, AZ
First pitch: 4:10 pm E.T.
TV broadcast: YES, DBACKS.TV
Radio broadcast: WFAN 660/101.9 FM, WADO 1280 (NYY), ESPN 620 AM, La Campesina 101.9 FM & 860 AM (AZ)
Online stream: MLB.tv (out-of-market only), Gotham Sports App

item.dc:creator: Kristie Ackert; USA TODAY
item.description: Alex Bregman walked off the field Sunday, Sept. 20 with a towel pressed to his face and blood running down his cheek. item.content:encoded:
Alex Bregman walked off the field Sunday, Sept. 20 with a towel pressed to his face and blood running down his cheek. The Chicago Cubs third baseman was hit in the face by a foul ball as he waited in the on-deck circle in the top of the fourth inning against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball park.
Bregman was taken to a local hospital for further testing after the scare in Cincinnati. After the 9-1 win, Cubs manager Craig Counsell told reporters the ball hit Bregman in the cheekbone, which is swollen, and left a cut on his face. Bregman was evaluated for broken bones.
It happed with two outs and the Cubs leading 5-0. Michael Busch checked his swing on a 1-2 pitch from Reds right-hander Luis Mey, and the ball ricocheted toward Bregman. He dropped to the ground immediately, clutching his face, then got up and walked to the clubhouse under his own power. There was no official diagnosis.
Alex Bregman was hit in the face by a foul ball off the bat of Michael Busch while on deck in the 4th inning. Matt Shaw came in to PH.
We wish Alex a speedy recovery 🙏 pic.twitter.com/4uqCRQvHwE
Bregman heating up
Before the injury, Bregman had done damage to the Reds. He drove in a run with a first-inning single, then walked and scored in the Cubs' four-run third inning.
The 32-year-old is hitting .260 with 26 home runs, 88 RBIs and an .801 OPS this season. He signed a five-year, $175 million contract with Chicago last winter. The three-time All-Star won two World Series with the Astros.
What's next for Bregman and the Cubs
The timing is the problem for Bregman and the Cubs. Chicago is on the verge of clinching a playoff berth, needing just one win or an Arizona Diamondbacks loss to lock in wild card spot. If Bregman needs time away, the Cubs have Matt Shaw and Pedro Ramirez to fill in at third base. Neither has Bregman's experience in a playoff race.
Any fracture would change the outlook considerably. Facial fractures around the cheek bone or eye socket can sideline a player for weeks, and a hitter usually has to be cleared before he can face live pitching again.
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Cubs' Alex Bregman hospitalized after getting hit in face with foul ball

item.content:encoded:
Brown took a no-decision Sunday against Atlanta, striking out while allowing three hits and two walks in five scoreless innings.
Brown had Atlanta out of sorts, generating 18 whiffs en route to fanning double-digit hitters for a second consecutive start. The right-hander has now worked at least five innings while conceding fewer than three runs in six of his last nine outings since the beginning of August. He's set to wrap up his regular season against the division-rival Athletics in hitter-friendly Sacramento, where he'll bring a steady 3.26 ERA, 1.27 WHIP and 120:51 K:BB over 102 innings.

item.title: [MLB.com] Bregman awaiting test results after being hit in face by foul ball while in on-deck circle
item.dc:creator: Bill Ladson
item.description: CINCINNATI -- Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman had to leave Sunday’s 9-1 victory against the Reds at Great American Ball Park after getting hit in the left cheek bone by a foul ball from teammate Michael Busch. With two outs in the fourth inning, Busch was at the plate when he half-swung at a pitch thrown by Reds right-hander Luis Mey. item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman had to leave Sunday’s 9-1 victory against the Reds at Great American Ball Park after getting hit in the left cheek bone by a foul ball from teammate Michael Busch.
With two outs in the fourth inning, Busch was at the plate when he half-swung at a pitch thrown by Reds right-hander Luis Mey. Busch fouled off the pitch and the ball hit Bregman while he was in the on-deck circle. Bregman immediately went into the dugout, and he was replaced by pinch-hitter Matt Shaw.
Bregman was sent to the hospital for X-rays and a CT scan, but there wasn't any initial word after the game regarding what kind of damage was done.
“I don’t know anything more than that,” Cubs manager Craig Counsell said. “He had a cut under his eye. He was bleeding from his nose a little bit. It’s pretty swollen. It was below the eye. I honestly thought it hit him in the nose. I thought he had a broken nose, but I knew it hit him somewhere in the face. It’s just an unfortunate accident. I’m hoping and praying he is all right.
“We have to get good results from the hospital first. [Bregman] got hit in the face, so you are worried about his general well-being first. If we get a good report, we’ll move to the next step. I want to get a good report.”
Shaw drew a walk, then remained in the game to play second base, with Pedro Ramírez shifting to third base.
The Cubs, who were winning 5-0 at the time of Bregman's exit, can clinch a postseason berth if the D-backs lose to the Yankees on Sunday afternoon.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Corbin Burnes Blown off Mound in Disastrous 3rd Inning vs Yankees
item.dc:creator: Jack Sommers; Unknown
item.description: The Arizona Diamondbacks are fighting for their playoff lives and were counting on Corbin Burnes to come back and help them in September. item.content:encoded:
The Arizona Diamondbacks are fighting for their playoff lives and were counting on Corbin Burnes to come back and help them in September.
Unfortunately he's been anything but a help to the team's push to make the Postseason.
Corbin Burnes Gets Hammered by Yankees
Burnes wiggled out of a first-inning jam when he allowed a walk and a single to start the game. But he retired the next three batters and pitched a scoreless second inning as well.
Burnes appeared to be cruising when he got two quick outs in the third too, but then disaster struck. Heliot Ramos launched a line drive homer 107 MPH off the bat into the left field bleachers to tie the game at 1-1. It came on a middle-middle 92 MPH sinker.
A sharp base hit by Luis Garcia Jr. followed, and Torey Lovullo got the pen up, as Ryne Nelson began throwing. But George Lombard hit a 91 MPH cutter, also in the middle of the plate, 20 rows up, 424 feet out to left for a two-run blast.
That would not be the end of Burnes' torture. The very next batter, Spencer Jones, went down and got a curveball at the bottom of the zone, crushing it 448 feet onto the concourse in left center field.
That was all for Burnes, who was pulled from the game with a pitching line of 2.2 innings, five runs on four hits, including the three homers. He left the game trailing 4-1, handing it off to Nelson. Nolan Arenado hit a grand slam in the fifth inning to put the D-backs ahead 6-4 and get Burnes off the won-loss hook.
Rough Road to Recovery
It's been a rough road to recovery for Burnes, who suffered an elbow injury on June 1 of last year. He was attempting to return from Tommy John surgery by the All-Star break this year, but a shoulder injury dealt him a setback.
Somewhat controversially, the D-backs ended up rushing Burnes through his rehab process, bringing him back before he was fully stretched out.
He was finally able to make his season debut on September 8, throwing three scoreless innings. His next outing went poorly however, as he went 4.2 innings and allowed five runs on five hits and two homers.
Burnes has now allowed nine runs in 10.1 innings, for a 7.84 ERA, giving up five homers in the process. His velocity on the cutter, already down to a career low 92.7 coming into Sunday's game, bottomed out at 90.9.
The movement profile on his signature pitch is a shadow of it's former self as well. Simply put, the cutter doesn't cut right now. A right-handers cutter, by definition should break glove side.
Fully 34% of his cutters thrown heading into today were actually moving to the arm side, not glove side. In Sunday's outing, 19 of 39, 48% of cutters broke armside. During his peak years that number was about 2-3%, but had crept up to 11-16% in recent years prior to 2026.
D-backs fans were warned by this publication not to set expectations too high for a starter returning mid-season from Tommy John surgery. That's certainly been the case this year.
Perhaps after a full off-season throwing program and spring training, Burnes can regain his form. That's if there is no lockout interrupting Spring Training, of course.
Burnes won the NL Cy Young in 2021 and was one of the most durable pitchers in the game prior to signing with the Diamondbacks during the 2024-25 offseason. He is still owed four years, $140 million on his contract after this season. He has an opt-out that he will certainly not be exercising. The D-backs can only hope that he'll be able to help next year.
Jack Sommers is a credentialed beat writer for Arizona Diamondbacks ON SI. He's also the co-host of the Snakes Territory Podcast and Youtube channel. Formerly a baseball operations department analyst for the D-backs, Jack also covered the team for MLB.com, The Associated Press, and SB Nation. Follow Jack on Twitter @shoewizard59
Follow shoewizard59

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Hunter Brown Has Made the Adjustments, but the Astros Aren’t Turning Them Into Wins
item.dc:creator: Yirsandy Rodriguez; Unknown
item.description: Hunter Brown hit his glove with his right hand to celebrate the excellent catch by second baseman Nick Allen, who took Matt Olson out of the play. The fifth inning had ended and, once again, Brown did his part of the plan with five scoreless innings, 10 strikeouts for the fifth time in his last 10 starts and just three hits allowed. item.content:encoded:
Hunter Brown hit his glove with his right hand to celebrate the excellent catch by second baseman Nick Allen, who took Matt Olson out of the play. The fifth inning had ended and, once again, Brown did his part of the plan with five scoreless innings, 10 strikeouts for the fifth time in his last 10 starts and just three hits allowed.
On the other hand, the Houston Astros could not respond. Brown left the game with a minimal 1-0 lead thanks to a solo home run by José Altuve in the bottom of the fourth inning against Atlanta Braves left-hander Martín Pérez. Once the bullpen came into action, the Braves turned the score around with a four-run rally in the top of the sixth inning.
The story was repeating itself. It is Brown’s 11th consecutive start in which he has reached at least five innings. During that stretch, he is 5-2 with an improvement to a 2.76 ERA compared to his 4.05 ERA in his first eight starts of this year. However, the Astros have wasted four of his dominant starts without being able to take advantage of the impact of their main rotation ace.
Before Sunday’s game, Houston’s last at-home game in this regular season, the team was 9-9 in Brown’s starts. In eight of those losses, they scored four or fewer runs. Brown has continued to throw between 90 and 100 pitches in each of his last seven outings, and he has made significant adjustments at this key moment when Houston is playing for the Division lead against the Texas Rangers as the priority, or, if they lose the top spot, at least a spot in the Wild Card Series.
A look at Brown’s significant adjustments
Sunday’s start was the typical outing in the style of the Hunter Brown, who finished third in the Cy Young Award voting last year: a large number of swings and misses, control of the upper part of the strike zone and that ability to attack hitters. Brown began with a strike to 15 of the 21 opponents he faced and got at least one strikeout with five of the seven types of pitches he threw. Three came with the sinker and four-seam fastball, while generating a 53.8% swing-and-miss rate (seven of 13) with his mix of knuckle curveball, cutter and changeup.
If we compare two key stretches that define Brown’s return to dominance, there are very interesting differences between his first eight starts and these last 10.
Without a doubt, Brown’s most significant change is in the sinker. In his first eight starts, it was largely a pitch to tie up the hitter. 41.6% of the swings resulted in tied up, but the problem was that it produced just 13% whiffs. As his main pitch, Brown needed to find the upper part of the zone where he has usually dominated and make hitters chase the sinker at the corners of the zone.
The adjustment got underway to the point that, in his last 10 starts, tied up swings dropped to 18.6%, flailed doubled (32.6%) and whiff has risen to 26.4%. That explains part of another result, and it has been the improvement in late swings during this recent stretch. When the sinker reaches this point and breaks hitters’ timing, Brown’s entire arsenal around it becomes more effective thanks to the great contrast of his knuckle curveball, cutter and changeup.
The curve also took an important step, further improving its swing-and-miss rate from 30.5% to 38.7%. As you can see in the table, the four-seam shows another type of evolution. It continues generating a similar whiff rate (23.4%), but Perfect Contact fell from 24.7% to 15.6%. The more Brown’s arsenal works, the smaller the opponents’ margin for error becomes as his pitches create different problems.
The bad news for Brown is that the Astros still cannot take enough advantage of his starts, and the bullpen has wasted the win probability that his dominance is generating. The Astros will face a finish that could seem easy, but in reality, their results against the Athletics and Mariners have been puzzling: against both opponents, the team is 6-14 this season, with a –16 run differential.
Yirsandy is a baseball writer specializing in MLB coverage with experience across multiple teams and storylines. He currently writes for Diamond Centric, where he covers the New York Mets, San Diego Padres, Chicago Cubs, Milwaukee Brewers, and Kansas City Royals. My work focuses on game coverage, player analysis, and storytelling that connects performance with context. My Substack has also been an important part of my writing development, where I’ve built much of my baseball coverage and storytelling voice over time. I’m passionate about combining reporting, research, and thoughtful analysis to produce engaging baseball content for readers.

item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK (AP) — Cristopher Sánchez earned his major league-leading 18th win Sunday, leading the Philadelphia Phillies to a 7-2 victory over the New York Mets.
The Phillies (86-70), who salvaged a split of the four-game series, entered Sunday in the third National League wild-card spot, one game behind the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres and four games clear of the Arizona Diamondbacks.
Sánchez surrendered six hits — including Bo Bichette’s sixth-inning homer — and struck out six over 6 1/3 innings as he snapped a tie with the Boston Red Sox’s Sonny Gray for the big league lead in wins.
Join our family of readers starting at $5 for your first month and support local, unbiased journalism.
Already have an account? Log in to continue.
Otherwise, follow the link below to join.
| Please log in to continue |
The last Phillies pitcher to lead the majors in wins was Steve Carlton with 23 in 1982.
Justin Crawford had a three-run triple and Luis Arraez finished with two RBIs. Alec Bohm and Trea Turner each had run-scoring hits. Kyle Schwarber tied a career high with four walks.
Rookie Jonah Tong (2-2) gave up four runs and struck out five in 4 2/3 innings for the last-place Mets, who finished 36-45 at home — their worst record at Citi Field since the 2013 team went 33-48.
PIRATES 4, ROYALS 3
PITTSBURGH (AP) — Rafael Flores Jr. hit the go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth inning to help Pittsburgh to a win over Kansas City and complete a series sweep.
After Ryan O’Hearn led off with a single to center, Flores sent a slider from Nate Pearson (2-3) into the left-field bleachers for his 10th homer this season.
Pittsburgh rallied with a two-run homer in the eighth for a second straight day. Brandon Lowe had his 33rd of the season in a 6-5 win Saturday.
Carmen Mlodzinki (8-7) got the win. He allowed two runs and three hits in three innings. The reliever gave up a pinch-hit, two-run home run to Vinnie Pasquantino that gave Kansas City a 3-2 lead with two outs in the seventh.
Mason Montgomery earned his 16th save. He retired the first two batters in the ninth before Luke Maile hit a double and took third on a fielding error by Jake Mangum. Montgomery got Isaac Collins to fly out to right to strand Maile.
The Royals went ahead 1-0 in the first inning with three straight singles off Lake Bachar. Bobby Witt Jr. beat out a groundball to second baseman Lowe. He moved to third on a single to right from Jac Caglianone and scored when Perez shot one through the middle of the infield.
RAYS 5, RED SOX 1
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Griffin Jax tossed five shutout innings and the Tampa Bay crept closer to the AL East title with a victory over Boston.
The Rays will have an opportunity to clinch the franchise’s fifth division title during Tuesday’s doubleheader at the New York Yankees.
Boston would have clinched a playoff spot with a victory. The Red Sox, who were 32-46 and 15 1/2 games back in the AL East on June 24, have since gone 52-25. They could still wrap up a spot Sunday with a Houston loss.
Jax (8-10) allowed three singles and worked out of a bases-loaded jam in the fifth inning by striking out Roman Anthony. Cole Sulser, Brody Hopkins and Steven Matz each pitched an inning of scoreless relief.
Boston’s Trevor Story spoiled the shutout in the ninth with a one-out home run off right-hander Ty Johnson.
The Rays scored four first-inning runs off left-hander Patrick Sandoval (1-7). Jonny DeLuca smashed a two-run, bases-loaded double down the left-field line and Chandler Simpson followed with a two-run single. Sandoval began the inning by walking Yandy Diaz and Ryan Vilade, then surrendering a single to Junior Caminero.
CUBS 9, REDS 1
CINCINNATI (AP) — Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 45th home run as Chicago moved closer to clinching a postseason berth with a victory over Cincinnati.
Chicago (87-69) reduced its magic number to one and could wrap up a berth if the Diamondbacks lose to the Yankees later Sunday.
The Cubs began the day tied with the Padres and one game ahead of the Phillies for the top NL wild-card spot which would earn them home-field advantage in the wild-card round. The Cubs own the tiebreakers over the Diamondbacks, Padres, and Phillies.
Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman left Sunday’s game in the fourth inning after being struck in the face by a foul ball off the bat of Michael Busch while standing near the on-deck circle.
Cubs left-hander David Peterson (9-8) allowed a run on three hits in seven innings with one walk and seven strikeouts.
The Cubs loaded the bases with one out in the third. Ian Happ singled in a run and Nico Hoerner walked to force in another to extend Chicago’s lead to 3-0. Pedro Ramirez’s two-run single made the score 5-0.
Reds right-hander Rhett Lowder (6-12) allowed five earned runs on six hits with three walks and three strikeouts.
CARDINALS 5, NATIONALS 3
ST. LOUIS (AP) — Iván Herrera hit a pair of home runs, and Leo Bernal also homered as St. Louis scored three runs in the eighth inning to come from behind and beat Washington.
Bernal hit his fifth homer of the season off Yovanny Cruz (0-2) after Erik Tolman walked Jordan Walker with two outs in the eighth inning.
Herrera hit his second homer of the game and 18th of the season to tie the game at 3-all after hitting a solo shot in the first inning.
It was Herrera’s third career multi-homer game and second this season after going deep twice on June 13 at Minnesota.
Luis Gastelum (5-3) pitched a scoreless eighth inning for St. Louis, and Riley O’Brien pitched a perfect ninth to earn his National League-leading 38th save.
Cardinals starter Quinn Mathews allowed three runs on seven hits and two walks in a career-high seven innings.
Jake Irvin allowed two runs on three hits and had eight strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings for the Nationals.

item.dc:creator: Bill Ladson
item.description: CINCINNATI – Al comenzar el domingo el último juego de la serie contra los Rojos, el jardinero central de los Cachorros, Pete Crow-Armstrong, venía de un fin de semana frustrante, al irse de 10-0 con cuatro ponches en los primeros dos encuentros de la serie. item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI – Al comenzar el domingo el último juego de la serie contra los Rojos, el jardinero central de los Cachorros, Pete Crow-Armstrong, venía de un fin de semana frustrante, al irse de 10-0 con cuatro ponches en los primeros dos encuentros de la serie. Pero dejó atrás esos días complicados al quedarse a un triple de completar el ciclo y ayudar a Chicago a aplastar 9-1 a los Rojos en el Great American Ball Park.
La victoria dejó a los Cachorros un poco más cerca de la postemporada, pero necesitan que los Yankees derroten a los D-backs más tarde la tarde del domingo para asegurar oficialmente su boleto a octubre. Chicago tiene a su favor el criterio de desempate por enfrentamientos directos ante los Padres (5-1) y los Filis (6-1), los dos equipos que están por debajo en la lucha por los Comodines de la Liga Nacional, lo que le da ventaja en la pelea por obtener la localía para la Serie del Comodín, que comienza el 29 de septiembre.
Crow-Armstrong se fue de 5-3 con un jonrón y dos carreras impulsadas. Todo comenzó en el primer inning ante el derecho de los Rojos, Rhett Lowder. Crow-Armstrong conectó un sencillo al jardín derecho y luego se robó la segunda base, quedando a dos estafadas de lograr la primera temporada 40-40 en la historia de los Cachorros. Finalmente anotó con un sencillo de Alex Bregman, quien salió del juego en el cuarto episodio tras recibir en la cabeza el impacto de una pelota de foul conectada por su compañero Michael Busch.
Chicago anotó cuatro carreras ante Lowder en el tercer episodio, con PCA como principal protagonista. Abrió el inning con un doble y anotó la segunda rayita del juego gracias a un sencillo de Ian Happ. Fue el 30mo doble de la temporada para PCA, convirtiéndose en el 10mo jugador en la historia de Grandes Ligas con al menos una campaña de 40 o más jonrones, 30 o más dobles y 30 o más bases robadas, uniéndose al venezolano Ronald Acuña Jr., Jeff Bagwell (dos veces), Ryan Braun, Ellis Burks, el cubano José Canseco, Shohei Ohtani, Alex Rodríguez, el dominicano Alfonso Soriano y Larry Walker.
Crow-Armstrong luego conectó un cuadrangular en el quinto capítulo, su 45to de la temporada, para igualar a Kyle Schwarber en el liderato de MLB.
La estrella de los Cachorros tuvo una última oportunidad de conseguir el triple que le faltaba para completar el ciclo en el octavo acto ante Carson Spiers, pero elevó al campocorto dominicano Elly De La Cruz para el primer out de la entrada.

item.title: [Bleed Cubbie Blue] Cubs 9, Reds 1: Pete Crow-Armstrong ties Kyle Schwarber for the MLB home run lead
item.dc:creator: Al Yellon
item.description: After going 0-for-10 with four strikeouts in the first two games of this series, Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong had himself another big day in the third contest. PCA singled, doubled, homered and stole a base and helped lead the Cubs to a 9-1 blowout of the Reds, a victory tempered by a freak injury to Alex Bregman. More on the latter anon, first let’s wrap this win. The Cubs got on the board in the first inning. PCA led off the game with a single and stole second, his 38th [VIDEO]. The
item.content:encoded:
After going 0-for-10 with four strikeouts in the first two games of this series, Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong had himself another big day in the third contest. PCA singled, doubled, homered and stole a base and helped lead the Cubs to a 9-1 blowout of the Reds, a victory tempered by a freak injury to Alex Bregman. More on the latter anon, first let’s wrap this win.
The Cubs got on the board in the first inning. PCA led off the game with a single and stole second, his 38th [VIDEO].
The Cubs extended their lead in the third. PCA led off with a double. A note on that double from BCB’s JohnW53:
With his third-inning double, Pete Crow-Armstrong has at least 30 homers, doubles and steals.
Only one Cub had done that before: PCA, last year.
Forty players on other teams have done it, 12 of them also multiple times. PCA is among 10 with two. Alfonso Soriano did it four times; Barry Bonds and Jose Ramirez, three.
It was noted on the Marquee broadcast that PCA’s 40-HR, 30-double, 30-steal year is the first ever by a MLB center fielder — nope, not Willie Mays, not Ken Griffey Jr., no one, until now. I’ve said it before, but don’t ever forget what you are seeing from Pete this year — it is truly historic.
Anyway, PCA then went to third on a ground out by Seiya Suzuki. The Cubs then loaded the bases on walks drawn by Michael Busch and Bregman.
Per the Marquee broadcast, that’s 22 bases-loaded walks for the Cubs this year, the most in MLB.
With the bases still loaded, Michael Conforto struck out, but Pedro Ramirez followed with a two-run single to make it 5-0 [VIDEO].
Now to the Bregman incident in the fourth inning. With two out, Busch hit a foul ball that struck Bregman, who was in the on-deck circle, in the face. Bregman immediately left the game and was replaced by Matt Shaw. Here’s what that looked like [VIDEO].
Per Craig Counsell’s postgame remarks, the ball hit Bregman in the cheekbone, which is swollen. There was also a facial cut, but we don’t know anything beyond that. Hopefully it’s not too serious and Bregman doesn’t have a concussion.
While all this was going on, David Peterson was sailing along, striking out seven over the first four innings. The Reds made it 5-1 on a solo homer by JJ Bleday in the fourth.
The Cubs got that run right back in the fifth on a solo homer by Michael Conforto, his 15th [VIDEO].
If you’re keeping track:
Kyle Tucker, 16 HR, 515 AB
Michael Conforto, 15 HR, 294 AB
That blast tied PCA with Kyle Schwarber for the MLB lead. The Cubs also lead MLB in home runs with 217; as noted on the Marquee broadcast, the last time the Cubs led all of baseball in home runs was 1958, led by Ernie Banks with 47 in his first MVP season.
Peterson completed six innings, allowing three hits and just the one run on Bleday’s homer. Here are his seven strikeouts [VIDEO].
More on Peterson’s afternoon from BCB’s JohnW53:
David Peterson’s quality start was his fifth as a Cub, fourth most on the team. Shota Imanaga has 14, as many as the next two combined: Matthew Boyd, eight, and Colin Rea, six. Edward Cabrera and Jameson Taillon both have four. Five others have one to three.
Peterson could be a valuable weapon in the postseason, either as a starter or out of the bullpen.
The Cubs weren’t done homering, either. After Caleb Thielbar threw a scoreless seventh, Suzuki lofted his 25th into the batter’s eye to make it 9-1 [VIDEO].
More on recent Cubs home runs from John:
With their three home runs, the Cubs have hit nine in their last four games (three, one, two, three). They had hit 12 in their previous 14 games, since smacking a team-record nine at home vs. the Brewers on Aug. 31.
Edward Cabrera was given the eighth inning, a good low-leverage situation. He allowed a leadoff single and after retiring the next hitter, another Reds batter reached on an error by Ramirez. But Cabrera got Elly De La Cruz to hit into an inning-ending double play.
Colin Rea finished up with a 1-2-3 ninth, his first game action in 11 days, on just eight pitches. Here’s the final out [VIDEO].
The Cubs will clinch a postseason berth if the Yankees defeat the Diamondbacks Sunday, a game that’s just begun at the time of this recap. The Padres, tied with the Cubs for the top wild card spot with the Cubs holding the tiebreaker, are playing the Marlins in a contest in San Diego that’s also just underway. The Phillies defeated the Mets Sunday, so the Cubs still lead Philadelphia by a game. Thanks to the Mets for taking two of the four games from the Phillies over the weekend.
The Cubs have Monday off, then open the final regular season home series Tuesday evening against the Marlins at Wrigley Field. Kevin Gausman will start for the Cubs and Janson Junk will go for Miami. Game time Tuesday is 6:40 p.m. CT and TV coverage will be via Marquee Sports Network.

item.title: [MLB.com] PCA's latest offensive outburst puts Cubs on verge of playoff clinch
item.dc:creator: Bill Ladson
item.description: CINCINNATI – Entering Sunday’s finale against the Reds, Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong had a frustrating weekend, going 0-for-10 with four strikeouts over the first two games of the series. But he made up for those difficult days by coming a triple shy of the cycle and helping Chicago pound the Reds, 9-1, at Great American Ball Park. item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI – Entering Sunday’s finale against the Reds, Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong had a frustrating weekend, going 0-for-10 with four strikeouts over the first two games of the series. But he made up for those difficult days by coming a triple shy of the cycle and helping Chicago pound the Reds, 9-1, at Great American Ball Park.
The victory helped bring the Cubs an inch closer to the postseason, but they need the Yankees to beat the D-backs later Sunday afternoon to officially clinch October baseball. Chicago owns the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Padres (5-1) and the Phillies (6-1), the two teams below them in the NL Wild Card race, giving them the upper hand to earn home-field advantage for the Wild Card Series starting Sept. 29.
Crow-Armstrong went 3-for-5 with a homer and two RBIs. It all started in the first inning against Reds right-hander Rhett Lowder. Crow-Armstrong singled to right field and then stole second base, putting him two steals shy of the first 40-40 season in Cubs franchise history. He eventually scored on a single by Alex Bregman, who left the game in the fourth after getting hit in the head by a foul ball from teammate Michael Busch.
Chicago scored four runs off Lowder in the third frame, and it was PCA who led the charge. He led off with a double and scored the second run of the game on a single by Ian Happ. It was PCA’s 30th double of the season, making him the 10th player in Major League Baseball history to notch 40-plus homers, 30-plus doubles and 30-plus stolen bases in a season at least once, joining Ronald Acuña Jr., Jeff Bagwell (twice), Ryan Braun, Ellis Burks, Jose Canseco, Shohei Ohtani, Alex Rodriguez, Alfonso Soriano and Larry Walker.
Crow-Armstrong later homered in the fifth for his 45th blast of the season, tying him with Kyle Schwarber for the MLB lead.
The Cubs star got one last chance to tally the triple that would complete his cycle in the eighth against Carson Spiers, but he popped up to shortstop Elly De La Cruz for the first out of the inning.

item.content:encoded:
Wyatt Langford convirtió un elevado sacrificio de rutina en una de las jugadas más espectaculares de la temporada de los Rangers.
Con Langford en tercera base, Evan Carter conectó un elevado al jardín central. Langford hizo el pisa y corre y aceleró hacia el home mientras el lanzamiento obligaba al catcher Alejandro Kirk a colocarse directamente en su camino.
Entonces, Langford decidió saltar.
La estrella de los Rangers pasó por encima de Kirk, aterrizó más allá del plato y rápidamente regresó para tocar el home y anotar la carrera.
La increíble jugada ayudó a Texas a conseguir una victoria 6-2 ante Toronto y quedar como único líder de la División Oeste de la Liga Americana, a una semana del final de la temporada regular.

item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays may be without their ace starting pitcher as they pursue a playoff berth during the final week of the 2026 MLB regular season.
Dylan Cease underwent an MRI exam on his right shoulder Saturday night and has been scratched from his start scheduled for Wednesday against the Baltimore Orioles. Blue Jays manager John Schneider told reporters Sunday that Cease could be shut down for the remainder of the season.
Going into Sunday's play, Toronto (76-79) was three games behind the Chicago White Sox (79-76) for the American League's third and final wild-card playoff spot. The Houston Astros are one game ahead of the Blue Jays in the standings at 77-78. Toronto has a 4.2% chance of making the postseason, according to FanGraphs.
.@thehazelmae and @ArdenZwelling provide the latest on Dylan Cease and the Blue Jays' pitching plan as they try to stay alive in the AL Wild Card race. pic.twitter.com/hhaPPLdHea
— Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) September 20, 2026
If Cease's MRI shows no serious concerns, it's possible that he could make one more start during the regular season's final three-game series with the Cincinnati Reds. But if the Blue Jays are too far back in the playoff race by then, it's unlikely Cease would pitch again.
Schneider explained that Cease has been dealing with an issue in his shoulder for several weeks and has been throwing with less velocity. The eight-year veteran described the problem as shoulder fatigue, according to Schneider.
In his start Friday versus the Texas Rangers, Cease's fastball was clocked as low as 90 mph and he pitched only 2 2/3 innings in a 7-1 loss. He finished with 6 walks and 3 strikeouts, allowing 1 earned run and 6 hits.
"It wasn't alarming enough to say, 'Hey, I can't pitch,' and was hoping to kind of come out of it," Schneider said, via The Athletic, "But just really hasn't bounced back. So I think [we] just said, 'All right, let's take a look at it.'"
Cease, 30, is in the first year of a seven-year, $210 million contract he signed with the Blue Jays in November.
He is second in the AL with a 2.40 ERA and trails only Milwaukee's Jacob Misiorowski among MLB pitchers with 239 strikeouts. Overall, he has an 11-6 record in 29 starts, pitching 169 innings.

item.content:encoded:
With the Texas Rangers pushing toward the postseason, Langford turned a routine sacrifice fly into one of the wildest plays of their season Saturday night, hurdling Toronto Blue Jays catcher Alejandro Kirk before scrambling back to touch home plate. Texas defeated Toronto 6-2 at Globe Life Field, a victory that moved the Rangers into sole possession of first place in the American League West with one week remaining in the regular season. And the decisive moment came with Langford literally leaping over an obstacle in the sixth inning. Langford was standing at third base when Evan Carter lifted a fly ball to center field. As the ball traveled toward Brett Bateman, Langford tagged and took off for home. Bateman's throw arrived slightly up the line, forcing Kirk to move into Langford's path. So Langford jumped.

item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays are looking to avoid being swept by the Texas Rangers on Sunday and have made some changes to their lineup.
Toronto is coming off a 6-2 loss on Saturday after losing 7-1 on Friday. The two losses seemingly ended the Blue Jays' playoff hopes.
The Blue Jays are now 76-79.
Toronto Blue Jays Announce Brandon Valenzuela News
Toronto is looking to avoid the series sweep and has made some major changes to its lineup.
The Blue Jays are resting some regular players, as starting catcher Alejandro Kirk is getting the day off, with Brandon Valenzuela getting the start. He will also be hitting eighth.
Toronto's lineup on Sunday is as follows:
- B. Bateman CF
- V. Guerrero Jr. 1B
- N. Lukes RF
- K. Okamoto 3B
- S. Keys DH
- J. Smith LF
- A. Giménez SS
- B. Valenzuela C
- E. Clement 2B
Toronto will start Spencer Miles as the opener, as it's a bullpen game with Spencer Arrighetti getting the bulk of the innings.
Kirk getting the day off isn't a surprise, as Valenzuela has been catching and starting a lot on Sunday to give Kirk the day off in the series finale.
Valenzuela is a great defensive catcher with a cannon of an arm, yet his bat has struggled as of late. He's hitting .217 with 8 home runs and 21 RBIs. However, in his last 7 games, he's hitting .105 with 0 home runs and 0 RBIs, while striking out 5 times.
Toronto Right Now
The Blue Jays have struggled all year, and now their playoff fate is likely sealed.
Toronto lost the first two games of a three-game road series against Texas, which seemingly ended their playoff hopes. The Blue Jays have been blown out in both of their games against the Rangers, which is frustrating for the team.
Jose Soriano struggled in the outing, which was frustrating for the team as the Blue Jays sent Dylan Cease and Soriano, their two best pitchers, in the first two games.
"We're still positive. Doesn't matter the result, we're still positive," said Soriano. "We're not going to win every game we play. The other team's trying to win, too. So, we try to control what we can control and play one game at a time."
The Blue Jays will go on a three-game road trip against the Baltimore Orioles starting on Monday. Toronto will end its season with a three-game home series against the Cincinnati Reds.
Toronto likely has to finish the year 7-0 to have any shot of making the playoffs.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Toronto Blue Jays Announce Brandon Valenzuela News During Rangers Series appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Tarik Skubal leaves Dodgers temporarily for personal reasons 1 day after start against Giants
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh
item.description: Tarik Skubal has been one of the Los Angeles Dodgers' biggest additions this season, but the veteran left-hander will now step away from the team temporarily. The Dodgers placed Skubal on the bereavement list Sunday, one day after he started against the San Francisco Giants. Manager Dave Roberts announced the move, according to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya. Skubal is expected to be away from the team for a few days. The Dodgers will adjust their pitching plans while he handles a personal matter.
item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal has been one of the Los Angeles Dodgers' biggest additions this season, but the veteran left-hander will now step away from the team temporarily.
The Dodgers placed Skubal on the bereavement list Sunday, one day after he started against the San Francisco Giants. Manager Dave Roberts announced the move, according to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.
Skubal is expected to be away from the team for a few days. The Dodgers will adjust their pitching plans while he handles a personal matter.
Tarik Skubal leaves Dodgers after Giants start
The timing comes immediately after Skubal's latest start. He worked five innings against the Giants on Saturday, allowing eight hits, four earned runs and two walks while striking out three.
The Dodgers still won 10-4, with Mookie Betts going 4-for-4 and Will Smith adding a home run. Skubal received the win despite allowing four earned runs in the outing.
The start came during an important stretch for the Dodgers, who are already looking toward their postseason rotation. Skubal has given Los Angeles another frontline option since joining the club from Detroit.
His temporary absence, however, will force the Dodgers to make a short-term adjustment.
Dodgers turn to Emmet Sheehan
Sep 3, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) walks to the dugout during a pitching against the St. Louis Cardinals during the sixth inning at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
Emmet Sheehan is expected to step back into the Dodgers' pitching plans Sunday. The right-hander provides another option as Los Angeles manages its rotation while Skubal is away.
The Dodgers have enough pitching depth to cover a short absence. Yoshinobu Yamamoto remains in the rotation, while Blake Snell has returned from the injured list.
Los Angeles has also already secured the NL West, giving the club some flexibility with its pitching plans. That could allow the Dodgers to avoid putting extra pressure on Skubal to return immediately.
Still, his availability will matter once the postseason begins. Skubal has been an important part of the Dodgers' rotation since the trade, and the team will want him ready for October.
For now, the Dodgers will move forward without their ace for the next few days. The focus will be on Skubal's return timeline and how Los Angeles adjusts its pitching plans in his absence.

item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, the New York Yankees will finish their series with the Arizona Diamondbacks.
The Yankees won the first game by a score of 9-2 (on Friday).
Paul Goldschmidt had one hit, one walk and two runs.
He was not in the lineup for Saturday’s 5-3 loss.
Goldschmidt also remains out of the lineup on Sunday.
7x MLB All-Star Will Be A Yankees Free Agent
With the season nearly over, it’s worth noting that Goldschmidt will become a free agent who is available to sign with any team in the MLB this winter.
He is being paid $4 million for the 2026 season.
If Goldschmidt wants to keep playing, it’s hard to imagine a world where the Yankees would not want him.
It’s also fair to wonder if any other teams would have interest.
In addition to being an incredible veteran in the clubhouse, the 39-year-old is still a very productive player.
Goldschmidt is batting .253 with 85 hits, 18 home runs, 50 RBIs, 44 runs and one stolen base in 102 games this year.
Looking At The Rest Of Goldschmidt’s Career
Goldschmidt was picked in the 8th round of the 2009 MLB Draft.
He spent the first eight years of his career with the Diamondbacks.
From 2013-18, Goldschmidt made five straight trips to the All-Star Game.
Following Arizona, Goldschmidt had another strong run with the St. Louis Cardinals (2019-24).
He made another trip to the All-Star Game (and won the 2022 National League MVP Award).
Looking At New York Right Now
The Yankees are the second-place team in the American League East with an 89-65 record in 154 games.
They have won seven out of their last ten games.

item.content:encoded:
Por: Edgar Ochoa/ NOTIVER
El “Chevi” va por título
El receptor veracruzano Alberto Barriga cerró un 2026 de consolidación en las Ligas Menores con los Arizona Diamondbacks, confirmando que su nombre sigue tomando fuerza dentro de la organización; el joven originario de Loma del Carmen, Veracruz comenzó la temporada en Clase A Avanzada con Hillsboro y, gracias a su rendimiento y consistencia, consiguió dar el salto a Doble A con los Amarillo Sod Poodles, donde continuó demostrando sus condiciones.
En el balance global del año, Barriga conectó 87 imparables, disparó 13 cuadrangulares y produjo 49 carreras en 354 turnos, para un promedio de .246, números que hablan de un bate que sigue madurando.
Pero donde realmente ha llamado la atención es detrás del plato, con un brazo catalogado como de categoría doble-plus y un buen trabajo en el encuadre de pitcheos, además de la capacidad para manejar al cuerpo de lanzadores en momentos de presión.
A sus apenas 21 años, el veracruzano fue parte importante de los Amarillo Sod Poodles en su camino a la gran final de la Liga de Texas, luego de celebrar en el terreno la clasificación tras superar la semifinal.
Ahora viene lo bueno, porque Barriga y su equipo ya tienen la mira puesta en Springfield, sucursal de los St. Louis Cardinals, para disputar la Serie de Campeonato de Doble A, al mejor de tres juegos, que arranca este domingo.
Sin duda, una gran oportunidad para que este talento de Loma del Carmen, Veracruz siga escribiendo su propia historia y poniendo muy en alto el nombre de Veracruz.
Domingo softbolero
Este domingo se juega la cuarta jornada del Softbol 40 y más “Otoño 2026” en la Liga de Playa de Vacas, y la cartelera promete intensidad total desde temprano en el diamante veracruzano.
La actividad arranca calientita a las 9:00 AM con un duelazo: Notaría 50 buscará sacarse la espina tras caer ante Súper Médicos, teniendo la dura tarea de frenar a unos motivados Súper Pollos, que vienen de vapulear a Wikiboyz.
Más tarde, a las 11:00 horas, el equipo de Compadres & Amigos hará su aparición en la jornada dominical para medirse cara a cara contra el encendido cuadro de Súper Médicos.
Finalmente, para cerrar con broche de oro a las 13:00horas, Dragones y Wikiboyz se verán las caras en un duelo muy interesante, pues ambos urgen de la victoria luego de que los mitológicos cayeran la semana pasada 8-2 ante la escuadra de C & A, en un juego donde Juan Cortés se llevó los honores y Héctor Jiménez cargó con el amargo descalabro.
¡Preparen las porras porque la pelota blanda va a volar con todo este fin de semana en Playa de Vacas!

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers made a flurry of roster moves before Sunday afternoon's series finale against the Giants, placing left-hander Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list, recalling right-handers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt from Triple-A Oklahoma City and optioning right-hander Seth Halvorsen.
The Dodgers also gave right fielder Kyle Tucker Sunday off after he fouled a ball off the lower knee/upper shin area on his right leg on Saturday night. Manager Dave Roberts does not think the soreness will become an ongoing issue for Tucker, who is expected back in the lineup on Tuesday.
Here's how these moves will impact the Dodgers on Sunday and beyond:
Skubal will be away from the team for "a couple days," Roberts said. Players may spend between three to seven days on the bereavement list, so Skubal might not miss his next start, which is projected to come on Friday in San Francisco.
"Some personal stuff going on," Roberts said, "but he's fine."
Skubal is 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA in nine starts since being dealt to L.A. ahead of the Trade Deadline.
Sheehan was set to pitch bulk innings on Sunday behind opener Jack Dreyer. The thought was that pitching Sheehan behind an opener could not only help him get deeper into the game, but also prepare him for a possible bullpen role in the postseason, which would be his only path to making the roster.
In his previous two starts for the Dodgers, Sheehan allowed one earned run across 11 2/3 innings. After a strong stint in Triple-A, he has looked to trend in the right direction in what has been an inconsistent season overall (5-8, 4.79 ERA).
Tucker has heated up at the end of the first season of his four-year, $240 million contract, which has been disappointing (his .728 OPS is on track to be a career-worst mark in a full season). Since Sept. 9, he's hitting 15-for-35 (.429) with five home runs and 35 total bases, his most in a 10-game span this season.
On Saturday, Tucker exited the game after six innings due to a combination of the hit-by-pitch and the lopsided score. He said he feels fine, but Roberts decided to give him an extra day to rest after Tucker had played the previous nine games without a day off.
"I feel like everyone's grinding at this point in the season," Tucker said. "But I'll be good with it."

item.title: [FanSided] MLB Rumors: Red Sox-Randy Arozarena rumblings and what's next for the Pirates

item.content:encoded:
Sure, the pennant race has taken centerstage the last few weeks, but soon enough 18 teams will start their offseasons earlier than expected. The Seattle Mariners, somehow, are one of those teams. It'll likely cost Dan Wilson his job, and force former AL Postseason heroes off the roster. But the Mariners aren't alone in terms of disappointing campaigns from contenders who made the postseason just a year ago. What of the Detroit Tigers, or even Cincinnati Reds in the National League?
In essence, that's what this time of the season is about for 18 teams. Looking back at what went wrong, and adjusting their offseason plans from there. Unfortunately for all of baseball, we're staring down the barrel at a lockout, which could force teams to rush their plans or miss out altogether, especially when it comes to Randy Arozarena, Brandon Lowe and Torey Lovullo.
Brandon Lowe wants to sign a new contract with the Pirates
Lowe had a series of walkoff hits this past week to prove his importance to the Pirates, even as Pittsburgh misses the postseason once again. The Pirates properly addressed their lineup this past winter, in part by trading for Lowe on an expiring contract. You could argue he's been their most consistent player, especially at the dish. Pairing Lowe, who is 32 years old, with Konnor Griffin for the next few seasons would show Pirates fans the front office and ownership is committed to winning for a change.
“I think this team’s got a very bright future and a lot of good players, and there’s a lot of good baseball that’s going to be played in this park for a long time. [If] they want to talk, I’m all ears," Lowe said on a possible extension.
Yet, Lowe could be a little out of the Pirates price range after the season he's had. Lowe 33 home runs and an .826 OPS in the middle of Pittsburgh's lineup. Considering just how thin the free-agent market is in terms of proven infielders — especially those who can hit at the level Lowe can — could make it tougher to meet his asking price.
Torey Lovullo knows this could be it with the Diamondbacks
The Diamondbacks August surge has turned into a September lull. The Diamondbacks remain alive in the NL Wild Card standings and face the San Diego Padres to end the season. Thus, if they can keep their deficit to three games or less, then perhaps the Snakes can fight for Torey Lovullo's job after all.
It's not as though Lovullo's message has grown stale in Arizona, but the way he dealt with the Ketel Marte drama lacked conviction. Eventually, all managers must move on the greener pastures, and Lovullo knows this.
“I understand it, it’s the realities of this game," Lovullo said, “and you got to win. That’s what it comes down to. I think we won a lot here. Have we won enough."
If Arizona can sneak into the playoffs, perhaps he can change his fate.
Could the Red Sox sign Randy Arozarena?
Arozarena is a free agent after the season and he's a fan favorite in Seattle. Despite Randy's World Baseball Classic kerfuffle with Cal Raleigh, the two seem to have a solid relationship at this point in the season. Arozarena rebounded and had a solid year, accruing a 5.3 bWAR and .861 OPS with 26 home runs as of this writing. Arozarena could be one of the best hitters on the open market. He's an above-average defensive outfielder, as well, with an arm we wouldn't recommend running on.
The 31-year-old was linked to the Boston Red Sox earlier this week by Ryan Divish, who is not a Boston sports media pawn, I can assure you. Still, the Red Sox have a lot of outfield depth as is, including in the farm system. Does it make sense to add Arozarena for a premium price?
For now, these are just rumblings. Arozarena can and should be connected to any number of teams this offseason, especiallty given the market lacks proven sluggers. Randy would be an upgrade for most teams, but the Mariners would be better off ponying up, barring there aren't any leftover issues between him and Raleigh.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers announced a major roster move ahead of Sunday's series finale against the San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers have recalled right-handed pitchers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt from Triple-A. Sheehan will take down bulk innings on Sunday as LA looks to preserve the bullpen heading into the final week of the regular season.
As for the corresponding moves, left-handed pitcher Tarik Skubal was placed on the bereavement list and will be away from the team for "a couple days," per manager Dave Roberts. Additionally, right-hander Seth Halvorsen was optioned.
Dodgers Recall Emmet Sheehan, Kyle Hurt
Sheehan was surprisingly demoted this past week amid a dominant stretch of play.
Across his last two starts at the MLB level, Sheehan allowed just one run over 11.2 innings with 15 strikeouts.
“Man, Emmet’s been great. The last two have been fantastic,” Roberts said after he was sent down. “Emmet’s done everything he can do in his power to force our hand, which I love. ... The last two have been really good.”
Now, Sheehan is getting another opportunity to take down bulk innings and audition for a spot on the postseason roster. If he has another strong outing, he'll likely secure a spot in the postseason bullpen as a multi-inning option.
As for Hurt, he's been up and down multiple times this season. The right-hander has made 43 appearances at the big league level, compiling a 4.33 ERA with 56 strikeouts to 23 walks over 43.2 innings of work.
He's unlikely to factor into the team's October plans, but could take down innings over the final week of the regular season.
Dodgers Place Tarik Skubal on Bereavement List, Option Seth Halvorsen
Skubal will deal with a personal matter for the next couple days, but should be back in time to make one more start before the conclusion of the regular season.
He pitched on Saturday, allowing four runs over five innings with three strikeouts.
As for Halvorsen, he's made 11 appearances at the big league level for the Dodgers this season, accruing an 8.10 ERA with six strikeouts to two walks over 10 innings of work.
He was acquired by the Dodgers a couple weeks before the trade deadline in a three-player deal with the Colorado Rockies. He likely won't return to the big league club for the remainder of the year.

He was born and raised in Los Angeles and has extensively covered Southern California sports in his career. Noah is the publisher of Dodgers on SI after contributing as a writer and editor over the last three years.

item.title: [New York Post] Kyle Tucker out of Dodgers lineup as new injury concern surfaces
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: Just as Kyle Tucker was finally starting to heat up, he became the latest Dodgers star to suffer a potential injury concern. On Sunday, Tucker was not in the Dodgers’ lineup for their series-finale against the San Francisco Giants, absent a day after he left Saturday’s game early following a foul ball off his right knee/shin area. The good news: Tucker insisted on Sunday that he felt fine and didn’t anticipate it causing ongoing problems. Still, manager Dave Roberts had said Saturday night he ex
item.content:encoded:
Just as Kyle Tucker was finally starting to heat up, he became the latest Dodgers star to suffer a potential injury concern.
On Sunday, Tucker was not in the Dodgers’ lineup for their series-finale against the San Francisco Giants, absent a day after he left Saturday’s game early following a foul ball off his right knee/shin area.
The good news: Tucker insisted on Sunday that he felt fine and didn’t anticipate it causing ongoing problems.
Still, manager Dave Roberts had said Saturday night he expected Tucker in the lineup on Sunday, depending on how the issue progressed.
Tucker initially suffered the injury in the third inning Saturday night, when a foul ball banged high enough up his leg it evaded his shin pad.
The four-time All-Star immediately went down in pain, and was checked out by Roberts and a trainer for several moments.
Initially, Tucker stayed in the game, drawing a walk (and racing around the bases to later score a run) in the fifth while playing out in right field until the seventh.
However, he appeared to be moving around somewhat gingerly after the injury, and was ultimately removed once the score got out of reach in the Dodgers’ eventual 10-4 win.
Postgame, Tucker didn’t seem overly concerned with the issue, saying he should be “good with it” and that the lopsided score was a factor in his precautionary removal.
“I feel like everyone is grinding at this point of the season,” he noted.
On Sunday morning, he echoed that sentiment, saying Roberts had informed him Sunday they were “just gonna at least give me the day.”
The Dodgers will have to hope the injury doesn’t impact Tucker’s recently resurgent performance. In his last 10 games, the $240 million outfielder has finally started to turn a corner, going 15-for-35 with five home runs, nine extra-base hits and 11 RBIs in that stretch.
In 2024, a similar foul ball left Tucker with a right shin fracture that sidelined him for three months.
However, he said this one hit in a different spot of his leg, while once again downplaying the potential severity of the problem.
“This was a little different,” he said. “I feel fine.”

item.content:encoded:
The Arizona Diamondbacks play their final regular season game at Chase Field on Sunday, September 20 against the New York Yankees.
The D-backs won 5-3 on a walk-off homer by Pavin Smith Saturday night, following the a 9-2 loss in the series opener on Friday. It was an emotional win for the D-backs who were celebrating the 25th anniversary of their World Series Championship over the Yankees in 2001.
The D-backs' record is 81-74. They're four games behind the Philadelphia Phillies for the third NL Wild Card spot, and five games behind the San Diego Padres. Arizona plays the Padres in the final three-game series of the season next weekend in San Diego.
Starting Lineup
The Diamondbacks will have Gabriel Moreno behind the plate for the third game this series, and a day game after night. Typically that start would go to James McCann but in the team's current situation on the brink of elimination, expect Moreno to play every game.
Left-hand batters Smith and Jesus Sanchez are in the lineup at first base and DH respectively. Jordan Lawlar is out of the lineup again, and Tim Tawa will man centerfield. Pre game Torey Lovullo said he felt the right/left matchup favored putting Sanchez in the lineup over Lawlar.
Pitching Matchups
Right-hander Will Warren starts for the Yankees. He is 10-6 with a 3.89 ERA on the season, but has been red-hot as of late, allowing just two earned runs over his last four starts, 21 innings. Warren utilized a four-pitch mix of four-seamers (93.7 MPH), sinkers, sweeper, and changeups.
Corbin Burnes is making his third start since coming back from Tommy John Surgery. He's only thrown 7.2 innings so far, and his last outing was limited to 75 pitches, as he went 4.2 innings and allowed five earned runs. Expect that number to be up to 85 or even 90 pitches in this outing.
Burnes' velocity is understandably down from last year, averaging just 92.6 MPH on his trademark cutter, compared to 94.1 prior to the elbow injury that required surgery. Of perhaps greater concern is the pitch is not actually cutting. The glove-side horizontal movement in his Cy Young year was 4.1 inches. Last year it was 2.4 inches. In two starts so far it's just 0.4 inches.
What the movement looks like on the cutter will be the key element to watch in this game. Burnes may have to rely more on his curveball and changeup, along with his sinker if the cutter does not improve.
Following the game the D-backs will fly to Colorado to face the Rockies for three games starting Tuesday. With the off-day on Monday and every game a must win game, expect Torey Lovullo to pull out all stops to win should Burnes falter early, much as he did with Brandon Pfaadt on Saturday night. Pfaadt was pulled in the fifth inning, giving way to Justin Martinez.
Jack Sommers is a credentialed beat writer for Arizona Diamondbacks ON SI. He's also the co-host of the Snakes Territory Podcast and Youtube channel. Formerly a baseball operations department analyst for the D-backs, Jack also covered the team for MLB.com, The Associated Press, and SB Nation. Follow Jack on Twitter @shoewizard59
Follow shoewizard59

item.title: [pinstripealley.com] Yankees Rivalry Roundup: Rays rebound against Red Sox with walk-off
item.dc:creator: Andrew Mearns
item.description: The Yankees’ odds of winning the AL East are down to 2.8 percent per FanGraphs after getting walked off by the Diamondbacks last night. I know mathematically that makes sense, but the chances mentally feel even more extreme. I’ve been having “fun” (or whatever) comping the odds to certain pitchers from history getting a hit.
