item.content:encoded:
The Yankees’ odds of winning the AL East are down to 2.8 percent per FanGraphs after getting walked off by the Diamondbacks last night. I know mathematically that makes sense, but the chances mentally feel even more extreme. I’ve been having “fun” (or whatever) comping the odds to certain pitchers from history getting a hit. We are the dregs. Remember mid-2000s Mets pitcher Aaron Heilman? I personally remember him most for giving up the homer to Yadier Molina late in Game 7 of the 2006 NLCS, just before Adam Wainwright famously caught Carlos Beltrán looking to win the pennant.
Anyway, Heilman was a horrendous hitter. He singled once in his rookie year, and then never got another hit. He ended his career 1-for-47, so an .021 average. So the Yankees just need magic only a little bit more sufficient than that RBI single by Heilman off Sidney Ponson on August 12, 2003! Hell yeah.
It’s not happening, but we press on because it’s good to check up on what everyone else is doing anyway. Here’s what was going on Saturday.
Tampa Bay Rays (94-60) 2, Boston Red Sox (84-71) 1
The Yankees gained a full game on the Rays on Friday for the first time in over a week, as Boston snapped their six-game winning streak. There was no such fortune to be found yesterday though; Tampa Bay made sure of that well before first pitch in Arizona, and it only got worse from there. By the end of the night, the Rays once again had a five-game lead over the Yanks; Tampa Bay’s magic number (combination of Rays wins or Yankees losses) to clinch the AL East is four.
This one was a pitchers’ duel to the bitter end. Brayan Bello had easily his best outing of a turbulent season (and probably the best of his career), firing eight shutout frames at the Trop and fanning 11 Rays, tying a personal best from July 9, 2024. As he only went 5.1 in that one and faced merely the soon-to-depart-Oakland A’s rather than the division-leading Rays.
The only true blemish on Bello’s record came when Jonathan Aranda cracked an opposite-field homer to make it a 1-1 game in the fourth. Tampa Bay had a chance to make it 2-1 against Bello in the seventh when Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson led off with singles. Bello then induced a grounder from Victor Mesa Jr. to move up the runners, and then another off the bat of Richie Palacios to Trevor Story, who nailed pinch-runner Jonny DeLuca at home. Palacios swiped second, but Bello fanned Cedric Mullins to end the inning. The Rays went down in order in the eighth to end Bello’s brilliant night.
Unfortunately for Bello, a win wasn’t in the cards because Boston put up next to nothing against Freddy Peralta and the Rays’ pitching staff. Doubles by Caleb Durbin and Roman Anthony gave the Red Sox their one run in the second, but they were stymied from there. They had chances!
- Second inning after Anthony’s two-out double: Mickey Gasper lineout to center
- Fourth inning with runners on first and second, one out: Story strikeout, Durbin popout
- Fifth inning with runner on second, one out: Anthony groundout, Gasper strikeout
- Sixth inning with runners on first and second, two out: Durbin fly out to left
- Eighth inning after Adley Rutschman’s one-out double: Wilyer Abreu strikeout, Nick Sogard lineout
Even against lockdown Rays closer Bryan Baker, Boston had one last shot to take a late lead. After Story grounded out, Durbin lined a double down the left field line to put himself in scoring position for Jarren Duran. Durbin darted from second, however, and got thrown out stealing third. Duran promptly followed with a triple over DeLuca’s head in center. Isiah Kiner-Falefa bounced one to Junior Caminero at third to end the threat.
Granted a chance to walk it off, Tampa Bay didn’t waste it. Rather than blasting a homer to finish the game as he had twice earlier this homestand, Caminero began the ninth against Garrett Whitlock with a single to left. (A catwalk curtailed Durbin’s effort to catch a popup earlier in the AB.) DeLuca popped up, but Chandler Simpson grounded one through the six-hole for another hit. The runners moved up when catcher Connor Wong let a Whitlock sinker up bounce off his glove for a passed ball. Palacios ended the night with flare to center that fell in, securing the win for Tampa Bay. At least the Wild Card Series is also almost certainly going to be at Yankee Stadium now, I suppose.
AL Rock Fight
Cleveland Guardians (80-75) 12, The Athletics (61-94) 6
Two crooked numbers effectively decided Saturday’s affair with the A’s in a hurry. Tanner Bibee kind of stunk and would allow six runs in a dozen hits while failing to make through five, but it hardly mattered. Cleveland erased a 2-0 deficit in the first on a three-run shot from rookie Chase DeLauter and two-run homer by Angel Martinez. The A’s got one back in the third, only to see another five-spot from the Guardians on poor Jacob Lopez as David Fry, Austin Hedges, and Brayan Rocchio all delivered RBI doubles. Martinez later added a homer and an RBI single in a career-best four-hit day.
Chicago White Sox (79-76) 3, Detroit Tigers (73-82) 1
Cleveland’s win meant that Chicago was stuck at a game back in the AL Central in the best-case, but they did at least help push one of their Wild Card foes out of the picture with a win. Honestly, this was probably kind of a dud of a game for anyone who isn’t a White Sox fan, the lone highlights being Sean Burke’s six scoreless frames and Miguel Vargas’ sixth-inning solo shot to make it 3-1, Chicago (the other runs scored on an RBI single by Munetaka Murakami and a fifth-inning sac fly). Spencer Torkelson had a chance to tie the game with a homer following Hao-Yu Lee’s two-out single in the ninth, but he flew out to center to end it.
Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) 1, Baltimore Orioles (75-80) 0
Yeah, it’s time to stick a fork in the O’s. It was all but certain for awhile now, but Chicago’s win combined with Baltimore’s second-straight loss to Milwaukee means that the Orioles are four back with a week to play, plus multiple teams in front of them. Trevor Rogers was the hard-luck loser here while Baltimore got blanked on four hits and Rece Hinds lost a fly ball from Joey Ortiz in the sun, allowing him to triple and score on Gary Sánchez’s RBI grounder. Woof.
Texas Rangers (78-77) 6, Toronto Blue Jays (76-79) 1
The O’s aren’t the only bird that are all but shot down, either. Trade Deadline acquisition José Soriano coughed up an early homer to Josh Jung, beginning a five-inning, six-run outing that pushed Toronto three games out in the Wild Card and the Rangers into a one-game AL West lead over Houston. The only downside for Texas was that second-half surprise Cal Quantrill—who has a 1.75 ERA since re-entering the rotation in late July—left in the second with lat tightness, so old friend Jordan Montgomery picked up the slack in long relief, retiring 11 of the 12 hitters he faced with no hits allowed.
Atlanta Braves (91-64) 6, Houston Astros (77-78) 3
Houston and Texas have been wrestling all week over the prestigious “Who can win this horri-awful division with a .500-ish record” crown. Sunday it went to Texas with the Astros falling out of their tie for first place (remember that they own the tiebreaker). Isaac Paredes had put Houston ahead with a solo homer and an RBI knock in the third, but the Astros’ bullpen set that lead on fire. The big blow came off the bat of Ronald Acuña Jr., who belted a grand slam off Bryan Abreu in the seventh after AJ Blubaugh made a right mess of things.

item.title: [sportingnews.com] Kyle Schwarber and Colson Montgomery are in a race for MLB history no one wants to make | Sporting News
item.dc:creator: Matt Sullivan
item.description: There are plenty of records players are chasing to close out the 2026 MLB season. For the Philadelphia Phillies and Chicago White Sox, they have a pair of star sluggers seeking the same kind of history. Kyle Schwarber and Colson Montgomery, two of the game's best power-hitters, are in pursuit of the same MLB history. The only issue? This isn't the kind of history a player wants to set. Bob Nightengale of USA Today shared how Schwarber and Montgomery are both chasing the MLB single-season strikeo
item.content:encoded:
There are plenty of records players are chasing to close out the 2026 MLB season. For the Philadelphia Phillies and Chicago White Sox, they have a pair of star sluggers seeking the same kind of history.
Kyle Schwarber and Colson Montgomery, two of the game's best power-hitters, are in pursuit of the same MLB history. The only issue? This isn't the kind of history a player wants to set.
Bob Nightengale of USA Today shared how Schwarber and Montgomery are both chasing the MLB single-season strikeout record held by Mark Reynolds. Unfortunately, both have a real chance at making this MLB history.
Kyle Schwarber and Colson Montgomery are in pursuit of same dubious MLB history
"Phillies DH Kyle Schwarber and White Sox shortstop Colson Montgomery are on the verge of making dubious baseball history," Nightengale writes. "Schwarber and Montgomery each had 216 strikeouts entering Sunday, endangering Mark Reynolds' all-time record of 223 strikeouts in 2009."
Players are striking out more than ever, and for these two sluggers, strikeout history is very much in play.
Entering play on Sunday, September 20, both Montgomery and Schwarber have seven more games to go during the 2026 regular season.
They're each at 216 strikeouts, needing just seven to tie the all-time single-season record set by Reynolds.
Considering both will likely be starters for all of their remaining games amid a postseason push, this strikeout record is very possible.
With seven games to go, they need to average one strikeout per game to tie Reynolds' record. Of these two sluggers, Montgomery might have the slight advantage for the record.
In the last week, Montgomery has struck out 10 times, tied for the second-most in MLB during that span. Schwarber in that same span has struck out six times. If those paces held, Montgomery would reach 226 strikeouts, while Schwarber would reach 222.
The race for this MLB record is a fascinating one, although the players themselves probably don't want to actually break this dubious MLB record.

item.title: [sportingnews.com] Nolan Arenado refusing to land on IL for Diamondbacks was a good thing | Sporting News
item.dc:creator: Matt Sullivan
item.description: The Arizona Diamondbacks are 4.0 games back in the NL Wild Card race as the final week's worth of games are set to get underway. As Arizona's working their way back into contention, one of the most important contributors has been Nolan Arenado. But they almost didn't have him for this stretch of the year. According to USA Today's Bob Nightengale, Arenado could've landed on the injured list a few weeks ago, but refused the Diamondbacks' wish to place him on the IL. That refusal has borne fruit, a
item.content:encoded:
The Arizona Diamondbacks are 4.0 games back in the NL Wild Card race as the final week's worth of games are set to get underway.
As Arizona's working their way back into contention, one of the most important contributors has been Nolan Arenado. But they almost didn't have him for this stretch of the year.
According to USA Today's Bob Nightengale, Arenado could've landed on the injured list a few weeks ago, but refused the Diamondbacks' wish to place him on the IL. That refusal has borne fruit, as the future Hall of Famer has been incredible for the D-Backs lately.
Diamondbacks are fortunate Nolan Arenado refused placement on IL
"The Diamondbacks wanted to place Arenado on the IL a few weeks ago with a left intercostal injury and an inflamed thumb, but he refused, insisting he could play through the injuries in the pennant race," Nightengale writes.
Arenado has been a solid contributor for the Diamondbacks overall this season, and it would make sense for Arizona to protect the veteran third baseman if he wasn't 100%.
But Arenado didn't want to hit the injured list, refusing a potential placement on the IL. That refusal has been a major boost for Arizona.
Since the start of September, roughly around when the Diamondbacks would've asked Arenado to hit the IL, he's been one of the best hitters in MLB.
In 16 games and 56 at-bats, Arenado has 18 hits, seven runs scored, two doubles, five home runs, nine RBIs, seven walks, a .321 batting average, and a 1.031 OPS.
If it wasn't for Arenado playing at such a high level, the Diamondbacks might've been much farther back than four games, as they enter play on Sunday, September 20.
While the Diamondbacks' postseason future is still up in the air, Arenado's decision to refuse to hit the injured list has proven to be the right call so far.

item.content:encoded:
Sep 20, 2026, 12:36 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Kyle Tucker (knee) left Saturday night's game early against the division-rival San Francisco Giants after fouling a ball off his right knee/shin, but manager Dave Roberts told Jack Harris of The California Post that the lopsided score played into Tucker being removed early. Roberts expects Tucker to be back in action for Sunday's series finale at Dodger Stadium, but they will see how he feels in the morning. Before leaving the eventual 10-4 win on Saturday, Tucker went 1-for-3 at the plate with a walk and a run scored for the Dodgers. He was replaced in right field by Alex Call. The 29-year-old left-handed slugger has not lived up to his big free-agent contract in 2026 in his first year in L.A., as he is currently slashing .235/.334/.394 with a .729 OPS, 17 homers, 70 RBI, 88 runs, and 11 stolen bases across his 515 at-bats. However, after hitting under .200 in August, Tucker has picked things up and has hit .288 (17-for-59) with six homers, three doubles, a triple, 13 RBI, 17 runs scored, and two steals in 18 games in September. The Dodgers are hoping he can continue to swing a hot bat going into the playoffs in October.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The California Post - Jack Harris
More Recent News
Reds Place Chase Burns on Injured List With Groin Strain


Keith Hernandez




Sep 20, 2026, 12:30 PM ET
The Cincinnati Reds announced on Sunday that they placed right-hander Chase Burns (groin) on the 15-day injured list (retroactive to Sept. 19) with a strained right groin and selected the contract of right-hander Carson Spiers from Triple-A Louisville in a corresponding move. The Reds had been working to limit the young right-hander's innings in recent weeks, and now his 2026 season will come to an end with a week remaining on the schedule. The 23-year-old former second overall pick in 2024 from Wake Forest University had a fantastic first full season in the majors this year, earning his first All-Star nod while going 15-3 with a 2.86 ERA (3.24 FIP), 1.17 WHIP, and 185:56 K:BB in 154 1/3 innings pitched across his 29 starts for the Reds. Burns recorded a strong 29.4% strikeout rate while walking 8.9% of the batters he faced. He is one of the best upside arms in terms of strikeout stuff in the big leagues, as long as he can stay healthy going forward. The native of Italy was limited to exactly three innings in each of his final three starts in 2026, allowing four earned runs while walking six and striking out 14.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Cincinnati Reds
Willson Contreras Sitting Out Series Finale in Tampa


Keith Hernandez




Sep 20, 2026, 12:24 PM ET
Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras (hand) remains absent from the team's starting lineup for Sunday's series finale against the division-rival Tampa Bay Rays, per MLB.com. Nick Sogard is making a third straight start at first base for the BoSox and is hitting fifth against Rays right-hander Griffin Jax. Contreras is missing a third straight game after he was hit by a pitch on his right hand in Thursday's win over the Texas Rangers. The good news is that X-rays came back negative for any fractures in his hand, so fantasy managers should consider him day-to-day going into the final week of the 2026 regular season. With a scheduled day off coming on Monday, hopefully Contreras will be back on the field for Tuesday's series opener at Fenway Park against the Cleveland Guardians. The 34-year-old Venezuelan has a career-best 27 home runs and 81 RBI in 2026 in his first year in Boston, but he hit just .217 (18-for-83) with a .715 OPS in 23 games in August, and he has played in only four games so far in September due to various injuries.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Shohei Ohtani has "Good Chance" to Play Next Week


Keith Hernandez




Sep 20, 2026, 12:54 AM ET
There is a "good chance" that Los Angeles Dodgers two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps) will be activated from the 10-day injured list for the series against the division-rival San Diego Padres at home next week, manager Dave Roberts told Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic. Ohtani is eligible to come off the IL on Wednesday, so he could be back as the team's designated hitter for the second game of the series at Dodger Stadium. The four-time MVP apparently looked good after running the bases and taking simulated at-bats off a Trajekt machine before Saturday's game. There is still a little time for the 32-year-old Japanese native to help the Dodgers and fantasy managers in the final stretch of the 2026 regular season. However, the Dodgers probably are not going to rush him back, so it would not be a surprise to get a game or two off in the final four or five games of the year. Ohtani has hit .277/.380/.522 with a .902 OPS, 30 homers, 80 RBI, 89 runs scored, and 11 stolen bases in 502 at-bats. It has been a strong season, but nagging left-knee and right-biceps injuries since early July caught up with him, and he was placed on the IL after hitting an un-Ohtani-like .241/.322/.472 with a .795 OPS in 27 games in August.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Fabian Ardaya
Sep 20, 2026, 12:47 AM ET
WEEI's Rob Bradford reports that it is "sure looking like" Boston Red Sox left-hander Payton Tolle has a "good shot" at pitching Game 1 of a wild-card series to kick off the postseason with the way the Red Sox are lining things up. It means that the 23-year-old southpaw will not get a start this weekend against the division-rival Tampa Bay Rays. The former second-rounder from TCU in 2024 has had a strong first full season in the big leagues with Boston in 2026, going 9-6 with a 3.02 ERA (3.04 FIP) and 1.07 WHIP with 166 strikeouts and 38 walks in 143 innings across his 25 starts. Another lefty, Patrick Sandoval, is now scheduled to make the start for the BoSox in the series finale in Tampa. Tolle allowed four earned runs in 5 2/3 innings against the Seattle Mariners on Aug. 31, but he has only given up one earned run with one walk and 19 punchouts in 12 innings across his last two starts against the Baltimore Orioles and Kansas City Royals in September.--Keith Hernandez
Source: WEEI - Rob Bradford
Xavier Edwards Leaves Early on Saturday With Thumb Discomfort


Keith Hernandez




Sep 20, 2026, 12:31 AM ET
Miami Marlins infielder Xavier Edwards (thumb) left Saturday night's game at Petco Park against the San Diego Padres early with discomfort in his left thumb, according to Christina De Nicola. The Marlins' training staff was checking Edwards' left hand out when he fouled a ball off in the seventh frame. It is worth noting that Edwards previously missed time this season with a sprained left thumb, which he might have aggravated on Saturday night. Before leaving the ballgame, Edwards went 0-for-3 with a walk and two strikeouts. He was replaced at the keystone in San Diego by Jared Serna. If the 27-year-old switch-hitting middle infielder did aggravate his left-thumb sprain, there is a good chance that he will not play again for the Marlins in the final week of the 2026 season. Edwards came into Wednesday's contest with a nice .282/.361/.373 slash line with a .733 OPS, a career-high six home runs, a career-high 52 RBI, 61 runs scored, and 21 stolen bases in 141 games played. He has stolen 20-plus bases in each of the last three seasons, including a career-high 31 back in 2024.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Christina De Nicola
Aaron Judge Hopes to be Back for Postseason, No Timetable Given


Keith Hernandez




Sep 20, 2026, 12:23 AM ET
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge (calf) said on Saturday that his right-calf strain is in the soleus muscle, according to Bryan Hoch of MLB.com. However, Judge would not say what grade of strain his MRI exam revealed. "I'd like to be back by the postseason. That's definitely the plan. I got really no answers for you on any timeline or anything like that," Judge said. The New York Daily News' Gary Phillips reports that neither Judge nor manager Aaron Boone has shared much information on his injury, with the Yankees treating his calf strain like "classified CIA intel." "It doesn't matter what grade it is," Boone said. "We're at nine games left [in the season]." Because we have no idea of the exact severity of his calf injury, it is entirely plausible that Judge could miss most, or all, of any potential Yankees playoff run in October. Judge has been throwing, working out, and getting treatment, and he said he is "gonna do everything we can do to get back as soon as we can." Boone, though, merely said he is "hoping for the best." It will be difficult for the Yankees to go all the way if they do not get Judge back for the playoffs. It has been a frustrating year for the three-time MVP and all of his fantasy managers, as he has only played in 66 games due to a stress fracture in his rib, slashing .241/.360/.511 with 18 home runs, 41 RBI, 45 runs, and five steals.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Bryan Hoch
Roki Sasaki to Return Next Week


Andy Webb




Sep 19, 2026, 10:37 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki (finger) will make his return to the mound next week during the series against the San Diego Padres, David Vassegh reports. Sasaki looked good during his side session on Wednesday, so the Dodgers have cleared him to get back on the mound. It doesn't sound like the Dodgers have decided whether Sasaki will start or come out of the bullpen during his outing against the Padres. The right-hander has been out since late August due to a finger blister. The expectation is that Sasaki will likely pitch in a bullpen role for the team during the postseason.--Andy Webb
Source: David Vassegh
Trey Yesavage to Start on Monday


Andy Webb




Sep 19, 2026, 10:31 PM ET
Toronto Blue Jays starting pitcher Trey Yesavage (knee) is scheduled to start against the Baltimore Orioles on Monday, Arden Zwelling of Sportsnet.ca reports. Yesavage has been out since August after having surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his right knee. He only made one rehab appearance at Triple-A Buffalo before getting cleared to pitch for the big league club. The Jays plan to have Yesavage pitch roughly three innings or around 45 to 50 pitches. Spencer Miles is expected to take over for the bulk of the innings after Yesavage is done. It'll be interesting to see if the Jays decide to shut down Yesavage if they do get eliminated from playoff contention. Until then, it sounds like the right-hander is going to contribute here soon.--Andy Webb
Source: Arden Zwelling
Cal Quantrill Removed with Lat Tightness


Andy Webb




Sep 19, 2026, 10:22 PM ET
Texas Rangers starting pitcher Cal Quantrill (lat) exited early during Saturday's outing against the Toronto Blue Jays. Quantrill was pulled out in the second inning due to right lat tightness, Kennedi Landry of MLB.com reports. He was able to record four outs before exiting this contest. Jordan Montgomery took over on the mound and threw 3.2 scoreless innings. Quantrill figures to undergo an MRI, so fantasy managers will likely have to wait for the results on that. Nathan Eovaldi could be asked to move back into the starting rotation if Quantrill is forced to miss time. UPDATE: The Dallas Morning News' Shawn McFarland reports that Quantrill will undergo an MRI exam on Sunday morning, per manager Skip Schumaker.--Andy Webb
Source: Kennedi Landry
Sep 19, 2026, 10:15 PM ET
New York Yankees outfielder Spencer Jones (foot) was not in the starting lineup ahead of Saturday's game against the Arizona Diamondbacks. The Yankees decided to rest Jones on Saturday due to left foot/heel soreness, according to Brendan Kuty of The Athletic. It sounds like a day-to-day issue, so the Yankees are just going to play it safe. Jones is 1-for-19 with nine strikeouts over his last four games, so he could probably use a day off to rest and reset. Jose Caballero takes over in center field for Saturday's game. Fantasy managers should check back ahead of Sunday's game for another update on Jones.--Andy Webb
Source: Brendan Kuty
Shohei Ohtani Takes Simulated At-Bats


Andy Webb




Sep 19, 2026, 10:05 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps) has progressed to taking simulated at-bats off the team's pitching machine on Saturday, Jack Harris of the California Post reports. Ohtani was also able to run the bases as he works his way back from a biceps and knee issue. It's unclear if Ohtani will return when he's first eligible on Wednesday. The Dodgers have already clinched the postseason, so they don't exactly need to rush him back into the lineup. However, the Dodgers would probably like for Ohtani to play in a few regular-season games before the playoffs begin. Fantasy managers should check back for another update in a few days.--Andy Webb
Source: Jack Harris
Jac Caglianone Returning to Saturday's Lineup


Keith Hernandez




Sep 19, 2026, 5:54 PM ET
Kansas City Royals first baseman/outfielder Jac Caglianone (hand) is serving as the designated hitter and is batting third in Saturday's contest on the road against the Pittsburgh Pirates and right-hander Bubba Chandler, per MLB.com. Caglianone suffered a minor hand injury before Friday's series opener at PNC Park, but he is back in action on Saturday and should be returned to fantasy lineups against a right-hander, despite his cold streak of late. The 23-year-old former first-rounder has produced a .277/.328/.483 slash line with an .811 OPS, 23 home runs, 70 RBI, 66 runs scored, and six stolen bases in 484 at-bats in 2026 in his first full big-league season with the Royals. Cags was red-hot in August, slashing .411/.429/.684 with a 1.113 OPS, six home runs, eight doubles, 26 RBI, 17 runs scored, and three stolen bases in 24 games, but he has been banged up in September and has gone just 4-for-27 (.148) with zero homers, four RBI, one walk, and 11 strikeouts. He has never faced Chandler in the majors.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Sebastian Walcott to be Promoted to Triple-A


Keith Hernandez




Sep 19, 2026, 3:01 PM ET
Texas Rangers top infield prospect Sebastian Walcott is expected to be promoted to Triple-A Round Rock on Saturday, according to Kennedi Landry of MLB.com. Walcott will make his debut as the designated hitter on Saturday night. The No. 9 overall prospect in all of baseball, per MLB Pipeline, has only played in 39 games in the minors this year after having surgery on his UCL, but since returning, he has slashed .322/.398/.586 with nine home runs and 11 stolen bases in 37 games for Double-A Frisco. In a playoff series with the Rough Riders, Walcott went 4-for-11 with a homer and four stolen bases. Walcott is only 20 years old, but if he continues to ascend and looks good in spring training next year, he could push for an early-season MLB promotion for the Rangers. It is impossible to ignore his 40-homer upside at the shortstop position in fantasy baseball, which makes him a must-stash already in dynasty/keeper leagues.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Kennedi Landry
Orioles Shutting Ryan Helsley Down


Keith Hernandez




Sep 19, 2026, 1:40 PM ET
The Baltimore Orioles are shutting down right-handed reliever Ryan Helsley (elbow) for the rest of the season, general manager Mike Elias told Andy Kostka of The Baltimore Banner. The focus is on Helsley getting ready for next season. Elias said that Helsley is not dealing with a new injury, but the debate was over contracting his buildup timeline, and the O's opted against that. In related news, the Orioles reinstated right-handed reliever Felix Bautista (shoulder) from the 60-day injured list, and he will join the team's active roster for the first time since July of last year after he had surgery to fix a torn labrum and rotator cuff in his shoulder. Helsley's first year in Baltimore was a lost cause due to his elbow issues, as he was able to throw only 15 1/3 innings, going 0-4 with a 4.11 ERA, 1.43 WHIP, 21 strikeouts, and eight saves in 17 appearances. He will not be a lock to open the 2027 campaign as Baltimore's primary closer, especially with Bautista now back and healthy.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Baltimore Banner - Andy Kostka
Willson Contreras Still Out on Saturday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 19, 2026, 1:04 PM ET
Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras (hand) remains out of the team's starting lineup for Saturday's contest against the division-rival Tampa Bay Rays for the second straight day, per MLB.com. Nick Sogard will make another start at first base and will bat fifth against Rays right-hander Freddy Peralta. Contreras was diagnosed with a bruised right hand after leaving Thursday's game against the Texas Rangers after he was hit by a pitch. X-rays came back negative, though, so he is considered day-to-day and could make his return in Sunday's series finale in Tampa. Fantasy managers are hoping to get the 34-year-old Venezuelan back in their starting lineups as soon as possible, as the four-time All-Star has hit a career-high 27 home runs while driving in 81 runs in 129 games and 533 plate appearances in his first year with the club. Various injuries have limited Contreras to only four games so far in September, though, and he has gone 4-for-12 with a homer and two RBI.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Aroldis Chapman Won't Pitch This Weekend


Keith Hernandez




Sep 19, 2026, 11:07 AM ET
Boston Red Sox left-handed closer Aroldis Chapman (lat) felt some tightness in his lat while working out before Tuesday's game against the Texas Rangers and has not pitched since. Chapman said that he will not pitch this weekend against the division-rival Tampa Bay Rays, but he expects to return during the final homestand of the regular season, which starts on Tuesday, according to Ian Browne of MLB.com. The veteran southpaw downplayed the injury on Friday, saying that the Red Sox are being conservative and that he felt healthy enough to play catch before the series opener against the Rays, but the team told him not to. "I'm not worried at all," Chapman said. "From the first time I felt it to today, I feel very good. I was going to go out and throw, but the team wants to take it slow, and they want me to take my time." Fantasy managers will be without Chapman this weekend, but for championship matchups next week, he will hopefully be ready to return to ninth-inning duties. The 38-year-old has been excellent in 2026 in his second year in Boston, posting a 1.95 ERA with a 1.14 WHIP, 34 saves, and 68 strikeouts in 50 2/3 innings pitched. Right-hander Garrett Whitlock should handle a save situation this weekend if it arises in Tampa.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Ian Browne
Justin Verlander Throws Live Batting Practice


Dave Funnell




Sep 19, 2026, 10:03 AM ET
Detroit Tigers starting pitcher Justin Verlander (hamstring/hip) threw a one-inning, 20-pitch live batting practice session on Friday. The 43-year-old said that he felt great after this successful outing. This was yet another step in the right direction, as it was his first time throwing against live batters. What lies ahead in his progress remains to be seen, as the plan is for him to pitch one final time in his illustrious career on Saturday, September 26, against the Pittsburgh Pirates. Whether or not he is able to throw one inning or more remains questionable, but with him retiring after this season, chances are he will be healthy enough to make that appearance and cap off one of baseball's greatest careers. With 266 wins and 3,554 strikeouts over 21 seasons, the surefire Hall of Famer will be looking to finish his career where it started: in Detroit.--Dave Funnell - RotoBaller
Source: Chris McCosky
Trent Grisham Could Return This Season


Dave Funnell




Sep 19, 2026, 9:56 AM ET
New York Yankees outfielder Trent Grisham (hamstring) is pretty far into his recovery, two weeks after being placed on the 10-Day Injured List with a Grade 2 hamstring strain. Manager Aaron Boone reiterated that a return for him "could be in play" for the latter part of the season. It was also mentioned that when he does return, the Yankees would need to decide between him and Spencer Jones to play center field. This could complicate things for both players, as there could be some sort of platoon involving the two, diminishing their fantasy value down the stretch. Either way, the Yankees will be looking to solidify their lineup for the playoffs, and Grisham's fantasy value is very limited down the stretch, with or without a return before the playoffs.--Dave Funnell - RotoBaller
Source: Brendan Kuty - The Athletic
Tristan Peters Dealing With Multiple Injuries


Dave Funnell




Sep 19, 2026, 9:39 AM ET
Chicago White Sox outfielder Tristan Peters (rib/shoulder) crashed into the wall during Friday's game while trying to catch a fly ball in the outfield. He exited the game with contusions to both his ribs and shoulders, and Braden Montgomery took his place in the outfield. The good news is that he is listed as day-to-day and has no head injury, which was the initial concern at the time of impact. It's unclear if he will miss any time before returning, but with the White Sox in the middle of a divisional race, they may need his help sooner rather than later. The 26-year-old is hitting .272 on the season with 12 home runs and eight stolen bases, and is worth rostering in deep leagues.--Dave Funnell - RotoBaller
Source: Chicago White Sox
Justin Steele Completes Two-Inning Rehab Outing


Dave Funnell




Sep 19, 2026, 9:30 AM ET
Chicago Cubs pitcher Justin Steele (elbow) threw a 33-pitch, two-inning rehab outing on Friday for the Triple-A Iowa Cubs. This was his fifth appearance since beginning his rehab assignment and the fourth that has been two innings in length. Arguably his most impressive outing yet, Steele walked the first batter of the game before striking out the side. He would finish with five strikeouts in total while not allowing a hit. While the velocity on his fastball sat at 90.2 miles per hour, it was his slider that impressed the most, generating four whiffs. It's unclear what lies ahead for him, as the Cubs are in the middle of a race for the Wild Card. While they have a comfortable lead on the teams chasing them, they do need to prepare for the postseason, and Steele returning to the Cubs may not be in the cards. What's clear is that he is feeling much better than he has in quite some time, and any return to the Cubs would likely be for a peace-of-mind appearance to allow him to enter the postseason on a healthy note, giving him the opportunity to work on coming back even stronger next spring. Fantasy managers should not expect much from him down the stretch, but those in dynasty leagues should take note and add him while they can.--Dave Funnell - RotoBaller
Source: Jason Kempf

item.dc:creator: Ben Stinar

item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, the Houston Astros will look to avoid getting swept by the Atlanta Braves (at home).
They have dropped each of the first two games.
Most recently, the Astros lost by a score of 6-3 on Saturday.
Brian McTaggart of MLB.com wrote (on Saturday): “The Braves beat the Astros, 6-3. The Astros have lost 9 of 13 and have fallen under .500 (77-78). They are in second place for the first time since July 30 and trail the Rangers by one game with seven remaining. Home finale tomorrow.”
Jose Altuve (who started at second base) finished with three hits.
Houston Astros Announce Sudden Jose Altuve Change
For Sunday’s game, the Astros have announced their starting lineup.
Underdog MLB wrote: “Astros 9/20 J. Peña SS Y. Alvarez LF I. Paredes 3B J. Altuve DH Y. Diaz C C. Walker 1B C. Smith RF N. Allen 2B B. Matthews CF H. Brown SP”
Altuve (who is hitting 4th) has been moved to DH on Sunday.
The future Hall of Famer is currently batting .247 with 122 hits, 15 home runs, 44 RBIs, 66 runs and five stolen bases in 128 games.
He is in the middle of his 16th season (all with the Astros).
Social Media Reacts To Lineup On Sunday
Here’s what people are saying about the team’s lineup:
@PeytonR_25: “It’s a rough day to be an Astros fan. Astros lock in today please”
@DannyLoughery: “BRICE MATTHEWS WITH THE SEASON ON THE LINE THIS DUDE CANT BE FR🤣🤣🤣🤣”
@fredyus83: “Everybody except Joe loperfido🤬”
Looking At The Astros On Sunday
The Astros are the second-place team in the American League West with a 77-78 record in 155 games.
They have lost seven out of their last ten games (and are 39-41 in 80 games at home).
Following one more game with the Braves, the Astros will get the day off on Monday.
They will then head on the road for a series with the Seattle Mariners that starts on Tuesday night in Washington.

item.title: [heavy.com] Atlanta Braves Announce Sudden Austin Riley Decision During Astros Series
item.dc:creator: Cole Sullivan
item.description: The Atlanta Braves secured victories in each of their first two games against the Houston Astros this weekend. Now, on Sunday, they can go for the sweep while also clinching the NL East with a victory. Ahead of Sunday’s matchup, Braves manager Walt Weiss made some sudden changes to his starting lineup, including one involving veteran infielder Austin Riley. Braves Announce Riley Decision Riley has been an everyday player throughout the season, and he’s started nearly every game for Atlanta in Se
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves secured victories in each of their first two games against the Houston Astros this weekend.
Now, on Sunday, they can go for the sweep while also clinching the NL East with a victory.
Ahead of Sunday’s matchup, Braves manager Walt Weiss made some sudden changes to his starting lineup, including one involving veteran infielder Austin Riley.
Braves Announce Riley Decision
Riley has been an everyday player throughout the season, and he’s started nearly every game for Atlanta in September so far.
However, Weiss has decided to keep him out of the starting lineup for Sunday’s matchup and instead put Mauricio Dubon at third base.
Here’s the full Braves lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Braves 9/20 D. Baldwin C R. Acuña Jr. DH M. Olson 1B M. Harris II CF M. Dubón 3B O. Albies 2B M. Yastrzemski LF B. Hicklen RF H. Kim SS M. Pérez SP.”
Braves 9/20
D. Baldwin C
R. Acuña Jr. DH
M. Olson 1B
M. Harris II CF
M. Dubón 3B
O. Albies 2B
M. Yastrzemski LF
B. Hicklen RF
H. Kim SS
M. Pérez SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 20, 2026
Looking at Riley’s 2026 Season
Riley is 6-for-32 over his last nine games and hasn’t matched his usual production at the plate this season.
He’s appeared in 153 games and is on pace to set career lows in batting average (.220), slugging percentage (.360), and OPS (.652).
Despite those numbers, Riley has still produced at the plate, recording 62 runs, 120 hits, 17 home runs, and 69 RBIs across 545 at-bats.
Braves Right Now
Atlanta enters Sunday with a 91-64 overall record and has gone 6-4 in its last 10 games.
They hold the No. 3 seed in the National League, trailing the Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers.
If the standings hold, they’d be in line to host a best-of-three Wild Card series during the first week after the regular season ends, and as of right now, it would be against the Philadelphia Phillies.

item.title: [timesofindia.indiatimes.com] Inspiring story of the day: José Ramírez grew up playing with a glove that was too small and was ignored by MLB scouts; years later he reached 1,000 career RBIs
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk
item.description: Some baseball dreams begin with the finest equipment, elite coaching and scouts waiting to spot the next big star. José Ramírez's journey began very differently. The Cleveland Guardians star grew up with limited resources, faced doubts about his potential and had to fight for recognition. Years later, he reached 1,000 career RBIs, turning an overlooked beginning into a remarkable MLB story. José Ramírez's humble beginnings in the Dominican Republic Long before thousands of fans cheered his name
item.content:encoded:
Some baseball dreams begin with the finest equipment, elite coaching and scouts waiting to spot the next big star. José Ramírez's journey began very differently. The Cleveland Guardians star grew up with limited resources, faced doubts about his potential and had to fight for recognition. Years later, he reached 1,000 career RBIs, turning an overlooked beginning into a remarkable MLB story.
José Ramírez's humble beginnings in the Dominican Republic
Long before thousands of fans cheered his name at Progressive Field, Ramírez was a young boy in Baní, a city in the Dominican Republic, trying to make the most of whatever baseball equipment he could find.
His family faced financial struggles, and even getting a proper glove was difficult. In a 2023 MLB feature, Ramírez recalled the challenges his family faced while he was growing up.
“It was difficult for my dad,” he said through interpreter Agustin Rivero. “He didn’t have much work, we didn’t have much money. I had to play with a glove that was too tight.”
That small detail offers a glimpse into the reality of Ramírez's early life. For him, baseball was never simply a game played for fun. It represented a chance to change his family's circumstances and build a future beyond the financial limits he knew as a child.
Before he began playing organised baseball, Ramírez and other neighbourhood children played Vitilla, a popular Dominican street game. They used plastic water jug caps as balls and sticks as bats. The makeshift equipment could not match what elite prospects used, but the children made the most of what they had.
Ramírez also faced a challenge that had nothing to do with money. His small frame made him easy to overlook in a sport where scouts often search for size, strength and physical potential.
Yet, the young infielder kept showing up and competing. His story was taking shape long before a Major League Baseball team gave him a chance.
MLB scouts overlooked José Ramírez despite his talent
Ramírez's road to professional baseball was anything but straightforward. While other young players attracted attention at showcases in the Dominican Republic, he often found himself waiting on the sidelines.
By the time he was 17, his chances of securing a professional contract appeared to be slipping away. Many of the top Dominican prospects signed with MLB teams at 16, leaving Ramírez behind as scouts focused on younger players with more conventional physical profiles.
He was frequently used as a fill-in at showcases rather than receiving the same opportunities as the headline prospects. His lack of size and limited scouting attention made it harder for him to stand out, even when his performance suggested he deserved a closer look.
Ramírez later described the doubts he faced in an ESPN interview, recalling how people judged him before he had the chance to prove himself.
“I knew it would be hard for me [to get signed] because [scouts] are always looking for a Mike Trout, a Bryce Harper. Those kind of guys; big, strong guys. I imagine that [José] Altuve had the same thing happen to him. I guess nobody believed Altuve could be what he has become. Sometimes your size, a smaller body, one does not attract attention or anything and nobody believes in you,” he said.
The lack of interest could have ended his dream before it truly began. Instead, Ramírez continued to play, trusting his ability even when the people evaluating him did not share that confidence.
His opportunity finally arrived in 2009. During a showcase, Cleveland's scouting director John Mirabelli and scout Ramón Peña watched him play second base. Ramírez delivered three hits that day, followed by three more the next day and five hits during a doubleheader.
Peña pushed for Cleveland to sign him. The Guardians' organisation, then known as the Indians, eventually offered Ramírez a $50,000 signing bonus.
It was a modest investment compared with the money given to highly sought-after international prospects. But that decision would become one of the most significant signings in the franchise's history.
José Ramírez turned a modest signing into an MLB career
Even after signing with Cleveland, Ramírez had no guarantee of becoming a major league star. His small signing bonus did not bring the same expectations or opportunities that came with a lucrative prospect contract.
He had to earn his place at every level, moving through the Dominican Summer League, the Arizona Rookie League and several other Minor League stops. There were no shortcuts. Each promotion required him to prove that his performance could translate against stronger competition.
Cleveland's front office later acknowledged that Ramírez did not arrive with the attention usually reserved for elite prospects. His progress came through steady work rather than early hype.
That gradual rise makes his career particularly striking. Ramírez developed into one of baseball's most consistent hitters, combining contact skills, speed, power and versatility. He also became a switch-hitter capable of putting pressure on opposing pitchers from either side of the plate.
His success challenged the assumptions that had limited his opportunities as a teenager. The traits that once made him easy to overlook did not prevent him from becoming a central figure in Cleveland's lineup.
Over time, Ramírez became far more than a promising player who exceeded expectations. He established himself as a franchise cornerstone, a perennial offensive threat and a player whose contributions extended well beyond individual statistics.
The journey also reflects the importance of the people who believed in him early. Peña continued to advocate for Ramírez when others saw little reason to invest in him. That faith gave the young Dominican infielder an opening, but Ramírez still had to turn it into a career.
José Ramírez reaches 1,000 career RBIs with the Guardians
On September 18, 2026, Ramírez added another defining moment to his career. The Guardians star crushed a solo home run against the Athletics at Progressive Field, recording his 1,000th career RBI during Cleveland's 5-3 victory.
The milestone came in the sixth inning, with his 401-foot blast giving the home crowd another reason to celebrate a player who had spent years earning their admiration.
Ramírez became just the second player in Cleveland franchise history to reach 1,000 RBIs, joining Earl Averill. He also became the 12th active MLB player to reach the mark.
For a player who once struggled to attract the attention of scouts, the achievement carries a special meaning. It reflects years of consistency, development and the ability to deliver when his team needs him.
Guardians manager Stephen Vogt captured the scale of the accomplishment by putting it in perspective.
“I like to use those round numbers,” Vogt said. “[It’s] 10 years of 100 RBIs. When you break it down that way, it's incredible what he has accomplished, and he's not even close to being done, right?”
Ramírez, however, remained focused on the team's success rather than his personal achievement.
“Thank God for the opportunity to play here for this organization and be able to achieve [1,000 RBIs],” Ramírez said through team interpreter Agustin Rivero. “But most important is that we're able to win today, because you guys know what I really want to do here, which is win.”
That mindset helps explain why Ramírez's story resonates beyond the milestone itself. His journey is about more than proving scouts wrong. It is about turning a difficult start into a career built on persistence, consistency and loyalty to the game.
From a young boy playing with an ill-fitting glove in Baní to one of Cleveland's most accomplished hitters, José Ramírez has shown that a player's beginning does not have to define his ceiling. His 1,000th RBI is another chapter in a story that is still being written.
Reporting note: The career milestone and game details are based on MLB's September 19, 2026, report. The early-life details are drawn from MLB's 2023 profile and ESPN's reporting on Ramírez's rise.

item.title: [스포츠조선] 김하성, 결국 '벤치맨'으로 가을 맞나…PS 확정 뒤에도 개점휴업, 애틀랜타의 셈법은

item.description: [스포츠조선 박상경 기자] 애틀랜타 브레이브스가 포스트시즌 진출을 확정지은 가운데 김하성을 어떻게 활용할지에 관심이 쏠린다. 김하성은 지난달 두 번째 부상자 명단(IL) 복귀 후 로스터 한 자리를 지키고 있다. 하지만 주전 자리는 마우리시오 두반이 맡고 있다. 9월 들어 중요한 순간마다 방망이가 터지면서 전반기 극심한 부진에서 벗어나는 듯 했지만, 여전히 '주전'이라는 수식어와는 연결되지 않고 있다. 애틀랜타가 앞서 두반과 함께 활용했던 호르헤 마테오, 짐 자비스 대신 김하성을 택한 배경으로 '수비'가 거론됐다. 내외야 유틸리티인 두반이 올 시즌 공수에서 중요한 활약을 펼쳐준 건 사실이지만, 전문 유격수가 아니라는 불안감이 존재한다. 정규시즌과 무게감이 다른 포스트시즌에서 한 경기 실수가 승부를 좌우할 수 있다는 점에서 수비의 중요성은 더욱 커진다. 샌디에이고 시절인 2022년 포스트시즌 12경기를 소화했고, 이듬해 내셔널리그 유틸리티 부문 골드글러브로 수비력을 인정받았던 김하성의
item.content:encoded:
[스포츠조선 박상경 기자] 애틀랜타 브레이브스가 포스트시즌 진출을 확정지은 가운데 김하성을 어떻게 활용할지에 관심이 쏠린다.
김하성은 지난달 두 번째 부상자 명단(IL) 복귀 후 로스터 한 자리를 지키고 있다. 하지만 주전 자리는 마우리시오 두반이 맡고 있다. 9월 들어 중요한 순간마다 방망이가 터지면서 전반기 극심한 부진에서 벗어나는 듯 했지만, 여전히 '주전'이라는 수식어와는 연결되지 않고 있다.
애틀랜타가 앞서 두반과 함께 활용했던 호르헤 마테오, 짐 자비스 대신 김하성을 택한 배경으로 '수비'가 거론됐다. 내외야 유틸리티인 두반이 올 시즌 공수에서 중요한 활약을 펼쳐준 건 사실이지만, 전문 유격수가 아니라는 불안감이 존재한다. 정규시즌과 무게감이 다른 포스트시즌에서 한 경기 실수가 승부를 좌우할 수 있다는 점에서 수비의 중요성은 더욱 커진다. 샌디에이고 시절인 2022년 포스트시즌 12경기를 소화했고, 이듬해 내셔널리그 유틸리티 부문 골드글러브로 수비력을 인정받았던 김하성의 경험에 기대를 거는 눈치다.
이럼에도 김하성에게 꾸준한 기회가 주어지지 못하는 건 두반의 활약도 있지만, 전반적인 타격 지표 자체가 좋지 못하기 때문으로 풀이된다. 김하성의 8월 복귀 후 타율은 0.220(41타수 9안타), 홈런 없이 6타점이다. 다저스를 상대로 끝내기 안타를 기록하는 등 인상적인 장면을 만들어내기도 했다. 출루율도 0.304로 이전보다 향상됐다. 그러나 장타율이 0.244에 머물고 있고, OPS(출루율+장타율)도 0.548로 무게감이 떨어지는 게 사실이다.
와이스 감독은 포스트시즌 확정 후에도 선발 유격수로 두반을 기용하고 있다. 김하성은 17일(이하 한국시각) 시카고 컵스전 이후 벤치를 지키다 21일 휴스턴 애스트로스전에 선발 라인업에 복귀했다. 두반은 이날 3루수를 맡았다.
MLB닷컴은 레인 토머스가 IL에 오른 뒤 김하성과 두반의 공존 가능성을 제기한 바 있다. 두반이 좌익수 자리를 맡을 때 김하성이 유격수로 뛰는 것이다. 지난 15일 컵스전에서 와이스 감독이 이런 기용법을 활용한 바 있다. 휴스턴전에서는 기존 3루수 오스틴 라일리를 쉬게 하면서 두반을 이동시키고, 빈 유격수 자리에 김하성을 넣었다. 결국 두반의 기용법에 따라 김하성의 기용 여부도 갈리는 흐름이다.
현시점에서는 김하성이 포스트시즌 엔트리에 합류하더라도 기본적으로는 벤치에서 출발할 가능성이 높아 보인다. 다만 좌완 선발을 만날 경우 두반이 좌익수로 이동하고 김하성이 유격수로 선발 출전하는 선택지도 있다. 결국 제한된 기회에서 얼마나 자신의 장점을 보여주느냐가 관건이다. 변수가 많은 가을야구에서 기회가 언제 찾아올지는 알 수 없다. 김하성에게는 주어진 순간을 잡는 승부사 기질이 필요하다.
박상경 기자 ppark@sportschosun.com

item.title: [Yardbarker] Boston Red Sox Announce Jarren Duran Move on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Simeon Kotto
item.description: The Boston Red Sox and Tampa Bay Rays head into Sunday’s series finale at Fenway Park with the three-game set knotted at one win apiece after Saturday’s 2-1 Rays victory. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox and Tampa Bay Rays head into Sunday’s series finale at Fenway Park with the three-game set knotted at one win apiece after Saturday’s 2-1 Rays victory.
Left-hander Patrick Sandoval takes the mound for Boston against Tampa Bay right-hander Griffin Jax, a matchup that carries extra weight with the regular season winding down and playoff positioning still in flux.
Interim manager Chad Tracy has kept the bulk of his starting nine intact, but he has made a modest yet noticeable adjustment involving outfielder Jarren Duran, via Underdog MLB.
After sitting out the series opener and batting eighth on Saturday, Duran will slide up one spot into the seventh hole. He will hit in front of Isaiah Kiner-Falefa and Nate Eaton while remaining in center field, the position he has occupied since injuries to Ceddanne Rafaela and Eli White opened the job.
The rest of the order features Roman Anthony in left, Mickey Gasper at designated hitter, Adley Rutschman behind the plate, Trevor Story at shortstop, Nick Sogard at first, and Cooper Durbin at third.
The move comes during a difficult individual season for Duran. Entering Sunday he is hitting .206 in 144 games, with 65 runs, 110 hits, 20 home runs and 69 RBIs. His slugging percentage sits at .364 and his OPS at .626.
Speculation about a possible trade lingered for weeks before the August 4 deadline, yet Duran remained in a Red Sox uniform and has continued to receive regular playing time as the club pushes toward October.
Boston sits at 84-71 with seven games left and occupies what currently looks like the second American League Wild Card spot. Should the standings hold, the Red Sox would open the postseason on the road in a best-of-three Wild Card series against the New York Yankees.
Every remaining game, including Sunday’s finale against a familiar division rival, therefore carries playoff implications.
Tracy’s decision to bump Duran up in the order is a small tactical shift rather than a wholesale overhaul, but it signals a willingness to tinker as the club tries to generate more consistent offense down the stretch.
Whether the extra spot in the lineup produces results remains to be seen.
Duran’s season-long struggles have been well documented, yet he has shown flashes of the power and speed that once made him a fixture in the middle of Boston’s order.
A productive afternoon against Jax and the Rays would give the Red Sox a series victory and a bit of momentum heading into the final week.
With the calendar now late September and the postseason picture still taking shape, even incremental lineup changes can feel significant.

item.content:encoded:
Ethan Salas became the youngest MLB player with a walk-off hit since current Padres teammate Manny Machado in 2012.
Ethan Salas has only been in the majors for a few weeks, but he's already joining some impressive company.
In the process, the 20-year-old became the youngest MLB player with a walk-off hit since one of his current teammates, Manny Machado, accomplished the feat on Sept. 13, 2012.
"It's different, man," Salas told MLB.com. "You got 50,000 going ballistic for you and the boys ready for you if everything works out."
The moment continued a remarkable stretch for Salas, who was called up for the first time in early September.
His major-league career began quietly. Salas went hitless in his first 15 at-bats before tripling for his first MLB hit against San Francisco on Sept. 13.
Three days later, Salas' bat erupted.
He hit the first two home runs of his major-league career in a 9-3 victory over the Colorado Rockies. At 20 years and 107 days old, Salas became the youngest catcher in MLB history to hit two home runs in one game.
Saturday brought another milestone.
Manager Craig Stammen sent Salas to the plate as a pinch hitter with Cronenworth at third base and one out in the bottom of the 10th. Salas fell behind in the count before delivering the game-winning single.
"Good at-bat for him, fouled off a pitch, line drive right up the middle," Stammen told MLB.com. "That's what that kid can do."
The hit mattered well beyond Salas' place in the record book.
San Diego earned its 12th victory in 13 games and moved into sole possession of the second National League Wild Card spot. The Padres improved to 86-69 and moved another step closer to securing a postseason berth.
It has been a rapid progression for a player who didn't collect his first major-league hit until a week ago.
First came the triple. Then came the historic two-homer performance. Now Salas has his first walk-off hit and another connection to Machado in the MLB record book.
"Living the dream, man," Salas told MLB.com.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Pirates' Oneil Cruz Made Incredible Adjustment This Season
item.dc:creator: Ethan Merrill; Unknown

item.content:encoded:
PITTSBURGH — The scouting report on Pittsburgh Pirates star Oneil Cruz for years was simple. The light-tower power was undeniable. The speed was game-changing.
But the swing path, timing and entire approach against left-handed pitching were a glaring flaw that threatened to cap his ceiling and stop him from reaching his potential.
Cruz has shown he can have success against southpaws and he's been the best Pirates hitter against them this season.
It's a massive improvement and one that is quite shocking, given where Cruz was at last season.
Cruz's Struggles Against LHP in 2025
In 2025, left-handers exposed that flaw at a historic rate. Cruz hit .102 against southpaws, with just 11 hits in 108 at-bats, a .224 on-base percentage, and a .176 slugging percentage. He struck out 44 times in 125 plate appearances.
That performance wasn’t just bad for a player of his talent; it was among the worst platoon splits in baseball. For context, the league average against left-handed pitching hovered around .242, making Cruz’s production roughly 58 percent below the average major leaguer.
The Pirates essentially stopped playing Cruz against lefties last season, as he was absent for the final 12 times the club faced a southpaw.
It was a stark acknowledgment that the 6-foot-7 outfielder, once their most tantalizing young talent, had become a platoon liability.
A Breakthrough in 2026
Cruz entered the offseason with a specific goal: fix the hole. He hired a left-handed throwing batting-practice pitcher to simulate the look he consistently failed to solve during games. It was a deliberate, targeted approach to the most glaring weakness in his offensive profile.
The results in 2026 were transformative, as Cruz is hitting .322 against left-handed pitching this season, with an on-base percentage north of .400.
He’s walking more, striking out less, and controlling the strike zone in ways that were previously unthinkable.
The strikeout rate against lefties has dropped to around 35 percent—still high, but nearly identical to his strikeout rate against right-handers, meaning pitchers no longer have a clear platoon advantage to exploit.
The power hasn’t necessarily shown up in home run totals against lefties. Cruz has just one home run against southpaws this season, a figure that might raise eyebrows for a player known for tape-measure shots.
But that’s not the point. The goal wasn’t to hit for more power against lefties; it was to hit, period. And he’s doing that.
Against right-handers, the power remains exactly what it always was. Cruz has 18 home runs against right-handed pitching, and the exit velocities, towering drives, raw force that made him a highlight-reel staple—none of that has gone anywhere.
The difference is that teams can no longer neutralize him by bringing in a left-hander out of the bullpen. He’s no longer a candidate to be pinch-hit for. He’s no longer a hole in the lineup.
Oneil Cruz and His Pirates' Future
Cruz is under contract through 2026 at $3.3 million, and he’ll be eligible for free agency in 2029.
When that day comes, he’ll be a 30-year-old center fielder with elite athleticism and a track record of prodigious power.
The question teams will ask is whether he’s a complete hitter or a platoon player. For years, the answer was clearly the latter. Now, that answer is changing.
If Cruz continues to hit lefties at even a league-average rate, he’s no longer a liability in any matchup.
He’s unquestionably an everyday player. That distinction matters enormously in free agency. A platoon outfielder with power but a fatal flaw against same-side pitching gets a modest multi-year deal, maybe $40-50 million.
An everyday center fielder who can hit for power, get on base, and run the bases gets a contract that probably has a floor of $100 million.
Cruz hasn’t simply improved a statistic. He’s potentially eliminated the single biggest barrier between him and a massive payday.
The power was always there. The speed was always there. The defense in center field has developed. The only missing piece was the ability to hit left-handed pitching, and that piece is no longer missing.
For the Pirates, that development is a gift. For Cruz, it’s a career-altering adjustment. And for the rest of baseball, it’s a warning: the light-tower power no longer comes with an off switch.
Ethan Merrill is from Grand Rapids, MI, and brings with him a diverse background of experiences. After graduating from Michigan State University with a degree in journalism, he worked with the Arizona Diamondbacks for three seasons before settling in the Pittsburgh area in 2020. With a passion for sports and a growing connection to his community, Ethan brings a fresh perspective to covering the Pittsburgh Pirates.

item.title: [North Side Baseball] Dansby Swanson is Back, and the Numbers Show How Much Cubs Missed Him
item.dc:creator: Matt Ostrowski
item.description: Cubs Video Just in time for a potential postseason run, Dansby Swanson is back. The Cubs’ starting shortstop and defensive stalwart returned to the lineup on Friday in Cincinnati after missing roughly one month with an oblique injury. The Cubs should be incredibly grateful he made a return so quickly. item.content:encoded:
Cubs Video
Just in time for a potential postseason run, Dansby Swanson is back. The Cubs’ starting shortstop and defensive stalwart returned to the lineup on Friday in Cincinnati after missing roughly one month with an oblique injury. The Cubs should be incredibly grateful he made a return so quickly. When he went down with his injury, our own Matthew Trueblood wrote that “although Swanson has been his inconsistent self at the plate this year, his value as a defender at shortstop is virtually unparalleled.” It wasn't hard to see that value (or, rather, the lack thereof) during his absence.
Exactly how much did his one month on the injured list end up hurting the North Siders? We can reach a rough approximation of this using the Fielding Run Value stat at Baseball Savant. In the 125 games that they played prior to Swanson’s injury, the Cubs led all of baseball in this statistic, having saved 61 runs above average. That was a whopping 23 runs more than the second-place Cardinals.
In their 27 games without him, they saved seven runs above average, just eighth-best in baseball. They went from saving almost half of a run per game (above average) to about a quarter of a run. That feels like a significant drop.
Defense, much like baseball as a whole, is very much a team endeavor, even though it's often perceived as individual effort. Shortstop is certainly one of the most important defensive positions out there, though there are still eight other guys that all have a job to do. Is it fair to pin this entire defensive drop off on the absence of Swanson?
| Position | FRV/game with Swanson | FRV/game without Swanson |
| C | 0 | -0.04 |
| 1B | 0.02 | -0.04 |
| 2B | 0.06 | 0 |
| SS | 0.09 | 0.07 |
| 3B | 0.03 | 0.04 |
| LF | 0.02 | 0.15 |
| CF | 0.21 | 0.15 |
| RF | 0.06 | 0 |
The void that Swanson leaves at shortstop isn’t felt quite as acutely as the downstream effects are. The Cubs were fifth in FRV from their shortstops prior to Swanson going down, and in the month since, they only dropped to eighth. It’s the slide of Nico Hoerner from second base to short that really hurts. Pedro Ramírez has had a fine rookie season, and he filled in admirably in Hoerner’s stead, but the Cubs went from eighth in FRV at second base when Hoerner was the primary player at the keystone, all the way down to 18th with Ramírez as the primary guy.
One way we can attempt to further isolate this is by seeing how often the Cubs defense turned groundballs into outs. According to FanGraphs, the Cubs allowed a .219 batting average on groundballs with Swanson in the fold, and that jumped to .229 in the month that he was on the injured list. That doesn't capture the value that also leaked away due to more errors (Hoerner committed three while playing shortstop; Swanson has only committed seven in about five times the playing time) or due to double plays not being turned, but it gives us some inkling.
Defense is really hard to measure, especially in such small sample sizes, but I come away from this with two takeaways:
- The Cubs should be very grateful to have Nico Hoerner. He accepted his shift to second base four years ago without blinking. The shift from the left side of the infield to the right side is something we’ve seen lesser shortstops create drama over. Not this one, and as a result, the Cubs have essentially a shortstop at each middle infield position. When one goes down, the other can move over.
- The Cubs should also be extremely glad to have Dansby Swanson back. There was a noticeable decline in how this group graded out without their shortstop. It might feel marginal, and it is. However, playoff games are won on the margins.
Their pitching depth is still in doubt, and they might yet have to play the Wild Card Series on the road. Positionally, though, the Cubs are back to full strength, and the difference between being without Swanson and having him back can't be overstated.

item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, the Toronto Blue Jays will finish their series with the Rangers in Texas.
The Blue Jays have lost each of the first two games in the series, so they will look to avoid getting swept.
George Springer has two strikeouts and no hits in the series.
Keegan Matheson of MLB.com wrote: “#BlueJays lose and fall to 76-79. Cleveland won. Chicago won. They essentially need to make up four games with only seven games remaining. It would take a miracle.”
Struggling Blue Jays Player Making $23 Million
With the season nearly over, it’s worth noting that Springer is making a lot of money.
He is being paid $22.5 million for the 2026 season.
Right now, Springer is batting just .249 with 111 hits, 15 home runs, 53 RBIs, 57 runs and 12 stolen bases in 121 games.
The four-time MLB All-Star will be a free agent this winter.
X user @mdpsnjournal wrote (on Saturday): “Twice George Springer has come up to bat with a pair of runners on the bags and twice he’s headed to the dugout empty handed. Just can’t win much when your big names are unable to hit in the clutch.”
Looking At Springer
Springer is in the middle of his 6th season with the Blue Jays.
Last year, he helped the franchise reach the World Series for the first time since the 1993 season.
The 37-year-old had a very strong 2025 season where he batted .309 with 32 home runs in 140 games.
Springer had spent the first seven years of his career with the Houston Astros.
He helped the franchise win the 2017 World Series title.
It will be interesting to see where Springer ends up for the 2027 MLB season.
Looking At The Jays Right Now
The Blue Jays are the fourth-place team in the American League East with a 76-79 record in 155 games.
They have lost six out of their last ten games.

item.title: [The Times of India] Francisco Lindor vs Manny Machado net worth comparison in 2026: MLB contracts, career earnings, salaries, endorsements, investments, real estate and lifestyle compared
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk
item.description: Francisco Lindor and Manny Machado continue to be two of the highest-paid infielders in Major League Baseball, both signed to nine-figure, long-term contracts. item.content:encoded:
Francisco Lindor and Manny Machado continue to be two of the highest-paid infielders in Major League Baseball, both signed to nine-figure, long-term contracts. Lindor’s deal with the New York Mets extends through 2031, while Machado’s extension with the San Diego Padres extends through 2033.
The financial comparison is more than headline contract values. Their net worth includes their 2026 salary and all career earnings in MLB, as well as endorsements, investments and real estate holdings. However, specific personal net worth figures are not publicly available and are subject to estimation, not official disclosure.
Francisco Lindor and Manny Machado net worth comparison in 2026
Francisco Lindor and Manny Machado are also in the same ballpark of wealth, according to public estimates, in 2026. Lindor’s deal with the Mets has greatly boosted his wealth, while Machado has built up big earnings thanks to his contracts with the Padres and his previous MLB deals.
Celebrity Net Worth reports that Lindor’s current deal is for $341 million over 10 years, and it keeps him signed through the 2031 season. The deal Machado signed is bigger in total value at $350 million over 11 years and runs through 2033, according to Celebrity Net Worth.
| Financial category | Francisco Lindor | Manny Machado |
| Estimated net worth | $75M–$100M | $75M–$100M |
| Current MLB team | New York Mets | San Diego Padres |
| Current contract | 10 years, $341M | 11 years, $350M |
| Contract through | 2031 | 2033 |
| 2026 total salary/payroll figure | $32.48M | $25.09M |
| Average annual value | $34.1M | $31.82M |
Lindor’s financial foundation is a 10-year, $341 million deal with the Mets. Celebrity Net Worth said the deal averages $34.1 million a year and was designed to keep the All-Star shortstop in New York through the 2031 season.
According to Celebrity Net Worth, Lindor is ranked as one of the highest-paid players in Major League Baseball in 2026 with a total compensation of approximately $32.48 million. Career earnings projections have also climbed above $200 million, a nod to his time with Cleveland and New York.
Manny Machado wealth profile with San Diego Padres
Machado’s wealth comes from an elite MLB career and successive blockbuster contracts. Per Celebrity Net Worth, the Padres finalised his 11-year, $350 million extension in February 2023, keeping him in San Diego through the 2033 season.
The average annual value of the contract is approximately $31.82 million. His reported 2026 salary is about $25.09 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth. But the contract structure boosts his salary in later seasons, with Baseball-Reference listing an average of $39.1 million per year from 2027 to 2033.
Machado’s financial portfolio is not just his playing salary. His long career in the MLB, along with endorsements and property holdings, has helped establish other sources of wealth, although specific private investments and asset values are not fully disclosed.
Lindor and Machado contract earnings compared in 2026
The headline numbers give you a sense of how close the two financial profiles are, but they also reveal an important difference in the structure of the contract. Machado has the larger overall commitment at $350 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth, but Lindor has the larger average annual value at $34.1 million.
Lindor is also making more in 2026 than Machado is reportedly making. Celebrity Net Worth has Lindor’s AP-derived salary data at about $32.48 million for the season and Machado’s at $25.09 million.
| Contract and earnings category | Francisco Lindor | Manny Machado |
| Total current contract | $341M | $350M |
| Contract length | 10 years | 11 years |
| Average annual value | $34.1M | $31.82M |
| 2026 compensation | $32.48M | $25.09M |
| Contract expiration | 2031 | 2033 |
| Major MLB position | Shortstop | Third baseman |
That means the two are still among the highest-paid players in baseball. Lindor’s deal has the higher average salary, while Machado’s contract has the higher guaranteed amount and that extra year of contractual security. Their future net worths will also depend on taxes, spending, investment performance, endorsements and the value of assets accumulated from their careers.

item.content:encoded:
Wyatt Langford News: On base three times in win
Langford went 1-for-2 with two walks, an RBI, a stolen base and two runs scored in Saturday's 6-2 win over Toronto.
Langford has been an on-base machine for Texas over the last week, reaching base safely in all five plate appearances Friday. He's drawn walks and scored runs in four consecutive games. Over the last eight contests, Langford is 7-for-25 with eight walks (.455 OBP), two steals, two doubles, one home run, four RBI and seven runs scored.

item.title: [chicagotribune.com] Column: It’s only fitting the tumultuous Cubs and White Sox seasons are coming down to the final week
item.dc:creator: Paul Sullivan
item.description: What a wild week in Chicago this was. “You’re shaking your head in amazement sometimes,” Chicago Cubs manager Craig Counsell said earlier this week. “You spend your whole life in baseball and you just don’t see this happen on a baseball field.” Counsell was referring to Pete Crow-Armstrong’s prolific night Wednesday against the Atlanta Braves, where the center fielder continued to build his case as unanimous National League MVP with two home runs and a triple. Counsell could’ve used the same bas
item.content:encoded:
What a wild week in Chicago this was.
“You’re shaking your head in amazement sometimes,” Chicago Cubs manager Craig Counsell said earlier this week. “You spend your whole life in baseball and you just don’t see this happen on a baseball field.”
Counsell was referring to Pete Crow-Armstrong’s prolific night Wednesday against the Atlanta Braves, where the center fielder continued to build his case as unanimous National League MVP with two home runs and a triple.
Counsell could’ve used the same basic quote Friday night in Cincinnati when Michael Busch was thrown out at second to end a 6-4 loss to the Reds, leaving the Cubs in a three-way wild-card tie with the Philadelphia Phillies and San Diego Padres. Cubs fans watching on Marquee were shaking their heads in amazement because you don’t often see that happen on a baseball field either.
With the tying run at the plate in Ian Happ, there was no reason for Busch to try to take second, making the attempt a foolish risk.
“It was stupid,” Counsell told reporters afterward. “l’ll take responsibility for it. It was a dumb play.”
Confirmed.
It was good Counsell took the blame away from his player, since a simple “Stay put” order by the manager would’ve at least given Happ a chance for some ninth-inning heroics.
No, it wasn’t why the Cubs lost the game.
Starter Clay Holmes walked five and allowed six runs in 5 1/3 innings in a subpar outing, Javier Assad struggled in relief and Crow-Armstrong went 0-for-5 and stranded nine runners. No one is perfect, not even the face of the franchise.
But in a tight wild-card race in which every game matters, the Busch gaffe was the one that will be remembered if the Cubs don’t get home-field advantage in the wild-card round and are eliminated on the road. There’s still time to finish strong, and the Cubs are capable of winning a wild-card series away from Wrigley Field either way.
But unforced mistakes like that can’t happen at this time of year, as Counsell knows.
Meanwhile, White Sox manager Will Venable watched his usually reliable bullpen implode Friday night on the South Side, blowing a six-run lead in an 11-8 loss to the Detroit Tigers.
Sox fans roundly booed Venable during pitching moves, a rarity this season. Though Venable deserves credit for the Sox being in the race, his pitching decisions have come under fire of late, and the bullpen arms suddenly looked tired. But on Saturday he pushed all the right buttons in a 3-1 win over the Tigers, with Noah Schultz and Grant Taylor saving the win for Sean Burke.
Counsell and Venable are under pressure to get their teams into the playoffs, like every other manager with a contending team. Venable is playing with house money since nothing was expected of the Sox this season, but he’ll still get some of the blame if the team collapses after 2½ months in first place.
Counsell’s Cubs are a virtual shoo-in for a wild-card berth, but he’s also expected to take the Cubs deep into the postseason with one of the game’s elite players in Crow-Armstrong, a strong lineup and the best defense most of us have ever seen in Chicago.
Both managers have had good years overall, but it’s how they finish that eventually will define their seasons.
In a season as crazy as this, you knew it would come down to the final days.
No one said it was going to be easy. It never is when you’re a baseball fan in Chicago.
Clicks for coaches
Kudos to Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill for reportedly refusing to let the Hawks media department film his opening speech to his players at the first full practice of training camp. This seems to be a common theme in sports these days — teams’ marketing departments trying to make the coach or manager into some kind of Knute Rockne figure for social media clicks.
Whatever Blashill said deserves to be private with his players, not the rest of the world. And as much as we enjoy Ben Johnson’s postgame speeches after wins, it wouldn’t be a bad idea for the Bears to keep it private once in a while.
Is the speech meant for the players or for the glorification of the coach? I’ll sit down and wait for my answer.
Swing-and-a-miss time
Sox shortstop Colson Montgomery is nearing the all-time single-season record of 223 strikeouts, set by the Arizona Diamondbacks’ Mark Reynolds in 2009. Montgomery entered Saturday tied for 10th with 213 strikeouts, one behind the current leader, the Philadelphia Phillies Kyle Schwarber, and had three more Saturday to make it 216.
Former Sox slugger Adam Dunn was one strikeout away from tying Reynolds’ record in 2012, but manager Robin Ventura sat him the final game, an act of mercy for the likeable Sox star in a meaningless game.
Venable needs Montgomery’s bat in the lineup in a tight playoff race, so he can’t afford to sit him to avoid setting the record. It’s up to Montgomery to avoid a date with the record book.
Birds of a feather
Hundreds of Ole Miss students chanted “A–hole” during LSU coach Lane Kiffin’s interview segment on Saturday’s “College GameDay.” Last week hundreds of Texas students relentlessly booed Texas Sen. Ted Cruz during the same show.
Which one deserved it more? It’s a toss-up.
Last call
Tigers pitcher Justin Verlander is retiring next week, making Sunday his final day at Rate Field as a player. Hopefully the Sox will give him a tribute, as other teams have done, since he was part of some great Tigers-Sox games on the South Side in his Hall of Fame career.
Medinah’s star turn
I’ve never been invited to be a member at Medinah Country Club, but if I were I’d ask the club to revoke the invitation to President Trump to be honorary chairman at this week’s Presidents Cup, just as he denied access to the White House for reporters of CNN, MS Now and Politico.
The invite was made by PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp, who said in a statement Trump’s “participation will help elevate the event on the international stage while furthering our mission of bringing people together through the game of golf.”
They couldn’t have made a worse choice.
