item.content:encoded:
Looking for a home run prop to kick off Sunday’s MLB action?
Just over a week remains in the 2026 regular season, leaving very few days with a full slate of games to choose from when it comes to the home run market.
While betting on home run props can be tricky – the best players are only going deep about 30 to 40 times per season – it is a fun way to get involved in the MLB action while potentially securing a favorable pay out.
Still, when it comes to these picks, we preach responsible betting because any bet set at these prices (+300 or higher) is much harder to hit.
On Sunday, I’m targeting three left-handed hitters in Daily Dinger, including Detroit Tigers All-Star Riley Greene, who has been red hot at the dish, hitting .368 over his last 17 games.
Let’s dive into my pick for Greene and two more home-run threats on Sunday, Sept. 20.
Best MLB Home Run Prop Bet Picks for Sunday, Sept. 20
Riley Greene to Hit a Home Run (+374)
Greene has homered five times in his 17 games since coming off the injured list, and he’s hitting .400 with three homers and an OPS of 1.135 over the last two weeks.
I like this price for Greene against the Chicago White Sox and right-hander Davis Martin, who has given up 14 home runs this season and seven homers in six outings since Aug. 1.
Greene has dominated Martin in his career, going 5-for-12 (.417) with a .950 OPS. The Tigers outfielder is also a better hitter against right-handed pitching, homering 15 times against them this season while posting a .295 batting average.
Since he’s been so hot since returning to the lineup, Greene is a solid bet at this price, especially against a Chicago team that is in danger of missing the playoffs.
Luis Garcia Jr. to Hit a Home Run (+516)
New York Yankees first baseman Luis Garcia Jr. has been slumping this week, but he’s still hitting .293 with four homers over the last four weeks.
Garcia has 27 home runs and a .290 batting average against right-handed pitching this season, and he’s fared pretty well against Arizona Diamondbacks starter Corbin Burnes in his career. Garcia is 2-for-10 with a home run against Burnes, and the D-Backs righty has allowed two long balls in two appearances this season in his return from Tommy John.
Even though he’s been slumping this week, Garcia is simply mispriced at this number (+516). It’s very rare to get a player with 30 home runs in a season at north of 5/1, and Garcia has shown with the Yankees and Washington Nationals that he’s a slugging percentage machine, posting a .534 mark in 2026.
Alec Burleson to Hit a Home Run (+374)
St. Louis Cardinals slugger Alec Burleson has crushed right-handed pitching this season, posting a .316 batting average, 20 home runs and a .938 OPS. He’s also been red hot over the last two weeks, hitting 325 with a 1.001 OPS overall.
On Sunday, Burleson takes on the Washington Nationals and right-hander Jake Irvin, who has given up 17 home runs in his 20 appearances in 2026. Irvin led the NL in homers allowed in 2025, and the Washington bullpen (105 homers allowed) has the third-worst ERA in MLB.
Burleson is 3-for-7 (.429) with a homer, a double and an OPS of 1.500 against Irvin. He’s a solid bet at nearly 4/1 odds against this awful Washington pitching staff.
Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change.

item.title: [bolavip.com] NY Yankees’ Cody Bellinger all but surrenders to Rays, yet drops World Series warning
item.dc:creator: Federico O'donnell
item.description: The New York Yankees lost the second game against the Arizona Diamondbacks by a score of 5-3. The fact that the loss came on the heels of Aaron Boone keeping Yankees fans concerned about Aaron Judge ahead of the MLB Postseason didn’t help. The fact that it widened the Tampa Bay Rays‘ lead over the Pinstripers for first place in the AL East wasn’t great, either. Still, Cody Bellinger believes in his team. Apparently, not enough to be convinced that the Yankees may still make it a pennant race wit
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees lost the second game against the Arizona Diamondbacks by a score of 5-3. The fact that the loss came on the heels of Aaron Boone keeping Yankees fans concerned about Aaron Judge ahead of the MLB Postseason didn’t help. The fact that it widened the Tampa Bay Rays‘ lead over the Pinstripers for first place in the AL East wasn’t great, either. Still, Cody Bellinger believes in his team.
Apparently, not enough to be convinced that the Yankees may still make it a pennant race with the Rays and come away on top, but he sure is confident that once the postseason arrives, the Bronx Bombers can turn it up a notch. And who knows? Why not win the World Series?
It’s happened before, and the Yankees have already received a good omen from the New York Giants and New York Jets. The signs may be out there. In case they aren’t clear enough, Bellinger’s latest statement might help out even more. The Rays, and frankly, the entire MLB landscape, have been put on notice.
“Yeah, I mean, [the Rays] are playing tremendous baseball. It’s tough to climb up in the standings if they keep winning. Mathematically pretty tough, we have got to keep on rolling,” Bellinger said postgame, via YES Network. “Obviously, the goal is win the division, rest your guys, get those extra off days, that’s always goal No. 1. Ultimately, World Series champions have come out of the Wild Card.”
Decisive Rays-Yankees series
Although Bellinger’s admission after the defeat in Phoenix sounded almost like the Yankees were waving the white flag in the pennant race against the Rays, there is still some baseball left to play, and a couple of very meaningful games on the horizon. New York and Tampa Bay will meet for a four-game series at Yankee Stadium (Sept. 22-24, with a doubleheader on Sept. 22) that could very well decide who wins the American League East division.
If the Boston Red Sox can get a win in the rubber match against the Rays while the Yankees secure the series against the D-Backs, then a sweep by New York against Tampa Bay would put both teams at even-Stevens. A sweep is the only way for the Yankees to get the tiebreaker over the Rays, as they are currently down 3-6 in the season’s head-to-head.
Another Rays win over the Pinstripers will clinch the tiebreaker for them. It’s a tough ask for New York, but not impossible. Obviously, without Judge, the climb is only steeper, but it may be perfect timing for a new miracle in the Bronx.

| One game vs | Arizona D-Backs | Boston Red Sox |

item.title: [hitc.com] 'Finally but too late' - MLB fans make Seattle Mariners point after Cal Raleigh's monster home run
item.dc:creator: Divij Kulkarni
item.description: Cal Raleigh hit the longest home run of his MLB career in a loss against the Colorado Rockies, and MLB fans had a nuanced response. The Seattle Mariners and Cal Raleigh have utterly failed to build upon the momentum of nearly making it to the World Series in the 2025 MLB season. While they haven’t been mathematically eliminated yet, it is only a matter of time. ‘Big Dumper’ has been as disappointing as his teammates, although he did provide some entertainment on Saturday. Raleigh slammed a gigan
item.content:encoded:
Cal Raleigh hit the longest home run of his MLB career in a loss against the Colorado Rockies, and MLB fans had a nuanced response.
The Seattle Mariners and Cal Raleigh have utterly failed to build upon the momentum of nearly making it to the World Series in the 2025 MLB season.
While they haven’t been mathematically eliminated yet, it is only a matter of time. ‘Big Dumper’ has been as disappointing as his teammates, although he did provide some entertainment on Saturday.
Raleigh slammed a gigantic home run, which was initially recorded as having gone 472 feet. It was later corrected, but at 459 feet, it is still the longest of his career.
MLB fans are in awe of Cal Raleigh’s hit but disappointed in him and the Seattle Mariners
In 2025, Cal Raleigh powered Seattle to a 90-72 season with 60 home runs and 125 RBIs, earning All-Star honours and finishing second in AL MVP voting.
In 2026, Raleigh’s production has fallen to a quite poor .184 average with 23 homers and 68 RBIs, while the Mariners sit at 72-83, all but guaranteed to miss the playoffs.
That’s what fans pointed to even as they were admiring the baseball star’s incredible home run hit.
“Well, about time he’s started back hitting home runs,” one fan said, their frustration clear. “Nice to see Cal is back, if only EVERYONE ELSE WAS BACK TOO,” another fan added.
“That is a meaningless HR, they have actually lost to the Rockies,” a third fan said. “Cal Raleigh, finally but too late to mean much for Seattle’s season,” a fourth fan claimed.
“If only we had this Cal earlier in the season – so many ‘what ifs’,” one Mariners fan lamented. “It has been a terrible season, but Cal Raleigh’s resurgence is a wonderful thing,” a sixth fan wrote.
It is bittersweet to see Raleigh finally playing at the highest level when the team’s season is all but over. However, a return to form bodes well for 2027, the Mariners and Raleigh will be raring to bounce back.

item.title: [whittierdailynews.com] Mookie Betts stays hot as Dodgers hammer Giants
item.dc:creator: Doug Padilla
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities. Hitting in Shohei Ohtani’s leadoff spot for the second consecutive game, Betts’ four-hit performance on Saturday night topped his three-hit output from Friday and started some serious downhill momentum toward a 10-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants. The victory kept the Dodgers (95-60) two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) for the best record in the National League and four games
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities.
Hitting in Shohei Ohtani’s leadoff spot for the second consecutive game, Betts’ four-hit performance on Saturday night topped his three-hit output from Friday and started some serious downhill momentum toward a 10-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
The victory kept the Dodgers (95-60) two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) for the best record in the National League and four games ahead of the Atlanta Braves (91-64) for the No. 2 playoff seed with seven games remaining. That includes four games against the Giants, who continue to limp toward the finish line of a miserable, injury-riddled season.
Betts couldn’t be feeling better, with his past two games part of a run of 10 hits over the last three games he has played. After more than two months of looking for an offensive leader, Betts has charged into the role, while reaching base five times on Saturday.
“It’s good; It’s fun,” Betts said. “But the main thing is doing it when it counts. So right now, we just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, we just need it to show up (offensively).”
The Dodgers expect Ohtani to return for the playoffs as he makes progress from biceps and knee discomfort. Betts, though, is proving to be a more-than-adequate emergency replacement.
“You know, I couldn’t tell you that I saw this (coming), but I just felt that he was stronger,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great, and I think for me it’s just trying to keep him confident.”
The Dodgers also have been transformed by the emergence of catcher Will Smith, who returned at the start of September after three months away because of neck inflammation. He had a home run among his three hits Saturday to give him homers in consecutive games, with three over his past eight contests.
“He’ll play two or three that last series (at San Francisco), but yeah, after that, he’ll be our guy (for the playoffs),” Roberts said.
There is also 21-year-old rookie Josue De Paula, who has continued to operate with ease since arriving in the major leagues last week. De Paula had a two-run single Saturday and walked twice while scoring two runs.
All of it overshadowed Tarik Skubal’s ninth start for the Dodgers. The two-time American League Cy Young Award winner was far from his best, allowing four runs on eight hits over five innings. His three strikeouts were his least in an outing with his new club.
Skubal unleashed his frustrations in the dugout by throwing his glove and cap at the bench, while firing an empty sports drink bottle at the wall.
“Sometimes you get frustrated and you got to get it out,” Skubal said. “It’s no good just keeping it pent up. So yeah, I’m a believer in getting that stuff out and kind of just moving on from the moment. The frustration is based on execution and knowing who I am and I’m just not doing that.”
Skubal blamed a lack of fastball command for the inability to shut down the Giants.
“Not driving it up and in (and) kind of pulling the ball down at times, pushing it up at times,” Skubal said. “I think pitching is almost all fastball command and mine wasn’t great today.”
And yet the offense allowed Skubal (11-7) to pick up the win, while improving to 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA for the Dodgers.
“That’s our job. That’s what we’re supposed to do,” Betts said. “So sometimes it’s them, sometimes it’s us. As long as we win.”
Kyle Tucker provided a scare when he fouled a ball off the side of his right knee early in the game then departed in the seventh inning with the Dodgers leading by six runs. Tucker reached base twice Saturday after collecting six hits with two home runs the previous two games.
“Whatever’s working at the time, you just ride it out, whether or not it’s the way you want to go about it,” said Tucker, who expects to play Sunday. “If it’s working, it’s working. You just try to go up there and put up competitive at-bats and just do your part on defense.”
The offense was not only productive, it was steady. The Dodgers scored runs in each of the first six innings and when they were held scoreless in the seventh, Betts still reached base with a walk.
Betts opened the game for the Dodgers with a leadoff double and scored on a Max Muncy double. Betts brought home his own run with an RBI single in the second.
The Dodgers struck with Smith’s home run in the third and got an RBI double from Betts in the fourth but were still tied 4-4 heading into the bottom of the fifth. They blew the game open from there, getting a go-ahead two-run single from Tommy Edman and an RBI pinch-hit single from Miguel Rojas for a 7-4 lead.
They scored three more times in the sixth, getting a Smith RBI single followed by a two-run single from De Paula.
“I think this is the first time, seems like all year, that we’ve had four or five hitters swing the bats well for four or five games,” Roberts said. “So it’s been really good to see. Obviously, Mookie is a big part of it, but everyone else is doing their part.”
The Dodgers now have a 5-4 lead in the Giants in the season series and are in line for a sweep on Sunday, which would be their first against their longtime rival since April of 2024.

item.title: [MLB.com] Acuña's scorching September rolls on with go-ahead slam
item.dc:creator: Mark Bowman
item.description: “I’ve been telling him, ‘Let me see some Ronald Acuña [stuff],’” Dubón said. “I haven’t seen it all year. He’s been hurting or lacking. But now I get to see [some of that stuff].” Acuña Jr. laughed as he passed Dubón and the group of reporters who were receiving this message on Friday night. Life has been good recently for the 2023 National League MVP and it got even better when he hit a seventh-inning grand slam that provided the Braves a key 6-3 win over the Astros on Saturday night at Daikin
item.content:encoded:
“I’ve been telling him, ‘Let me see some Ronald Acuña [stuff],’” Dubón said. “I haven’t seen it all year. He’s been hurting or lacking. But now I get to see [some of that stuff].”
Acuña Jr. laughed as he passed Dubón and the group of reporters who were receiving this message on Friday night. Life has been good recently for the 2023 National League MVP and it got even better when he hit a seventh-inning grand slam that provided the Braves a key 6-3 win over the Astros on Saturday night at Daikin Park.
“I feel like every big situation that comes up, he's answering,” Braves starting pitcher Grant Holmes said. “For him to turn it around like he has in the past month, it's pretty special. He’s getting hot at the right time.”
Acuña’s surge over the past month has powered the Braves through a pennant race that is nearing its end. The Braves now sit six games ahead of the Phillies in the National League East with just seven games remaining. Any Atlanta win or Philadelphia loss the rest of the way would give Atlanta its seventh NL East crown within the past nine seasons.
“It's exciting, especially when you think of the entire year and you look at it from 10,000 feet,” manager Walt Weiss said. “There's some really good things going on, and some guys stepping up. Yeah, I’m proud of these guys.”
Acuña was a rookie when the first of those recent division crowns was captured in his 2018 rookie season, and he’s now the seasoned veteran counted on to deliver like he did with the latest of his five career grand slams.
Astros right-hander Bryan Abreu entered with bases loaded and one out in the seventh. After striking out Drake Baldwin, Abreu threw a 1-0 fastball that Acuña drilled over the left-center-field wall.
“It’s the best feeling ever when a guy is throwing 96 or 97 and you get it,” Acuña said. “You don’t feel anything.”
Acuña’s decision to widen his stance a few weeks ago has halted his struggles against fastballs. This grand slam came against a 96.9 mph fastball located in the top left quadrant of the strike zone. Just 20 of 1,723 swings taken by a right-handed hitter against a right-handed pitcher versus a pitch this speed or greater in that zone entering Saturday had resulted in a home run this year.
Acuña has homered six times in 17 games this month, and is hitting .373 with a 1.129 OPS over his past 21 games. He did a lot of damage against the Phillies, hitting .464 with three homers and a 1.377 OPS in seven games against them this month.
This surge has been reminiscent of what the Braves right fielder routinely did during his MVP season, or at least before he tore the left anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee in 2024. Three years earlier, he had torn his right ACL.
“If you have both knees reconstructed, it takes time, not only physically but mentally, to regain the confidence in really letting it fly,” Weiss said. “I think we're seeing that now with Ronald again.”
While attempting to gain confidence in his two surgically-repaired knees this year, Acuña dealt with separate left hamstring strains. He was hitting just .228 with a .731 OPS when Weiss left the outfielder out of the lineup for the Aug. 26 series finale against the Dodgers.
As the Braves completed a sweep that night, Acuña worked in the batting cage and grew comfortable with the wider stance he has used over the past few weeks. He tallied three hits against the Rockies the next night and has since looked like the same superstar he has been whenever he is healthy.
“Finally, I got my timing and everything,” Acuña said. “I’m just having fun out there.”

item.title: [saratogian.com] Pavin Smith’s 2-run, game-winning homer lifts D-backs over Yankees 5-3, helps slim playoff hopes
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: By DAVID BRANDT PHOENIX (AP) — Pavin Smith hit a two-run homer in the ninth inning to lift the Arizona Diamondbacks over the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday night, giving the D-backs’ slim playoff hopes a boost. Ildemaro Vargas started the ninth with a walk, winning an ABS challenge on a full-count pitch initially called a strike. After Jordan Lawlar struck out, Smith pinch hit and drove a cutter from Michael Fulmer (0-1) into the right-field seats. Arizona pulled within four games of Philadelp
item.content:encoded:
By DAVID BRANDT
PHOENIX (AP) — Pavin Smith hit a two-run homer in the ninth inning to lift the Arizona Diamondbacks over the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday night, giving the D-backs’ slim playoff hopes a boost.
Ildemaro Vargas started the ninth with a walk, winning an ABS challenge on a full-count pitch initially called a strike. After Jordan Lawlar struck out, Smith pinch hit and drove a cutter from Michael Fulmer (0-1) into the right-field seats.
Arizona pulled within four games of Philadelphia for the final NL wild card with seven games remaining, snapping a three-game losing streak on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of its 2001 World Series win over the Yankees.
Juan Morillo (1-1) pitched 1 1/3 hitless innings. D-backs right-hander Brandon Pfaadt gave up one run on four hits and a walk over 4 1/3 innings, striking out three.
New York’s 11 walk-off losses are one behind San Francisco, which has the most in the major leagues.
New York ace Cam Schlittler gave up three runs — but only one earned — over six innings. The right-hander allowed three hits and three walks, striking out six and lowering his ERA to 1.94.
Schlitter’s 24 starts with one or no earned runs this year is one shy of the record in the live-ball era since 1920, set by Sandy Koufax in 1963, according to Major League Baseball.
The All-Star didn’t allow a hit until the fifth inning when Nolan Arenado lined a one-out single into left field. The right-hander then made a costly error on Tim Tawa’s sacrifice bunt attempt, dropping the ball as he tried to throw to first. Jordan Lawlar capitalized on the miscue with a two-out triple into the left-center field gap for a 2-1 lead.
Austin Wells and Heliot Ramos hit solo homers off Kevin Ginkel in the sixth to push the Yankees ahead 3-2.
Corbin Carroll hit a sacrifice fly in the bottom half but Schlittler limited damage by striking out Arenado and Tawa to end the threat.
Up next
1. Arizona RHP Corbin Burnes (0-0, 5.87 ERA) and Yankees RHP Will Warren (10-6, 3.89) start Sunday.
___

item.title: [record-bee.com] Vitello’s risky bullpen gambit dooms SF Giants in loss to Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Justice Delos Santos

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Philip Abner was going right back into the fire.
Abner had just made the wrong kind of history on Friday night, surrendering four homers in one inning. Max Muncy and Kyle Tucker went back-to-back to start the frame, then Mookie Betts and Will Smith did the same later in the inning. Following that disastrous outing, manager Tony Vitello said Abner would “be back out there at some point.”
That “some point” arrived less than 24 hours later. With the game on the line. In front of an announced attendance of 47,410. Considering the circumstances, Vitello’s decision was a true stunner. A night removed from the worst game of his career, Abner had to put out a fire at the game’s most critical point.
If this were Hollywood, maybe Abner would’ve enjoyed his redemption. But redemption never arrived. No feel-good story, no bounceback. Only an agonizing inning and the latest bizarre loss in a season full of them, a 10-4 defeat that had the makings of an upset win against back-to-back AL Cy Young Award winner Tarik Subal.
“Just needing to get one out. [He was] our only lefty in the bullpen, needing to get one out,” said manager Tony Vitello of the decision. “Other than our two guys that we want to finish with the game, you saw everybody we had available.”
When the Dodgers’ left-handed-hitting Josue De Paula stepped to the plate with two on and two outs, Abner was the team’s only available left-handed reliever to spell rookie Yunior Marte.
Reiver Sanmartín landed on the injured list before the game. Sam Hentges, who was activated from the injured list before the game, was unavailable, per Vitello. Matt Wilkinson was another option, but “Tugboat” is starting on Sunday. So, Abner.
That said, Vitello wasn’t required to seek out the left-on-left matchup. Especially since Abner had just become the first Giants pitcher to allow at least four homers in one inning since Alan Embree on May 20, 2001.
The hitter before De Paula, Kyle Tucker, was also left-handed, but Vitello left Marte face him. Vitello was likely saving Dylan Smith and Trent Harris for the later innings, but Kuhnel and Duncan Davitt, who he used in the sixth and seventh, were options.
Given how Friday unfolded, Vitello was asked if there was any consideration of steering clear of Abner.
“We avoided [Kyle] Tucker,” Vitello said. “But kind of what we got going on right now is finding out what you can and can’t do. And if I’m in his position, I’m dying to get back out there and see what I can do. I’ve had several guys come in the office, and we’ve had that conversation before. … Maybe we come up with a different plan, but otherwise, looking t get one out right there.” xr
Vitello added: “We talked about it last night and let him know that there’d be an opportunity around the corner. We knew Sanmartín was out. Sam wouldn’t be available based off his routine and his flight schedule and all that. So, we have talked about that.”
Abner’s first pitch foreshadowed what was to come, a bounced curveball that catcher Andrew Knizner couldn’t handle. He walked De Paula on five pitches, loading the bases for switch-hitter Tommy Edman.
Edman, who crushes lefties, pulled a single to left that scored Teoscar Hernández easily. Left fielder Turner Hill’s throw beat Kyle Tucker to the plate but was a tad off line and got away from Knizner. De Paula advanced to third, while Edman took second.
Following Edman’s two-run single, Miguel Rojas emerged from the Dodgers’ bench and rapped a single of his own. De Paula strolled home for Los Angeles’ third run of the inning, but a perfect throw by Hill nabbed Edman at the plate to mercifully end the inning and Abner’s night. Marte finished his night having allowed six runs over 4 2/3 innings.
“That’s just how baseball is,” Abner told this news organization when asked of the last two nights. “There’s too many games. You’re not going to be perfect all year. I definitely haven’t had the year that I’ve wanted. I’ve got one more week, and I’m going to make the most of it. Whatever happens, happens.”
Regarding Friday’s outing, in particular, Abner revealed that he had been tipping his pitches.
“Giving up four home runs sucks. It’s even worse when we were looking at video and found out I was tipping my pitches a little bit and telegraphing every single one of them,” Abner said. “Not even just fastball and offspeed. I worked on what to do to figure that out today. Walking my lefty isn’t exactly a good start, but I appreciate him letting me get back out there as soon as possible. It’s just one of those series. You’re going to have a bad series, and that’s just how it is.”
The bottom of the sixth featured a different flavor of agony as reliever Joel Kuhnel allowed three runs (one earned) due to a pair of misplays.
Shortstop Christian Koss committed an error when he dropped a throw on a force play from first baseman Brett Harris that would’ve been the second out. Two batters later, Harris could’ve been charged with an error after failing to corral a playable scoop from Koss that would’ve ended the inning. De Paula made Harris’ gaffe hurt, immediately driving in two more runs with a single.
The margin of defeat doesn’t reflect the Giants’ feistiness during the game’s first half. Thanks in large part to Victor Bericoto, San Francisco and Los Angeles entered the bottom of the fifth tied 4-4 as the Giants tagged Skubal for four runs.
Bericoto hit a no-doubt, two-run homer off Skubal on a middle-middle fastball in the third, emphatically throwing his bat before rounding the bases. The Giants scored a run in the fourth when Jonah Cox perfectly executed the squeeze play, then another in the fifth when Bericoto and Jung Hoo Lee hit back-to-back doubles, the latter driving in the former.
Then, that fateful bottom of the fifth.
For Skubal, it was the first time he allowed four runs in a game as a Dodger. This month alone, the Giants have scored nine combined runs off Skubal and Paul Skenes, the reigning Cy Young Award winners in both leagues. Despite those efforts, the Giants have lost both games.
Abner, 24, is one of many players fighting for a spot on next year’s roster. Realistically, with 16 players on the 60-day injured list and a wave of cuts coming, Abner could be looking at his final days in San Francisco. Regardless of what’s next, Abner is hoping for the best.
And to put the last two nights behind him.
“I’m definitely hoping they’ll keep me around,” Abner said. “It’s a long offseason. I’m going to do a lot to improve myself, so I’m hoping they’ll take a chance on me and keep it going from there.”

item.title: [MLB.com] These stars have turned their seasons around in the second half
item.dc:creator: Theo DeRosa
item.description: One well-timed hot streak from a star player can be all a team needs to go on a big run. While many key contributors struggled in the first half of 2026, several have picked it up big time since the All-Star break, lifting their clubs to late-season success. Here are 10 players -- five hitters and five pitchers -- who have turned things around in the second half. All stats are through Saturday's games unless otherwise specified. Hitters Alex Bregman, Cubs For as good as National League MVP Award
item.content:encoded:
One well-timed hot streak from a star player can be all a team needs to go on a big run.
While many key contributors struggled in the first half of 2026, several have picked it up big time since the All-Star break, lifting their clubs to late-season success.
Here are 10 players -- five hitters and five pitchers -- who have turned things around in the second half.
All stats are through Saturday's games unless otherwise specified.
Hitters
Alex Bregman, Cubs
For as good as National League MVP Award favorite Pete Crow-Armstrong has been lately, it’s actually Bregman who entered Saturday leading all qualifying hitters with a 168 wRC+ in the second half. The third baseman has a .298/.376/.609 slash line since the All-Star break, with his 17 second-half homers tied for fourth most in MLB.
Batting just .241 with nine home runs and a .695 OPS prior to the break, Bregman hadn’t exactly been meeting expectations after signing a five-year, $175 million deal with the Cubs. Now, though, he is up to 5.1 FanGraphs WAR, his highest total since 2022 (5.4). He’s been a big reason the Cubs are currently on track to host an NL Wild Card Series at Wrigley Field, and he will be a key bat in the middle of Chicago’s lineup in the postseason.
Steven Kwan, Guardians
With this week’s series win over the White Sox, the Guardians have surged into first place in the AL Central, in large part thanks to their leadoff hitter’s resurgence. In addition to his strong defense in left field -- Kwan has won four straight AL Gold Gloves in left to begin his career -- Kwan has been on fire at the plate.
After a disappointing first-half slash line of .225/.332/.282, including a .188 batting average in May, Kwan ranks second among qualifiers with a .347 average and is tied with Yordan Alvarez for first with a .435 on-base percentage in the second half. He has been setting the table admirably for a Cleveland club not getting as much as usual from third baseman José Ramírez (94 wRC+) and could help the Guardians secure not only the division title but a key first-round bye.
Jackson Merrill, Padres
Merrill took a step back in 2025 after finishing second to the Pirates’ Paul Skenes in 2024 NL Rookie of the Year Award voting, and the Padres center fielder appeared headed for further regression based on early returns in 2026. Merrill’s OPS was below .600 in late May as San Diego scuffled offensively, and he took a .219/.278/.350 slash line into the break.
Since then, Merrill has been a major reason why the Padres have a 38-21 (.644) record in the second half, tied with the Brewers for the best in the NL. He’s hitting .312 with 16 home runs, 48 RBIs and a .944 OPS in 59 games in the second half while playing standout defense in center. Merrill’s ability to recapture his rookie form has given the Padres a fighting chance to host a Wild Card Series, and he’ll be a key middle-of-the-order bat for the club.
George Springer, Blue Jays
Springer improved his OPS by nearly 300 points from 2024 to 2025, slashing .309/.399/.560 and finishing seventh in AL MVP balloting as Toronto fell just short of a World Series title. But the veteran’s numbers fell off again early in 2026, especially after Springer returned from a stint on the injured list for a left big toe fracture. He hit just .218 with a .677 OPS before the All-Star break, a period of rest that seemed to help considerably.
Springer recorded multiple hits in five of his first nine second-half games, finishing July with an .878 OPS, before batting .321 with an .858 OPS in August. While he has slowed a bit in September, battling multiple injuries, he has clearly found his footing at the plate. It might not be enough to drag a Blue Jays team dealing with a host of pitching injuries and a down year from Vladimir Guerrero Jr. to the postseason, but Toronto -- three games out of an AL Wild Card spot -- still has a chance.
Fernando Tatis Jr., Padres
While Merrill’s turnaround has been integral to the Padres’ second-half surge, Tatis’ production out of the leadoff spot has perhaps been even more important. The three-time All-Star began the season by scorching the baseball into the ground, going 55 games before hitting his first home run of the year on May 30.
The second half brought on a true power surge for Tatis, who homered three times in his first four games after the All-Star break and is now up to 24 dingers on the season. Entering Saturday, his 167 wRC+ in the second half was second in MLB, behind only Bregman. Tatis has raised his season OPS to .819 and has given the Padres a dangerous option at leadoff down the stretch.
Pitchers
Brayan Bello, Red Sox
Bello has turned the page on a dismal start to the season. The right-hander, coming off a 3.35 ERA as a starter in 2025, had a 9.00 ERA in his first six starts of 2026 and was moved to a bulk-relief role. Still, Bello took a 6.06 ERA into the All-Star break as the Red Sox finally began to heat up, winning nine straight games to end the first half and extending the streak to a franchise record-tying 15.
Bello has continued to impress for Boston, earning the start on Saturday and baffling the Rays over eight innings of one-run ball with 11 strikeouts. In the midst of a statistically unprecedented season, he’s found something that works, which has been crucial for a Red Sox team that has surged into postseason position and appears headed for another clash with the Yankees in the AL Wild Card Series.
Robert Gasser, Brewers
Tommy John surgery in June 2024 cut short Gasser’s promising rookie season, but he returned to make two solid starts at the tail end of 2025. The left-hander couldn’t sustain that success early in 2026, taking a 5.24 ERA into the All-Star break after being tagged for seven runs in three innings in his final first-half start.
Since then, Gasser has a 3.00 ERA in 57 innings of work after holding the Orioles scoreless over seven excellent innings on Saturday in Baltimore. In his first four September outings, including two against the Cubs, he has allowed just four earned runs across 21 innings pitched. With Brandon Woodruff’s 2026 return questionable and Kyle Harrison struggling mightily, Gasser’s improvement has made him an important arm for a Milwaukee team fighting to secure the NL’s No. 1 seed.
Tyler Mahle, Braves
Mahle owned a 5.13 ERA through his first 18 starts of 2026 for the Giants, but the Braves saw something in the veteran right-hander. Atlanta acquired Mahle ahead of the Trade Deadline for righty reliever Anthony Molina in a move that has paid considerable dividends for the Braves’ battered rotation.
Mahle has allowed only seven earned runs in eight starts for Atlanta, completing six or more innings in all but one of those outings. His 1.28 ERA in that span is the third best among all pitchers (min. 40 innings), and he’s been an excellent complement to ace lefty Chris Sale atop the Braves rotation. With Spencer Strider, Spencer Schwellenbach, Bryce Elder, Reynaldo López and Hurston Waldrep all on the injured list, Mahle has not only covered important innings but has been remarkably effective.
Aaron Nola, Phillies
Nola had an ERA above 6 in an injury-marred 2025 season, and his 2026 looked to be more of the same. The usually dependable right-hander gave up 20 home runs in the first half alone, tied for the fifth most in MLB, and headed into the All-Star break with a 5.75 ERA.
Since then, Nola has returned to near-vintage form for the Phillies, who have also gotten strong second halves from lefty Jesús Luzardo (currently on the injured list with left shoulder inflammation) and rookie righty Andrew Painter. After Thursday’s excellent start against the Mets, Nola has a 2.78 ERA in the second half, striking out 67 in 71 1/3 innings despite giving up 14 more home runs in just 12 starts. If he can limit the long balls, he could be at least an adequate replacement for Luzardo if the southpaw cannot return for the start of the postseason.
Brandon Pfaadt, D-backs
Pfaadt hasn’t quite lived up to his billing as a former top prospect just yet, but he’s shown flashes, such as his success against the Dodgers and Phillies during the D-backs’ 2023 World Series run. The righty's recent results have been quite encouraging, too: Pfaadt has a 3.01 ERA in the second half, including a run of 27 2/3 scoreless innings across four starts from July 28-Aug. 14. 
Optioned to Triple-A Reno in June after a poor start to the year, Pfaadt now has the chance to help pitch the D-backs into the playoffs, which might be difficult in an NL Wild Card race featuring the Cubs, Phillies and Padres. Pfaadt is lined up to start during Arizona’s final series of the season, a pivotal three-game set in San Diego from Sept. 25-27, and his outing could determine the D-backs’ postseason fate.

CHICAGO (Kyodo) -- Seiya Suzuki collected two hits, including a run-scoring single, as the Chicago Cubs defeated the Cincinnati Reds 5-2 on Saturday.
Batting third as the designated hitter, Suzuki went 2-for-3 with an RBI at Great American Ball Park.
"Although I wasn't waiting for (a changeup), I was able to get the bat on it," Suzuki said.
"The quality of my outs hadn't been very good lately, so my swings probably looked hesitant, but I was able to swing the bat in good form today."
Munetaka Murakami hit an RBI single to open the scoring as the Chicago White Sox beat the Detroit Tigers 3-1.
The Japanese slugger, who has hit 32 home runs in his MLB rookie season, went 1-for-4 with an RBI at Rate Field.
Meanwhile, Kazuma Okamoto singled to finish 1-for-4 as the Toronto Blue Jays lost to the Texas Rangers 6-2.

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Richie Palacios dropped a blooper into shallow right in the ninth inning to score Junior Caminero and give the Tampa Bay Rays a 2-1 victory over the Boston Red Sox on Saturday.
Tampa Bay, which has three walk-off wins on its current homestand, lowered its magic number to clinch the AL East to five games. The second-place Yankees are in Arizona on Saturday night.
Prior to Palacios’ single, the Rays were 0 for 17 with runners in scoring position over the first two games of the series. The postseason-bound Rays, who’ve won seven of their last eight, capitalized on two fortuitous bounces in the ninth.
First, Caminero’s foul popup bounced off the Tropicana Field catwalk and out of the reach of third baseman Caleb Durbin. Caminero then lined the next pitch from Garrett Whitlock (7-2) into left. Three batters later, after Chandler Simpson singled, Connor Wong’s passed ball moved Caminero to third.
Bidding to clinch a wild-card berth, the Red Sox squandered a prime opportunity in the top of the ninth.
Facing closer Bryan Baker (4-2) in a tie game, Boston got a double from Caleb Durbin and a triple from Jarren Duran. However, Nick Fortes threw out Durbin stealing third before Duran’s triple, and Caminero made a stellar play at third base to retire Isiah Kiner-Falefa, stranding Duran.
Boston also wasted a phenomenal effort from starter Brayan Bello, who matched a career high with 11 strikeouts. In eight innings, he allowed five hits, one run and no walks. Red Sox closer Aroldis Chapman (lat tightness) was unavailable.
The Red Sox took a 1-0 lead with doubles from Durbin and Roman Anthony in the third inning. Trevor Story extended his hitting streak to 10 games with a sixth-inning single.
Jonathan Aranda tied it with an opposite-field solo homer on the first pitch of the Rays’ fourth.
The Rays are an MLB-best 25-14 in one-run games.
Boston could have clinched a playoff berth with a win combined with a loss by either the Rangers or Astros. Both of those teams were seven games behind the Red Sox with eight games remaining entering Saturday.
UP NEXT
Right-hander Griffin Jax (7-10, 3.80 ERA) gets the nod for the Rays on Sunday in the series finale. Boston had not announced a starter.

item.content:encoded:
홈 플레이트에서의 승부는 언제나 흥미진진합니다. 하지만 그 플레이가 a) 보기 드문 명장면이고 b) 상징적인 의미까지 담고 있을 때는 그야말로 특별한 짜릿함을 선사합니다.
와이엇 랭포드가 19일 밤(미국 현지시간) 글로브 라이프 필드에서 열린 블루제이스와의 경기에서 바로 그러한 명장면을 연출하며 텍사스의 6대2 승리에 기여했습니다.
6회말 에반 카터가 날린 중견수 뜬공 때 3루에서 태그업한 랭포드는 홈을 향해 전력 질주했습니다. 블루제이스의 중견수 브렛 베이트먼의 송구가 홈 플레이트 쪽으로 다소 치우치게 날아오면서, 토론토의 포수 알레한드로 커크가 랭포드의 진로를 가로막는 위치로 이동했습니다.
그러자 랭포드는 그의 위로 뛰어넘는 '허들(hurdle)' 동작을 선보였습니다.
유일한 문제는 랭포드가 다시 땅으로 내려왔을 때 홈 플레이트를 밟지 않고 지나쳐버렸다는 점이었습니다. 송구가 커크 뒤로 빠졌기 때문에 평소라면 큰 문제가 되지 않았을 상황이었습니다.
하지만 변수가 있었습니다. 투수 폴 시월드가 백업을 위해 홈 뒤로 와 있었고, 시월드에게는 랭포드가 다시 몸을 돌려 홈을 찍기 전에 태그할 수 있는 확실한 기회가 주어졌습니다. 하지만 랭포드는 시월드가 자신에게 도달하기 전에 재빨리 홈 플레이트를 터치하며 텍사스의 이날 경기 6번째 득점을 올렸습니다.
랭포드는 레인저스 스포츠 네트워크와의 인터뷰에서 "그냥 고개를 숙이고 달렸습니다"라며, "상대 포수가 베이스라인 쪽에 위치하게 되었습니다. 그냥 모든 일이 순식간에 벌어졌습니다. 사실 그렇게 뛰어넘을 계획은 전혀 없었습니다"라고 당시 상황을 설명했습니다.
랭포드의 이 놀라운 도약은 토요일 승리를 통해 레인저스가 팀 전체로서 이뤄낸 성과를 완벽하게 상징하는 명장면이 되었습니다. 텍사스는 정규시즌 마감을 단 일주일 앞두고, 텍사스주의 라이벌인 휴스턴을 뛰어넘어 아메리칸리그 서부 지구 단독 선두 자리로 도약했습니다.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

20 Sep 2026, 04:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Kim Klement Neitzel)
Richie Palacios produced a two-out, walk-off single in the ninth inning as the Tampa Bay Rays edged the Boston Red Sox 2-1 on Saturday afternoon in St. Petersburg, Fla., to even their final home series of the regular season.
Against Garrett Whitlock (7-2), Palacios looped a 1-2 sinker into shallow right to score Junior Caminero as the Rays (94-60) hit their third walk-off winner during the nine-game homestand.
Jonathan Aranda homered while Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson posted two hits apiece as Tampa Bay improved to 7-1 on the homestand.
Bidding for a fifth consecutive win over five starts, Freddy Peralta received no decision after yielding just one run on four hits over 5 2/3 innings that took 97 pitches. He struck out six and walked two.
Caleb Durbin stroked two doubles and scored for the Red Sox (84-71), who lost for the first time in three games.
Starting pitcher Brayan Bello went a season-best eight innings and allowed one run on five hits with a career high-tying 11 strikeouts.
The Rays got an out with the infield drawn in and appeared to escape trouble in the third. Then Roman Anthony, who homered and had three RBIs in Friday's 4-2 win in the opener, remained hot and made it 1-0 with a two-out double that scored Durbin.
Cedric Mullins laid down a bunt single and reached second on Durbin's throwing error to open the third, but he was picked off and caught trying to steal third on Jorge Mateo's failed sacrifice bunt.
In the fourth, Aranda tied it 1-all when he rocked his 22nd homer to left field as he took Bello's 97 m.p.h. four-seam fastball the opposite way.
With Bello still in the game in the seventh, Hicks led off with a single and Simpson dropped one into right with no outs. Following a groundout and a fielder's choice, Bello ended the threat by whiffing Mullins on a foul tip.
Durbin lined his second double with one out in the ninth, but Hicks tossed him out trying to steal third. Jarren Duran followed with his fifth triple, but Isiah Kiner-Falefa grounded out to deep third to end the inning off Bryan Baker (4-2).
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
BALTIMORE (AP) — The Milwaukee Brewers tied a team record with their 97th win of the season, beating Baltimore 1-0 Saturday with the help of a fly ball lost in the sun by Orioles right fielder Rece Hinds.
Already assured of their fourth straight NL Central title and eighth playoff berth in nine season, the big league-best Brewers (97-58) matched the wins total of last year’s team that finished 97-65.
Baltimore (75-80) fell four games behind the Chicago White Sox for the AL’s last wild card with seven to play.
Robert Gasser (5-5) allowed three hits over seven innings, Abner Uribe worked around a leadoff single in the eighth, and Aaron Ashby pitched a perfect ninth for his third save, finishing the Brewers’ 11th shutout this season and first 1-0 win.
Hinds lost Joey Ortiz’s fly ball in the sun in the second inning and tumbled to the ground, and Gary Sánchez hit into a run-scoring groundout.
Trevor Rogers (10-11) struck out 10, walked one and allowed three hits in a season-high eight innings.
Up next
Milwaukee RHP Jacob Misiorowski (15-5, 1.89 ERA) faces Baltimore RHP Brandon Young (9-4, 3.65) as the three-game series concludes Sunday night.

item.content:encoded:
HOUSTON (AP) Ronald Acuña Jr. hit a go-ahead grand slam in the seventh inning, and the Atlanta Braves beat Houston 6-3 Saturday night to drop the Astros out of the AL West lead.
Houston (77-78) fell one game behind Texas (78-77) and trails the Chicago White Sox (79-76) by two games for the last AL wild card. The Astros had held at least a share of the division lead each day since Aug. 25.
Atlanta assured its eighth playoff berth in nine seasons on Friday and is in position to clinch its first NL East title since 2023 on Sunday.
Trailing 2-1, Atlanta loaded the bases against AJ Blubaugh (5-3) and Acuña homered off Bryan Abreu for his second grand slam this season and the fifth of his big league career.
Acuña singled and walked twice in his first three plate appearances. He has homered in three of his last four games.
Mike Yastrzemski added a solo homer in the eighth inning.
Grant Holmes (10-5) allowed two runs and eight hits over six innings.
Yainer Diaz hit an RBI double in the eighth off Dylan Lee, who struck out pinch-hitter Nelson Velázquez to end the inning.
Raisel Iglesias pitched a perfect ninth inning for his 34th save in 37 chances.
Jose Altuve had three hits for Houston, while Isaac Paredes was 2 for 3 with a home run, walk and two RBIs.
Christian Walker had two hits after entering the game hitless in his previous 23 at-bats.
Hayden Wesneski allowed one run on four hits over 5 1/3 innings.
Astros RHP Hunter Brown (6-3, 3.43 ERA) and Braves LHP Martín Pérez (9-9, 3.07 ERA) start Sunday.

item.content:encoded:
Conecta Isaac Paredes su jonrón número 22, pero los Astros pierden liderato de su división
El hermosillense esta a nueve cuandrangulares de su récord en Grandes Ligas
Isaac Paredes conectó este sábado su cuadrangular número 22 en la presente campaña de MLB, aunque no fue suficiente para evitar que los Astros de Houston cayeran por 6-3 ante los Bravos de Atlanta y cayeran al segundo lugar en la División Oeste de la Liga Americana.
El tablazo del hermosillense llegó en el cierre de la primera entrada, ante el abridor Grant Holmes, quien había dominado a Jeremy Peña y a Yordan Álvarez iniciando esa tanda.
Paredes remolcó una segunda anotación en la tercera baja, con un sencillo al jardín derecho que fue suficiente para impulsar a Peña después después que este último había conectado un triple.
El mexicano también anotó dos carreras, una vez que en el octavo episodio negoció una base por bolas y más tarde fue mandado al plato con doblete de Yainer Díaz.
Con siete campañas de experiencia en Grandes Ligas, la presente ya es la segunda mejor en términos de cuadrangulares para el sonorense, solo por detrás de los 31 conseguidos en 2023 con los Rays de Tampa Bay.
Ese jonrón también lo acercó a 10 del récord que ostenta Aurelio Rodríguez (124), el tercer jugador nacido en México con más cuadrangulares en Ligas Mayores. Vinicio Castilla (320) y Jorge Orta (130) encabezan la lista.
A los Astros de Houston les restan siete encuentros en la temporada regular, por lo que su marca podría incrementarse todavía más de aquí al próximo domingo 27 de septiembre.

Trea Turner News: On base four times in Saturday's loss
Turner went 2-for-3 with two walks, a run scored and a stolen base in Saturday's 10-3 loss to the Mets.
The star shortstop was busy on the basepaths Saturday, but Turner is struggling to build any momentum ahead of the playoffs. He's collected multiple hits in four of his last 11 games, but over that stretch he's batting just .256 (11-for-43) with two homers, three steals, five RBI and eight runs. Turner needs one more homer to record the fourth 20-20 campaign of his career.

item.content:encoded:
【カブス5-2レッズ】シンシナティ／グレートアメリカンボールパーク、9月19日（日本時間20日）
熾烈なワイルドカード争いを繰り広げているカブスは敵地でのレッズ3連戦の2戦目。五回に鈴木誠也のタイムリーでリードを2点に広げた直後、レッズの反撃に遭って同点に追いつかれたものの、六回にマイケル・ブッシュの20号ソロで勝ち越すと、終盤にも追加点を奪い、5-2で勝利した。ワイルドカード争いで4番手につけるダイヤモンドバックスの結果次第ではあるが、早ければ20日（同21日）にもポストシーズン進出が決定する。 カブスは二回、先頭のニコ・ホーナーの二塁打から1死一、三塁とチャンスを広げ、マット・ショウの犠牲フライで1点を先制。先発のマシュー・ボイドが好投を続ける中、五回には2死三塁の場面で鈴木誠也がレフトへのタイムリーを放ち、2-0とリードを広げた。 ボイドは五回、先頭のエウヘニオ・スアレスに四球を与えると、1死後にJJ・ブレデイにライトへのヒットを浴び、遊撃手ダンズビー・スワンソンの送球エラーが絡んで1失点。2死後、キブライアン・ヘイズにセンターへのタイムリーを許し、2-2の同点に追いつかれた（ボイドの自責点は1）。 しかし、続く六回にブッシュの20号ソロが飛び出し、勝ち越しに成功。2番手のダニエル・パレンシアが2イニングをパーフェクトに抑える好リリーフを見せると、八回にはホーナーのタイムリーで貴重な追加点を奪った。 3番手のアーロン・シバーリは八回に2死一、二塁のピンチを招いたが、4番手のライアン・ゼファージャンがサル・スチュワートを空振り三振に仕留めて無失点。九回にはスワンソンの19号ソロでダメ押しの5点目を奪い、最終回はゼファージャンから5番手のライアン・ロリソンにつなぐ継投でレッズの反撃を封じ、5-2で勝利した。 鈴木は「3番・DH」でスタメン出場。初回の第1打席は四球を選んで出塁し、三回の第2打席はライトへのヒットを放った。五回の第3打席は2死三塁のチャンスでレフトへのタイムリー。八回の先頭打者として迎えた第4打席は空振り三振に倒れ、3打数2安打1打点1四球だった。今季の打撃成績は打率.267、OPS.833となっている。

item.content:encoded:
The MLB offseason is over a month away, but rumors are already spreading.
The Boston Red Sox are in the middle of one as it pertains to an outfielder.
Seattle Mariners LF Randy Arozarena is due to hit free agency after the conclusion of this year’s World Series, and Boston could make him a big offer, according to a Seattle reporter.
“(The Mariners are) going to lose their best offensive player. Randy Arozarena’s gonna be a free agent. I think we all know Randy would probably prefer to stay on the east coast,” The Seattle Times’ Ryan Divish said on Foul Territory on Friday. “I’m guessing Boston is ready to cut a huge check for him.”
Arozarena, 31, is having a career year for the Mariners. He was named an All-Star for the third time and is slashing .281/.377/.479 with an .856 OPS. He’s clubbed 25 home runs (two away from tying a career-high), scored 104 times, and driven in 63 runs across 147 games.
If he were on the 2026 Red Sox, he’d lead the club in runs and have the second-most homers behind Willson Contreras (27).
Arozarena, a Cuban native, was named the 2021 American League Rookie of the Year in 2021 as a member of the Tampa Bay Rays. The Rays dealt him to Seattle in 2024, but his time to choose his next team is coming up.
Divish said he doesn’t think the Mariners will “get in a bidding war” for Arozarena once he hits the market.
If Boston were to land the right-handed hitter, they’d likely have to pay up. Arozarena could earn over $20 million annually as he’ll surely seek out a lengthy contract.
On top of the finances, the Red Sox would have to make room on their roster for the slugger. The team currently has eight outfielders on its major-league roster (Ceddanne Rafaela, Masataka Yoshida, and Eli White are on the injured list).
White and Jahmai Jones, whom Boston picked up at the trade deadline earlier this year, are both arbitration-eligible after this season. The team could non-tender one of the two to make room as one of many possible moves in a hypothetical scenario involving adding Arozarena.
Additionally, the Red Sox have reportedly attempted to trade Jarren Duran several times over the last couple of years. They could give that another go this winter and let Arozarena — who also plays LF — take his place.
Designated hitter is also an option for Arozarena. He’s DHed minimally, but given his age and Boston’s crowded outfield, it could be feasible.
Based on his career, Arozarena would be a magnificent fit at Fenway Park. In 32 career games played in Boston, he’s slashing .278/.351/.481 with an .833 OPS, five HR, 12 doubles, and 19 RBI.
Arozarena is set to hit free agency at an incredibly uncertain time in the league’s history, though. A lockout looms when the current collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1, which would halt the ability for clubs to sign free agents.
Boston would need to move rather swiftly in acquiring Arozarena — and any other players on the trade and free agent markets— before that deadline, and until a new CBA is agreed upon. The latter could take an indefinite amount of time.

item.title: [yardbarker.com] Caleb Durbin blows the game for Red Sox with brutal baserunning blunder

item.description: Caleb Durbin managed to do exactly what you do not want to do as the go-ahead run. The Boston Red Sox played Saturday against the division rival Tampa Bay Rays. In the top of the ninth inning at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. with the score tied 1-1, the Boston infielder Durbin hit a one-out double to represent the winning run. item.content:encoded:
Caleb Durbin managed to do exactly what you do not want to do as the go-ahead run.
The Boston Red Sox played Saturday against the division rival Tampa Bay Rays. In the top of the ninth inning at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. with the score tied 1-1, the Boston infielder Durbin hit a one-out double to represent the winning run.
In the middle of the next at-bat by teammate Jarren Duran however, Durbin committed an inexplicable blunder — he decided to make a break for third base. Durbin was then easily thrown out for the second out of the inning.
Caleb Durbin is caught trying to steal 3rd and Junior Caminero is FIRED UP
We are still tied in the 9th!pic.twitter.com/wrriTXW1yj
Making matters even worse for Durbin was that Duran proceeded to smack a triple in his at-bat (but was stranded at third after Isiah Kiner-Falefa grounded out to end the half-inning). While Duran’s triple would have allowed Durbin to waltz home if he had simply stayed put, the baserunning error left the game tied and opened the door for the Rays to win the game in the bottom of the ninth inning on a walkoff RBI single by Richie Palacios.
It is hard to tell exactly what Durbin was thinking there. He was already in scoring position and also had a left-handed batter up at the plate (meaning that the catcher had an obstructed throw to third base). Though Durbin has stolen 19 bases so far this season, that was simply a risk completely unnecessary for him to take in that situation.
On the bright side, the 84-71 Red Sox do look to be locked into the second AL Wild Card spot at this point, which would have them open up the playoffs against the rival New York Yankees. But these are the types of moments that explain why Boston is a Wild Card team to begin with (similar to the time that they cost themselves four runs by botching a single challenge).

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Mets owner Steve Cohen talks team's future, front office discussions, Pete Alonso's return to Citi Field
item.dc:creator: Robert Sanchez
item.description: On the day of Carlos Beltran's number retirement ceremony at Citi Field, a special and joyous occasion for the club and all those involved, Mets owner Steve Cohen made sure to also address the elephant in the room – what's been bubbling up for many Mets fans this season, particularly this past week. item.content:encoded:
On the day of Carlos Beltran's number retirement ceremony at Citi Field, a special and joyous occasion for the club and all those involved, Mets owner Steve Cohen made sure to also address the elephant in the room – what's been bubbling up for many Mets fans this season, particularly this past week.
Speaking with the SNY booth in the fourth inning on Saturday, Cohen was asked about the recent shenanigans that happened at the ballpark during the team's last series with the Baltimore Orioles.
In what was Pete Alonso's first time back in Queens since he left the Mets in free agency over the offseason, fans came out in droves and gave the first baseman quite the reception. Not only did they give Alonso a standing ovation in his first at-bat, standard for a former beloved player coming back to his old ballpark, but fans were also actively cheering for Alonso's success every time he went to the plate.
Things got murky when Alonso, who was chasing his 300th career home run, hit the milestone by hitting a game-tying home run against Kodai Senga in the top of the ninth inning, which caused the stadium to erupt in cheers – odd for a home ballpark.
The Mets went on to lose that game in extra innings and during the postgame, players, including Sean Manaea, admitted to being surprised by the response of the home fans seemingly cheering against their team.
"You can't make it up, it was just so crazy," Cohen said on Saturday. "The fans, they're passionate and when they feel something they're gonna let you know and I'm okay with that. Pete hits his 300th home run and it was sort of poetic. It was sort of amazing that it all occurred at the same time."
Cohen seemed to understand where the fans were coming from, letting their frustration out for a player they believed deserved to be a lifetime Met.
Of course, that's not how things turned out, and in the midst of a disappointing season, it made it all the more painful.
"I'll say it again, it didn't surprise me," Cohen said about the fan's response to Alonso's return. "I can remember being at a previous Mets event the previous year and the fans were vocal on Alonso and listen, it's hard to say goodbye to a homegrown player. Obviously he's well liked and a great Met and those decisions got made and unfortunately we gotta look forward and look forward to '27 and what we're gonna do.
"But it was weird because we got past the trade deadline and the team was playing well and you got a sense that fans were really getting excited and then Pete came in and we kinda reversed course for three days, but now I think we're back on track again."
It's true, prior to Alonso's homecoming, despite the lost season, fans seemed to be invested in the team because of the young talent that spurred hope for the future, as well as the team's improved performance on the field, albeit too late.
Still, Cohen believed that what the Mets had been building was enough to garner enthusiasm for what's to come, even if it came during a second consecutive season missing the playoffs.
"I think that's what the fans like," he said. "We're playing young, we're playing athletic. We've developed a lot of players in a very short period of time and so that's something you can really look forward to. So it's true, two things can be true: a lousy season, but still something to look forward to."
Something else Mets fans can look forward to is help arriving for president of baseball operations David Stearns – both in terms of the front office as well as a manager.
Cohen talked about the search for somebody to lead the team and what he wants to see out of his next manager, a conversation that fittingly happened during Beltran's number retirement ceremony.
"I see the manager's role as mostly about culture and bringing the locker room together," the owner said. 'I think the actual managerial decisions are, I would say, 20-30 percent of what they do and the rest of it is trying to galvanize your ball club and trying to get them in the right frame of mind and I'm looking for someone that can bring out the best in their ball players."
As for the front office, Cohen mentioned that he's "identified some things that we can do better" and talked about bringing in extra voices to the mix to help out.
"We're going to try to add certain voices into the front office that I think will be helpful and I know David supports that, and I'm looking forward to, when we make those decisions, to announce them," he said.
Cohen continued: "It doesn't have to be a GM, it could be other ways to support David and the front office and I think the whole point is to get more opinions in the front office and people who are either pretty good at evaluating talent or people who have been in those positions before in the front office – in high positions – and help David out and help the team out as far as getting a different point of view."
Cohen was also asked how he deals with, as he described it, such passionate fans that are always eager to give their two cents in how to run the team.
"Everyone's got an opinion, I'll tell you that," he said. "…And frankly, there's some good ideas out there, so my ears are open."

item.title: [Chicago Sun-Times] Kevin Gausman's roller-coaster run with Cubs might be result of Blue Jays' World Series run
item.dc:creator: Jeff Agrest
item.description: CINCINNATI — Veteran right-hander Kevin Gausman has been riding a roller coaster since joining the Cubs before the trade deadline. It’s not one he’s enjoying. “It’s really frustrating,” Gausman told the Sun-Times, “especially after being really consistent for the last five, six years.” Gausman has alternated good and bad outings for weeks, going from seven innings of scoreless ball to four innings with six runs, including three home runs. item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — Veteran right-hander Kevin Gausman has been riding a roller coaster since joining the Cubs before the trade deadline. It’s not one he’s enjoying.
“It’s really frustrating,” Gausman told the Sun-Times, “especially after being really consistent for the last five, six years.”
Gausman has alternated good and bad outings for weeks, going from seven innings of scoreless ball to four innings with six runs, including three home runs. In eight starts for the Cubs, Gausman has a 5.04 ERA.
In his previous five seasons, one with the Giants and four with the Blue Jays, Gausman had a 3.34 ERA in 158 starts. With 2,083 innings on his arm in 14 regular seasons, he knows he’s dealing with wear and tear, and it isn’t easy.
“You’ve got to give yourself a little bit of grace when it comes to the workload that I had last year,” Guasman said. “My 13th year, I made it to the World Series. So for 12 years, I had one way of doing the offseason. I’ve been in a lot of postseasons but never made it very far.”
In his first 12 seasons, Gausman totaled 25 ⅔ innings in the postseason. Last year during the Jays’ run to the World Series, he totaled 30 ⅔. In 2024, a non-playoff year, Gausman began his offseason throwing regimen on Oct. 28, the same day as Game 3 of the World Series. In 2025, he started Games 2 and 6 of the World Series.
“So I threw for over a year, threw the most pitches in all of baseball, most starts in all of baseball, most innings,” Gausman said. “So with that and less time, it was tricky trying to figure out how I make sure that I’m ready for the start of this season while also giving myself a little bit of a break. I came to the realization that I just wasn’t going to have much of a break.”
He might be feeling that now. After all, Gausman’s season with the Jays wasn’t rosy, either. He had a 4.38 ERA in 23 starts. Knowing the load he carried last season, the Jays had him build back up slowly in spring training. But as Gausman said, there’s no manual to help a pitcher prepare for the season after a World Series run.
“It’s hard to tell whether it was last year or just a combination of my whole career,” he said.
Cubs manager Craig Counsell said another factor is at play: Gausman is basically a two-pitch pitcher, fastball and splitter.
“It puts a higher premium on his execution,” Counsell said. “The hitter’s got two pitches to think about. He’s paid for his mistakes a little bit more. But when you’re relying on those two pitches, that kind of makes sense.
“The split-finger is also more difficult to throw, but when you get it going, it’s really hard to hit. When it’s not going your way, you’re probably going to throw balls with it. And he’s two pitches, so there’s not another pitch to go to.”
Which begs the question: How will the Cubs use Gausman in the postseason? They acquired him with his postseason experience in mind, but he might not get a start in the wild-card series. He doesn’t know what his role will be in the playoffs.
“I don’t think anybody knows,” Gausman said. “Nobody knew Chris Bassit was going to throw [8 ⅔] innings out of the [Jays’] bullpen in the World Series and only give up one run. It’s going to take every single guy on this staff to do what we want to do, which is go to the World Series.
“It’s all hands on deck. I’ve pitched out of the bullpen in the postseason. If you’ve been starting all year, it’s different. But you’ve just got to go into it with the mentality that it’s going to take everybody, and if you tell them you’re fresh, the phone might ring and it might be you.”

item.dc:creator: Tommy Wild
item.description: If there's one thing that Jose Ramirez has been known for throughout his career, it's how consistent he has been as the Cleveland Guardians star. Year in and year out, Ramirez is an MVP candidate in the American League. Unfortunately, the 2026 season has been a different story for Ramirez. The superstar's stats are nowhere near on par with his typical career numbers. There could be several reasons for this, but one of the primary ones has to do with the hamstring injury Ramirez suffered in the m
item.content:encoded:
If there's one thing that Jose Ramirez has been known for throughout his career, it's how consistent he has been as the Cleveland Guardians star. Year in and year out, Ramirez is an MVP candidate in the American League.
Unfortunately, the 2026 season has been a different story for Ramirez.
The superstar's stats are nowhere near on par with his typical career numbers. There could be several reasons for this, but one of the primary ones has to do with the hamstring injury Ramirez suffered in the middle of June.
Even though Ramirez only missed a little over a month with the injury, he still hasn't looked like the same hitter. Even though it's normal for a player returning from this injury to take time to regain their power, it's still been weird to see Ramirez struggle so much at the plate.
Even though the season numbers aren't there for Ramirez, what the Guardians can fall back on is his stats over the last few weeks.
It really looks like Ramirez has turned a corner and is regaining his form just in time for the final playoff push.
Ramirez has logged six hits in his last seven games, including a pair of doubles in the rubber match against the Chicago White Sox and a solo blast against the Athletics, which gave him his 1,000th career RBI.
Ramirez admitted that his recovery from the hamate injury is still a work in progress, but there have certainly been days when he's felt much better.
"Working on it everyday," said Ramirez through his interpreter Auggie Rivero.
"I have to keep working on the training room every day because this is the type of injury, one day you feel good, the next one doesn't feels so well... The last couple days I feel better, but we know this type of injury can just vary every day."
Manager Stephen Vogt acknowledged after Friday's win that Ramirez hasn't felt like the same player since coming back from injury, but has still made an impact on this team by leading by example in the locker room.
"As he was coming back, and we had to give him off days. He was not happy about it," Vogt said.
"He wants to play every day. He wants to give us everything that he has on any given day, and we know there are days when he is not feeling well, and he still goes out and gives 100 percent of what he has that day. It's just such a great example for young guys to see that just because you're not feeling 100 percent doesn't mean you can't go out and contribute to help the team win."
Cleveland's offense has been hot and cold at times this season, but if the Guardians are truly getting vintage Ramirez back for a potential playoff run, this could become one of the more dangerous teams in baseball come October.

item.title: [heavy.com] Dodgers GM Sends Honest Message on Tarik Skubal Trade
item.dc:creator: Owen Crisafulli
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers‘ quest to win their third straight World Series title is alive and well, as they have officially clinched the National League West division with eight games left on their schedule. For now, the team’s main goal involves getting healthy, but even if it can’t, it should still be the favorite to win it all until further notice. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers‘ quest to win their third straight World Series title is alive and well, as they have officially clinched the National League West division with eight games left on their schedule. For now, the team’s main goal involves getting healthy, but even if it can’t, it should still be the favorite to win it all until further notice.
At the trade deadline, the Dodgers did what they always do and went all-in by acquiring the reigning back-to-back American League Cy Young winner, Tarik Skubal, in a trade with the Detroit Tigers. It was almost expected that L.A. would be the team landing Skubal, but according to general manager Andrew Friedman, this was actually a move the team was hoping to avoid having to make.
Andrew Friedman Drops Truth Bomb on Dodgers’ Tarik Skubal Trade
With the Tigers failing to sign Skubal to a long-term contract extension over the offseason, he ended up being the big fish that every team wanted at the trade deadline. Of course, landing Skubal was going to require a massive haul of prospects, which is something the Dodgers always seem to have at their disposal.
Los Angeles has developed a reputation for simply being willing to go above and beyond what every other team in the majors is willing to do. Whether it involves shelling out more money for the top free agents, or giving up whatever prospects a team wants for its top player, the Dodgers are always making moves, which is why it wasn’t a surprise to see them land Skubal.
Despite that aforementioned narrative continuing to swirl around the team, Los Angeles has claimed that it didn’t want to have to make this sort of move this year. According to Friedman, the list of the Dodgers’ trade targets started and ended with Skubal, which could help explain why they were so willing to part with several of their top prospects for a guy who is set to hit the free agent market in just a couple of months.
“We looked to do everything we could over the offseason to avoid being a buyer in July, short of a real impact-type talent,” Friedman said, per Tom Verducci of Sports Illustrated. “And so, from our standpoint, our buy side list was Tarik Skubal. End of list.”
Dodgers’ All-In Mindset Could Lead MLB to a Lockout
Trading Skubal was always going to be risky for all 29 other teams in the majors because if he hits the open market, the Dodgers are going to be the favorite to sign him. Without a true salary cap in place, nothing is stopping Los Angeles from spending above and beyond what every other team is spending on its roster, and it has put that theory to the test over the past few years.
It’s gotten to the point where a lockout feels inevitable, as the Collective Bargaining Agreement will expire at the conclusion of the season, and there has been virtually no momentum towards a new deal. For now, the Dodgers are intent on winning another championship, but their actions could wind up being at the center of a very important discussion this offseason, with many folks viewing the Skubal trade as the final nail in the coffin.

item.content:encoded:
On Saturday, the New York Yankees will look to clinch a series victory when they play the second game of their series with the Diamondbacks in Arizona.
They won by a score of 9-2 on Friday night.
Paul Goldschmidt (who led off) had one hit, one walk and two runs.
Yankees Quickly Announce Paul Goldschmidt Change
For Saturday’s game, the Yankees have announced their starting lineup.
Underdog MLB wrote: “Yankees 9/19 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF L. García Jr. 1B H. Ramos RF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B R. McMahon 3B J. Caballero CF C. Schlittler SP”
Goldschmidt has been removed from the lineup.
The seven-time All-Star is in the middle of his second season playing for New York.
He is currently batting .253 with 85 hits, 18 home runs, 50 RBIs, 44 runs and one stolen base in 102 games this year.
Goldschmidt had spent the first eight years of his career with Arizona.
In that span, he made six straight All-Star Games (2013-18).
Following the Diamondbacks, he had a six-year run with the St. Louis Cardinals that saw him win the 2022 National League MVP Award.
Looking At The Yankees On Saturday
The Yankees are the second-place team in the American League East with an 89-64 record in 153 games.
They are 8-2 over their last ten games.
Currently, the Yankees are 4.0 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays.
Looking At The D-Backs On Saturday
The Diamondbacks are the third-place team in the National League West with an 80-74 record in 154 games.
They are 4-6 over their last ten games.

Prior to the first pitch of their second game against the Orioles, the Brewers announced lineup news. For Yelich fans, the news is especially important.
- LF: Jackson Chourio
- 1B: Vaughn
- C: Gary Sanchez
- SS: Cooper Pratt
- RF: Luis Lara
- 2B: David Hamilton
Starting Pitcher: Robert Gasser.
Judging from the roster for today's game, Gary Sanchez is coming in while Yelich comes out. William Contreras moves to designated hitter to make room for Sanchez.
Yelich is a 34-year-old slugger, while Sanchez is a 33-year-old catcher for the Brewers.
Looking At Christian Yelich & Gary Sanchez
Yelich is a 14-year MLB veteran who has been with the Brewers for nine seasons.
Over his career, he has been an All-Star several times, culminating in an NL MVP award in 2018. Yelich has enjoyed a solid 2026 campaign, notching 101 hits, 57 RBIs, 11 stolen bases, and 11 home runs in 112 games.
On the other hand, Sanchez has 44 hits, 35 RBIs, and 11 home runs in 83 games.
Pat Murphy on Christian Yelich
Recently, the Brewers manager has discussed Yelich's work ethic and his dedication to the game.
"I just remember he was here one night till 1 o'clock in the morning. A lot of guys in his situation, you've won MVP, you've been an all-star multiple times, you've done all the things in the game, you are 12 years in your career, and you know what: he still cares so much about the Milwaukee Brewers. That's the beauty of this whole thing…you have no idea how much this guy cares," Murphy said via a social media clip from Hunter Baumgardt.
Brewers Manager Pat Murphy reflects on a night during Christian Yelich’s tough stretch that Yeli was at the park working till 1:00am and how his care for the Milwaukee Brewers has led to him to getting back on track👇
“That’s the beauty of this whole thing.” pic.twitter.com/FkQGDmDkPJ
— Hunter Baumgardt (@hunterbonair) August 30, 2026
Whether Yelich is in the lineup or taking a night off to stay healthy for a deep playoff run, it sounds like Brewers fans are lucky to have him.

item.content:encoded:
Randy Arozarena could be eyeing a return to the AL East.
The Seattle Mariners All-Star outfielder Arozarena is “likely” to leave the team in free agency this offseason, Ryan Divish of The Seattle Times reported this week. Divish further added that Arozarena would “probably” prefer to join an East Coast team and suggested that the Boston Red Sox could potentially cut a “huge check” for him.
Arozarena, 31, is currently enjoying one of his best all-around seasons. Through 146 games for Seattle this year, Arozarena is batting .281 with 25 home runs, 75 RBIs, and 23 stolen bases. He also leads the AL with 104 runs scored and made the third All-Star team of his career this season.
But Arozarena will be hitting the open market this winter as one of the standout options in a fairly weak free agent class. That could indeed inspire somebody like the Red Sox, a team that seems to be one impact bat away from true World Series contention, to take a big swing.
Arozarena did already play in Boston’s division too as a member of the Tampa Bay Rays from 2020-24. There, Arozarena was an All-Star, an AL Rookie of the Year, and a key contributor to Tampa Bay’s 2020 World Series team as the ALCS MVP.
We heard earlier this month that the Mariners were expected to part ways with Arozarena and some other notable figures after the season. Now it appears that Seattle’s loss could be Boston’s gain (provided that the Red Sox are willing to fork over some major cash for the Cuban).
