The defending AL champion Blue Jays (76-78) are two games back in the wild-ca
item.content:encoded:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Corey Seager had an RBI double in a four-run second inning fueled by a throwing error, and the Texas Rangers beat the Toronto Blue Jays 7-1 on Friday night in the opener of a series matching AL playoff chasers.
The Rangers (77-77) reached .500 for a majors-leading 23rd time and pulled within one game of the White Sox for the third and final AL wild-card spot, although Chicago has the tiebreaker. The defending AL champion Blue Jays (76-78) are two games back in the wild-card race.
Texas also closed the gap on Houston by pulling even with the Astros atop the AL West, but the Rangers would have to win the division outright to finish ahead of their in-state rival. Houston lost to Atlanta 6-2.
The Rangers took the lead in the second on Evan Carter's bases-loaded grounder that scored Wyatt Langford, and Jake Burger also came home when shortstop Ernie Clement's throw trying to force him out at third bounced wide of the bag into foul territory. Seager made it 4-0 with his double.
Dylan Cease (11-6) walked a season-high six among his first 15 batters and was replaced with two outs in the third after throwing 38 balls and 36 strikes.
Six of the Texas runs were unearned as the Blue Jays walked 10 and had three throwing errors, two by third baseman Kazuma Okamoto.
Trevor Williams (2-0) finished with four scoreless innings after starter Kumar Rocker took a 4-0 lead into the fifth but couldn't finish and was replaced by Tyler Alexander.
Toronto's Nathan Lukes had the longest active hitting streak in the majors stopped at 13 games when he was replaced by pinch-hitter Davis Schneider in the fifth. Lukes was 0 for 2 with a deep liner that Carter, the center fielder, ran down at the wall in right center.
Up next
Blue Jays RHP José Soriano (12-7, 3.56 ERA) is set to face Texas RHP Cal Quantrill (9-5, 2.90) on Saturday.

Edmundo Sosa went 3 for 3 with a home run and a double for the Phillies (85-69), who remained tied with the Cubs for the top two wild-card spots after Chicago lost 6-4 to Cincinnati. Both teams began the day one game ahead of the San Diego Padres, who were scheduled to host Miami later Friday. Derek Hill al
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK (AP) — Juan Soto hit a three-run homer and the New York Mets kept the Philadelphia Phillies from gaining ground in the National League wild-card race with a 6-3 victory Friday night.
Edmundo Sosa went 3 for 3 with a home run and a double for the Phillies (85-69), who remained tied with the Cubs for the top two wild-card spots after Chicago lost 6-4 to Cincinnati. Both teams began the day one game ahead of the San Diego Padres, who were scheduled to host Miami later Friday.
Derek Hill also went deep and Bryson Stott had an RBI double for Philadelphia.
Soto also doubled and finished with three hits. A.J. Ewing’s two-run single capped a three-run first inning for the last-place Mets, who ended a five-game losing streak — their longest under interim manager Andy Green. Carson Benge had an RBI single in the first and reached base three times.
Francisco Lindor remained at 299 career homers after going 2 for 5 with a double.
Rookie left-hander Zac Thornton (5-5) allowed two runs and five hits in six innings. He struck out four and walked one. Thornton has permitted two runs or fewer eight times in 14 big league starts.
Dedniel Núñez got four outs for his second career save and first since July 13, 2024.
José Urquidy tossed 4 2/3 innings of scoreless bulk relief in his Phillies debut. Urquidy, designated for assignment by the Chicago White Sox on Tuesday, was claimed off waivers Thursday.
Phillies opener Tim Mayza (3-4) was charged with three runs. He threw 33 pitches but recorded just one out — the shortest outing by a Philadelphia starter since Cristopher Sánchez got only one out against the Washington Nationals on July 29, 2021.
Up next
The Mets will retire the No. 15 jersey worn by Hall of Fame center fielder Carlos Beltrán on Saturday before RHP Christian Scott (4-5, 3.76 ERA) opposes Phillies RHP Andrew Painter (3-9, 5.54).

item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays made franchise history when they gave Dylan Cease a record-setting seven-year contract in free agency for $210 million.
They surely would’ve hoped he could make history on the mound for them, too.
On Friday night, that’s what Cease did.
It just wasn’t the kind of history that the Blue Jays would’ve hoped for from Cease.
Dylan Cease Unfortunate History
Cease threw a pitching line that had never happened before in MLB history.
Against the Rangers, he went 2.2 innings, allowing three hits and walking six while giving up one earned run and striking out three.
That combination of five statistics had never happened:
🚨 PITCHERGAMI 🚨
Dylan Cease just threw a line that has NEVER happened in MLB history:
2.2 IP | 3 H | 1 ER | 6 BB | 3 K
TOR @ TEX
That’s the 389th Pitchergami of 2026 and 1 of 83,614+ unique lines on record.
— Pitchergami (@pitchergami) September 19, 2026
At first glance, it’s amazing that there are still pitching lines that have never happened before.
Then you look at this one, and it kind of makes sense.
Just in the walks and hits, Cease gave up nine baserunners while only getting eight outs. Generally, that would give up more than one earned run.
And in a past era, a pitcher that had given up only one earned run may be left in the game even with all the walks.
But everything factored together gave Cease this specific line, and it’s certainly a unique one.
Dylan Cease Trended This Way
The thing is, there was already a potential cause for concern entering the night.
A post on social media earlier in the day showed how Cease’s velocity had declined all season long.
In April, he averaged 97.8 miles per hour on his four-seam fastball
Cease kept that exact mark on his heater in May, 97.8 MPH again.
It declined to 97.4 miles per hour in June, a small enough decrease to not worry much.
Then in July, Cease was down to 96.7 MPH on his four-seam fastball on average. His August velocity was an average of 95.8 miles per hour.
And in September, Cease entered Friday night’s start at 95.3 miles per hour on average on his four-seam fastball.
It doesn’t automatically mean he’s hurt, but it also doesn’t seem like it can be ideal.
And on Friday night, Cease’s results finally reflected the potential that he’s got something a little off with him.
Fastball velocity doesn’t inherently impact walk numbers, so if you were trying to create a correlation here, it’d be more that Cease’s arm isn’t at full strength, which impacted both velocity and control.
Of course, there are other possible explanations.
All that’s clear is that Cease didn’t have it on Friday night, and it cost him.

item.content:encoded:
CLEVELAND -- - José Ramírez and rookie Travis Bazzana homered and Joey Cantillo pitched six scoreless innings as the Cleveland Guardians rallied to beat the Athletics 5-3 on Friday night and stay atop the AL Central.
Ramírez connected in the sixth inning to give the Guardians a two-run cushion. His 12th homer was also the seven-time All-Star's 1,000th RBI, making him just the second Cleveland player to reach the plateau. Earl Averill drove in 1,084 runs.
Bazzana snapped a 3-3 tie in the fifth as the Guardians came back after falling behind 3-0 in the first.
Cleveland, 18-9 since Aug. 20, came in tied with Chicago for first in the division. The White Sox hold the head-to-head tiebreaker.
Cantillo (10-9) allowed two hits in six innings after replacing opener Daniel Espino. Cantillo has not given up a run in 10 innings over his past two outings.
Hunter Gaddis and Cade Smith finished off the combined three-hitter. Smith worked the ninth for his 38th save.
Zack Gelof hit a three-run homer for the A's, who are 0-4 on their final road trip of 2026.
Bazzana put Cleveland ahead 4-3 in the fifth with his 15th homer, a 411-foot leadoff drive to center off Scott Blewett (2-1).
The Guardians had squandered early scoring chances, loading the bases in the first two innings but failing to push a run across.
Cleveland finally strung some hits together in the fourth, scoring three times off starter Mason Barnett to tie it.
Rocchio, who leads all MLB No. 9 hitters in RBI with 50, delivered a two-run double and scored on Ramírez's two-out single.
Espino opened for Cleveland and started poorly.
The right-hander walked three in the first and allowed the three-run homer to Gelof, his 19th.
Up Next
LHP Jacob Lopez (6-4, 5.02 ERA) starts Saturday for Oakland against Tanner Bibee (6-15, 4.16), who has gotten minimal support (3.05 runs per game) this season.
------

According to Jon Heyman of the New York Post, Judge will be eligible to return for the final game of the regular season. The Yankees removed Judge from Wednesday’s los
item.content:encoded:
On Friday, the New York Yankees announced they will place star outfielder Aaron Judge on the 10-day injured list on Saturday with a right calf strain.
From Bryan Hoch on MLB.com: Aaron Judge will be placed on the 10-day injured list tomorrow with a right calf strain, the Yankees say. A corresponding move will be made at that time.
According to Jon Heyman of the New York Post, Judge will be eligible to return for the final game of the regular season.
The Yankees removed Judge from Wednesday’s loss to the Minnesota Twins at Target Field in the sixth inning due to his calf injury.
“I tried to play it off and see how long we can go because these games are important down the stretch,” Judge said. “Talking it over I thought it’d be the right move to come out so we don’t cost the team on the field or cost the team on the basepaths.” Before the Yankees’ game against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field in Phoenix on Friday, Yankees outfielder Cody Bellinger was asked about Judge’s injury.
New York Yankees Star Cody Bellinger Makes Statement on Aaron Judge’s Injury
“Missing Judge, it hurts. We all know he’s the best hitter in the game,” Bellinger said to Hoch. “For us in here, our mindset is, we’re going to have to find a way. I think the talent in this locker room speaks for itself. I’m fully confident that we have enough talent in here that we can go out and win, and beat anybody.”
Aaron Judge has missed most of the season with a right rib stress fracture. New York placed him on the IL on June 2. He didn’t return until Sept. 7.
Since making his MLB debut in 2016, Judge has slashed 291/.410/.610 with 386 home runs and 871 RBI. He has won three AL MVP Awards.
New York Yankees Right Now
The Yankees began a three-game series against the Diamondbacks in Arizona on Friday night.

item.description: CLEVELAND -- As the Progressive Field crowd roared around him, José Ramírez paused and leaned back in the left-handed batter’s box to admire his work. item.content:encoded:
CLEVELAND -- As the Progressive Field crowd roared around him, José Ramírez paused and leaned back in the left-handed batter’s box to admire his work. There was no doubt where the baseball he launched to right field was headed.
That image has played on repeat over the past 14 seasons. This time, it came with a heavy dose of history, and it was well-timed as the Guardians continue to push for the postseason.
Ramírez tallied his 1,000th career RBI on Friday by launching his 297th career home run, in the sixth inning of the Guardians’ matchup with the A’s in the opener of a three-game series. The superstar third baseman joined Earl Averill (1,084) as the only players in Cleveland franchise history to hit the RBI milestone.
The Guardians improved to 79-75 with their third straight win. They entered Friday with the same record as the White Sox, but Chicago technically led the division because it holds the tiebreaker over Cleveland after winning the season series.
It means the Guardians must finish with more wins than the Sox to win the Central for a third straight year. Ramírez helped; his towering blast went a Statcast-projected 401 feet and had a 102.4 mph exit velocity.
Ramírez, who turned 34 years old on Thursday, is now just the 12th active player with 1,000 career RBIs, joining Freddie Freeman, Paul Goldschmidt, Nolan Arenado, Manny Machado, Giancarlo Stanton, Andrew McCutchen, Carlos Santana, Bryce Harper, Salvador Perez, Mike Trout and Eugenio Suárez.
The home run was Ramírez’s first since Aug. 30 and just his 12th this season. He entered Friday with an uncharacteristic .683 OPS in 117 games, in an injury-impacted campaign after he missed five weeks following left hamate surgery.
Ramírez has been dealt with the effects of that procedure since he came off the injured list on July 22. On Friday, he reminded us he’s always just one swing away from impacting a game in a big way.

Here are the takeaways... -- Mets left-handed starter Zac Thornton plunked leadoff batter Kyle Schwarber on a 3-2 count to get the game started. The rookie battled back, striking out Trea Turner and Bryce Harper before Mets first baseman Brett Baty made a diving stop on a Luis Arraez grounder down the line to put away the third out. -- Southpaw Tim Mayza served as the bullpen opener for Philadelphia, and Francisco Lin
item.content:encoded:
The Mets (70-84) defeated the Philadelphia Phillies (85-69) by a score of 6-3.
Here are the takeaways...
-- Mets left-handed starter Zac Thornton plunked leadoff batter Kyle Schwarber on a 3-2 count to get the game started. The rookie battled back, striking out Trea Turner and Bryce Harper before Mets first baseman Brett Baty made a diving stop on a Luis Arraez grounder down the line to put away the third out.
-- Southpaw Tim Mayza served as the bullpen opener for Philadelphia, and Francisco Lindor jumped all over him with a leadoff double. With one out, Bo Bichette worked a 10-pitch at-bat, culminating in a single to center field which moved Lindor up to third base. Carson Benge kept the line moving and drove in Lindor with an opposite-field single. Mark Vientos was walked to load the bases, and Phillies manager Don Mattingly pulled Mayza for right-handed reliever Jose Urquidy. A.J. Ewing roped an Urquidy fastball for a double, which scored two runs. Urquidy retired the next two Mets batters to limit the damage to three runs.
-- In the second inning, Ewing got turned around on a deep line drive to center, failing to haul in the RBI double for Bryson Stott, which cut the Mets' lead to 3-1. In the bottom half of the inning, Juan Soto doubled into the left-center field gap with two outs, but Urquidy struck out Bichette to end the threat.
-- With two outs away in the top of the sixth, Phillies left fielder Edmundo Sosa blasted a solo shot to left field, his third hit of the night. Excluding Sosa, Thornton allowed just two hits. He struck out four and walked one, allowing two earned runs across 87 pitches.
-- Soto took a hanging breaking ball thrown by Phillies right-hander Orion Kerkering 428 feet for a two-out three-run homer in the bottom of the sixth. Soto's 26th tater of 2026 put the Mets up 6-2.
-- Philadelphia center fielder Derek Hill responded with a solo home run off of Mets left-handed reliever Nate Lavender in the top of the seventh. Lavender persevered, retiring each of the next four batters he faced, before handing the ball to Dedniel Núñez to record the third out of the eighth. In the bottom half of the frame, Bichette grounded into a double play with the bases loaded. Núñez handled the ninth inning and retired the side to earn the first save of his season - and second save of his career - to seal the 6-3 win for the Mets.
Game MVP: Juan Soto
Soto notched his third game with multiple extra-base hits in September, going 3-for-5 with a double and a three-run homer. It was also Soto's third game of the season with at least three hits.
Highlights
What's next
The Mets play the Phillies in the third game of the four-game home series on Saturday at 4:10 p.m. on SNY. They will honor 2026 Baseball Hall of Fame inductee Carlos Beltrán.
New York will send out Christian Scott (3.76 ERA, 1.26 WHIP in 105.1 IP).
Philadelphia is set to start fellow right-hander Andrew Painter (5.54 ERA, 1.44 WHIP in 115.1 IP).

item.dc:creator: Sportsnet Staff
item.description: Things didn't go as planned for the Toronto Blue Jays and ace Dylan Cease to open their pivotal series against the Texas Rangers. Cease battled both his command and velocity throughout his start against the Rangers and wasn't able to complete the third inning before turning the ball over to manager John Schneider. The 30-year-old walked off the mound after 2.2 innings of work, having allowed three hits, four runs (one earned), and six walks while striking out three. It marked his shortest appear
item.content:encoded:
Things didn't go as planned for the Toronto Blue Jays and ace Dylan Cease to open their pivotal series against the Texas Rangers.
Cease battled both his command and velocity throughout his start against the Rangers and wasn't able to complete the third inning before turning the ball over to manager John Schneider.
The 30-year-old walked off the mound after 2.2 innings of work, having allowed three hits, four runs (one earned), and six walks while striking out three.
It marked his shortest appearance of the season.
Cease worked around some trouble early, inducing an inning-ending double play off the bat of Brandon Nimmo in the first after issuing a pair of one-out walks.
But the free passes and an untimely error cost the righty in the second.
After loading the bases with one out in the frame, Rangers centre-fielder Evan Carter chopped a ground ball up the middle that took a weird bounce off the mound and went straight to Blue Jays shortstop Ernie Clement.
Clement opted to try for an out at third, but his throw hit Jake Burger in the back and caromed down the left-field line, allowing two runs to score on the play.
Texas then added two extra runs on a sacrifice fly from Ezequiel Duran and an RBI double by Corey Seager.
Cease came back out for the third but saw his pitch count climb as he loaded the bases once again on a pair of walks and a Nicky Lopez single. He did bounce back to get the second out of the inning by striking out Elias Díaz before Brendan Cellucci entered and escaped the jam unscathed with a punchout of his own.
When all was said and done for Cease, he had tossed 74 pitches and 36 strikes while averaging 93.6 m.p.h. with his fastball — 3.3 m.p.h. slower than his season average of 96.9. — continuing a troubling trend of diminished velocity for the all-star.
Toronto had bumped Cease's scheduled start up a day so that he was opening this series in Arlington on regular rest, rather than leveraging Thursday's off-day to give the eight-year veteran an extra day and have him pitch on turn in Saturday's contest.

item.content:encoded:
El tabasqueño Jesús Broca y Biloxi Shuckers jugarán la final de campeonato de la Southern League
El serpentinero registró marca de 3 victorias y 6 derrotas en 38 apariciones, con 58.1 entradas lanzadas, un salvamento y 56 ponches
- Alexis Santamaría
- Septiembre 18, 2026 - 07:22 p.m.
- DEPORTES
El pitcher tabasqueño Jesús Broca continúa destacando con la sucursal de Doble "A" de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee, al avanzar a la final de campeonato de la Southern League con los Biloxi Shuckers.
El orgullo de la ranchería Boquerón atraviesa un buen momento con el conjunto de Biloxi Shuckers, que disputará el título ante los Rocket City Trash Pandas.
En la temporada regular, el serpentinero tabasqueño registró marca de 3 victorias y 6 derrotas en 38 apariciones, con 58.1 entradas lanzadas, un salvamento y 56 ponches. Además, terminó con una efectividad de 5.25 carreras limpias admitidas.
Los Biloxi Shuckers concluyeron el calendario regular con récord de 66-68, para un porcentaje de .493 en ganados y perdidos; sin embargo, lograron avanzar a la serie por el campeonato de la categoría Doble "A" de las Ligas Menores.
El primer encuentro de la final entre ambas novenas se disputará el 20 de septiembre en el Keesler Federal Park, casa de los Biloxi Shuckers.

Toronto is beginning a three-game road series against the Texas Rangers on the road on Friday. The Blue Jays have 9 games left and are 2 games back of a Wild Card spot. The Blue Jays will start Dylan Cease on Friday, with Jose Soriano getting the ball on Saturday. Dylan Cease Comments on Jose Soriano Before the Blue Jays began their three-game series against the Rangers, Cease was asked about Soria
item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays pulled off a blockbuster move at the trade deadline to acquire Jose Soriano.
Toronto is beginning a three-game road series against the Texas Rangers on the road on Friday. The Blue Jays have 9 games left and are 2 games back of a Wild Card spot.
The Blue Jays will start Dylan Cease on Friday, with Jose Soriano getting the ball on Saturday.
Dylan Cease Comments on Jose Soriano
Before the Blue Jays began their three-game series against the Rangers, Cease was asked about Soriano.
Soriano and Cease have formed a two-headed monster atop the Blue Jays rotation. With the Blue Jays, Soriano has had success, and Cease admits he’s impressed with him and his stuff.
“Soriano will step up. He’s nasty. He sits upper 90s with a bowling ball sinker and nasty off-speed, so every time he takes the ball, I feel really good about it,” Cease said, via Casino.org. “Anyone that takes the ball now will be a difference maker and has a chance to be a difference maker. Everyone in the team knows where we’re at. Everyone knows that every pitch is important, that every game is important, so we’ll see who steps up and how it all plays out.”
With the Blue Jays, Soriano is 3-1 with a 4.27 ERA in 8 starts. Although the numbers aren’t as dominant as Toronto may want, he is still an impact pitcher for the team.
Toronto Blue Jays Right Now
The Blue Jays enter their road series against the Rangers 2 games back of the Cleveland Guardians for the final Wild Card spot.
Toronto is also tied with the Rangers, so this series is pivotal and Cease said the Blue Jays remain confident in their group.
“I think we feel great,” Cease said. “We don’t ever go into any game or any series not expecting to do well. We have been playing well in the second half of the season and I believe we’ve had a lot of improvement in our play. We’ve genuinely played good baseball, so I think we’re staying level-headed and we know what we’ve got to do. We can still make the playoffs. I think that you have to have that mindset. You have to have that belief. It doesn’t pay to be pessimistic.
“We’re going out every day and we’re fighting hard, and to be honest with you, we feel like we’ve fought hard all year. It obviously hasn’t been our year in a lot of ways, and we haven’t done what we needed to do and want to do for a lot of the season, but the fact that we’re still in it and we’re still close really says it all. We’re all just taking it day by day and continuing to not give up that fight. Of course, if we win the series it’s going to put us in a way better position than not. I truly mean I’m going to treat every single game the same the rest of the way. Every single game that you ever play is a must-win for us.”
The Blue Jays are 76-77.

item.content:encoded:
Fernando Tatis Jr. pasa de un inicio para el olvido a una hazaña inédita en MLB
Después de pasar sus primeros 55 partidos de 2026 sin conectar un jonrón, Fernando Tatis Jr. encontró su poder y llegó a 23 cuadrangulares en los siguientes 94 encuentros
La temporada 2026 parecía convertirse en una de las más complicadas de la carrera de Fernando Tatis Jr.. El estelar dominicano comenzó el año sin poder sacar la pelota del parque y llegó a acumular 55 partidos consecutivos sin conectar un cuadrangular, una sequía especialmente llamativa para uno de los principales bateadores de los Padres de San Diego.
Sin embargo, cuando finalmente encontró el batazo que necesitaba, todo cambió. Tatis Jr. conectó su primer jonrón de la campaña el 30 de mayo, ante los Rockies de Colorado, y a partir de ese momento comenzó una transformación ofensiva que terminó convirtiéndose en una hazaña inédita en las Grandes Ligas.
El cuadrangular que puso fin a la sequía fue un auténtico cañonazo. El dominicano envió la pelota a 451 pies, un batazo que marcó el comienzo de su recuperación ofensiva.
Desde entonces, Tatis comenzó a acumular jonrones hasta alcanzar una cifra que ningún jugador había conseguido anteriormente: 23 cuadrangulares en un periodo de 94 partidos después de no conectar ninguno en sus primeros 55 encuentros.
De acuerdo con los reportes estadísticos publicados esta semana, Tatis Jr. se convirtió en el primer jugador en la historia de MLB en lograr esa combinación.
La transformación resulta todavía más llamativa porque no se trató simplemente de una racha de poder. El jardinero dominicano recuperó también su consistencia en el plato y se convirtió nuevamente en uno de los principales motores ofensivos de San Diego.
TATIS ENCONTRÓ SU PODER CUANDO MÁS LO NECESITABAN LOS PADRES
El jonrón número 23 llegó el 15 de septiembre ante los Rockies, en Coors Field. Tatis abrió el partido con un batazo hacia el jardín izquierdo que recorrió 454 pies, con una velocidad de salida de 106.5 mph y un ángulo de lanzamiento de 29 grados, de acuerdo con Statcast.
Un día antes ya había demostrado nuevamente su poder con otro batazo monumental: un cuadrangular de dos carreras de 449 pies y 111.1 mph de velocidad de salida.
El momento de Tatis coincide con el repunte colectivo de los Padres. San Diego llegó a encadenar ocho victorias consecutivas, una racha que terminó el 16 de septiembre con una derrota de 9-3 ante Colorado.
Tatis Jr. ha explicado que detrás de su recuperación no existe un secreto especial, sino trabajo constante, disciplina y cuidado físico.
El dominicano reconoció que estaba satisfecho con el proceso que había seguido incluso cuando los resultados ofensivos todavía no aparecían. Su enfoque, explicó, consistió en continuar trabajando de la misma manera y cuidar todos los aspectos de su preparación.
También reconoció la responsabilidad que representa su contrato de 340 millones de dólares, uno de los acuerdos económicos más importantes de las Grandes Ligas.
Para Tatis, esa responsabilidad se ha convertido en una razón adicional para presentarse cada día y buscar el mejor rendimiento posible con los Padres.
LOS NÚMEROS RESPALDAN LA RECUPERACIÓN
Al acercarse el cierre de la temporada regular, los números muestran hasta qué punto cambió la campaña del dominicano.
De acuerdo con las estadísticas oficiales disponibles, Tatis Jr. suma 23 jonrones, 78 carreras impulsadas, 35 bases robadas y un promedio de .286, además de un OPS de .816, en 150 partidos.
Esos números también reflejan una de sus principales características: su capacidad para aportar en diferentes facetas. Además de su producción de poder, Tatis ha agregado velocidad y presencia en las bases, con 35 robos durante la temporada.
Jackson Merrill también ha sido importante para San Diego. El joven jardinero acumula 25 cuadrangulares y 83 carreras impulsadas, cifras que lo colocan como otra de las piezas ofensivas relevantes de los Padres.
SAN DIEGO PELEA POR LLEGAR A OCTUBRE
El despertar de Tatis se produjo en un momento particularmente importante para los Padres.
Después de su espectacular racha de ocho triunfos, San Diego llegó al 16 de septiembre con marca de 82-69, a un juego de los Phillies por el segundo boleto de Wild Card de la Liga Nacional y con ventaja de 2.5 juegos sobre los Diamondbacks en la lucha por el último lugar disponible.
La derrota ante Colorado frenó la racha, pero no modificó el escenario de una carrera por los comodines que se mantiene abierta en las últimas semanas de la temporada.
Y en esa pelea, la versión actual de Tatis Jr. puede resultar especialmente importante para los Padres. El dominicano pasó de protagonizar una de las sequías de poder más llamativas del inicio de temporada a escribir su nombre en los libros de récords de MLB.
55 partidos sin jonrón. Después, 23 cuadrangulares en 94 encuentros. Una combinación que, hasta ahora, ningún otro bateador había conseguido en la historia de las Grandes Ligas.
Desde entonces, Tatis comenzó a acumular jonrones hasta alcanzar una cifra que ningún jugador había conseguido anteriormente: 23 cuadrangulares en un periodo de 94 partidos después de no conectar ninguno en sus primeros 55 encuentros.

De acuerdo con las estadísticas oficiales disponibles, Tatis Jr. suma 23 jonrones, 78 carreras impulsadas, 35 bases robadas y un promedio de .286, además de un OPS de .816, en 150 partidos.
Esos números también reflejan una de sus principales características: su capacidad para aportar en diferentes facetas. Además de su producción de poder, Tatis ha agregado velocidad y presencia en las bases, con 35 robos durante la temporada.
Jackson Merrill también ha sido importante para San Diego. El joven jardinero acumula 25 cuadrangulares y 83 carreras impulsadas, cifras que lo colocan como otra de las piezas ofensivas relevantes de los Padres.
SAN DIEGO PELEA POR LLEGAR A OCTUBRE
El despertar de Tatis se produjo en un momento particularmente importante para los Padres.
Después de su espectacular racha de ocho triunfos, San Diego llegó al 16 de septiembre con marca de 82-69, a un juego de los Phillies por el segundo boleto de Wild Card de la Liga Nacional y con ventaja de 2.5 juegos sobre los Diamondbacks en la lucha por el último lugar disponible.
La derrota ante Colorado frenó la racha, pero no modificó el escenario de una carrera por los comodines que se mantiene abierta en las últimas semanas de la temporada.
Y en esa pelea, la versión actual de Tatis Jr. puede resultar especialmente importante para los Padres. El dominicano pasó de protagonizar una de las sequías de poder más llamativas del inicio de temporada a escribir su nombre en los libros de récords de MLB.
55 partidos sin jonrón. Después, 23 cuadrangulares en 94 encuentros. Una combinación que, hasta ahora, ningún otro bateador había conseguido en la historia de las Grandes Ligas.

item.content:encoded:
La temporada regular de la MLB 2026 entra en su recta final y la pelea por los boletos a los Playoffs comienza a tomar forma. En medio de esta definición, varios peloteros mexicanos y mexicoamericanos mantienen vivas sus aspiraciones de llegar a la postemporada con sus respectivas organizaciones.
En la Liga Americana hay nombres que ya tienen prácticamente asegurado el escenario de octubre, mientras que otros todavía deben afrontar una intensa batalla por los puestos de comodín. Entre ellos aparecen jugadores que han tenido un papel importante durante la campaña y que buscan convertirse en representantes de México durante los Playoffs.
¿Qué mexicanos ya tienen encaminado su boleto?
Entre los jugadores que tienen su lugar asegurado destaca Jonathan Aranda, infielder tijuanense de los Tampa Bay Rays, franquicia que matemáticamente consiguió su clasificación a la postemporada y que se mantiene en la parte alta de la División Este de la Liga Americana.
Otro nombre que se encuentra en plena pelea es Jarren Durán, jardinero mexicoamericano de los Boston Red Sox. El pelotero forma parte de una novena que pelea por mantenerse en la zona de clasificación del joven circuito y que apunta a disputar la Serie de Comodines si consigue sostener su posición.
Por su parte, Alejandro Kirk continúa siendo una de las principales referencias mexicanas en las Grandes Ligas. El receptor de los Toronto Blue Jays afronta con su equipo una cerrada lucha por ingresar a los Playoffs de la Liga Americana, con cada partido de la recta final teniendo un peso importante en sus aspiraciones.
La pelea también está en la Liga Nacional
En el Viejo Circuito también hay varios peloteros con posibilidades de disputar la postemporada. Alek Thomas, jardinero mexicoamericano de los Arizona Diamondbacks, se encuentra involucrado en la cerrada pelea por los últimos boletos de comodín de la Liga Nacional.
Los San Diego Padres también cuentan con representación mexicana con Jeremiah Estrada, relevista mexicoamericano que forma parte del bullpen de una organización que se mantiene en puestos que actualmente entregarían un boleto a la postemporada mediante el comodín.
Mientras tanto, Javier Assad vive una situación favorable con los Chicago Cubs. El pitcher tijuanense forma parte de una novena que tiene prácticamente encaminada su clasificación, con los Cachorros ubicados en una posición privilegiada dentro de la carrera por los Playoffs de la Liga Nacional.
Otros jugadores también permanecen atentos a la definición de la temporada. Taijuan Walker, con los Philadelphia Phillies, así como JoJo Romero y Ramón Urías, con los St. Louis Cardinals, buscan mantener a sus respectivos equipos dentro de la conversación por los últimos lugares disponibles en la Nacional.

item.content:encoded:
La temporada 2026 de las Grandes Ligas entra en su tramo definitivo y la carrera por el Cy Young de la Liga Nacional comienza a tomar forma. Mientras algunos lanzadores todavía buscan cerrar fuerte para meterse en la conversación, Jacob Misiorowski ha conseguido separarse del resto gracias a una campaña en la que ha mostrado un nivel sobresaliente con los Milwaukee Brewers.
¿Por qué Jacob Misiorowski es el favorito al Cy Young?
Misiorowski ha sido particularmente consistente durante 2026 y encabeza a los pitchers abridores de MLB en varias categorías relevantes. Su dominio incluso se ha mantenido durante el último tramo de la campaña, una situación que ha fortalecido sus argumentos de cara al premio.
Durante agosto, el lanzador de los Brewers registró una efectividad de 2.32, cifra que representó su segundo peor registro mensual de toda la temporada. Su peor mes fue abril, cuando terminó con 3.58 de efectividad, lo que refleja la regularidad que ha mantenido conforme avanzó el calendario.
Uno de los lanzadores que todavía puede competir por el reconocimiento es Cristopher Sánchez, de los Philadelphia Phillies. El zurdo fue considerado uno de los principales favoritos al inicio de la carrera después de encadenar 50 entradas y dos tercios sin permitir carrera entre finales de abril y principios de junio. Aunque posteriormente perdió algo de terreno, sus números lo mantienen como un contendiente relevante.
Sánchez, de 29 años, lidera MLB en victorias con una marca de 16-4 y además presume una efectividad de 2.52, WHIP de 1.19 y 202 ponches en 175.1 entradas. Su desempeño lo mantiene dentro de la conversación, aunque ahora deberá aprovechar las últimas semanas de la temporada para intentar recortar distancia.
Otro nombre que aparece entre los contendientes es Chris Sale, de los Atlanta Braves. El veterano zurdo cuenta con experiencia y argumentos suficientes para mantenerse en la disputa, aunque Misiorowski ha conseguido colocarse por delante del grupo gracias al dominio mostrado a lo largo de la campaña.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, el caballo negro
Yoshinobu Yamamoto representa una alternativa que no puede descartarse. El japonés se ha convertido en una pieza constante de la rotación de los Los Angeles Dodgers y sus números reflejan el nivel que ha alcanzado durante su segunda temporada en las Grandes Ligas.
Después de 24 aperturas, Yamamoto tiene marca de 12-8, efectividad de 2.56 y un espectacular WHIP de 0.89. Además, suma 153 ponches y únicamente 36 bases por bolas en 158 entradas de trabajo. Son estadísticas que en otras temporadas podrían colocarlo directamente entre los favoritos.

item.content:encoded:
Livvy Dunne Dismisses Fantasy Baseball Manager's Paul Skenes Request With 'South Park' Meme
Don't bother Livvy Dunne with complaints about how Paul Skenes is impacting your fantasy baseball team.
After Dunne posted a TikTok video showing her doing gymnastics exercises, a fan in the comments decided to write a snarky message asking her to tell Skenes to "do good for my fantasy" team.
Rather than let the message slide, Dunne replied with a South Park meme featuring Stan saying "Dude, we don't care."
TOP NEWS
Mets 1B Has Memory Loss After Collision
🚨 Judge Going Back on IL
Lakers' Dodgers Jersey Promo🔥
It's hard to argue Skenes hasn't helped fantasy teams this season. He's obviously not pitching as well as he did in 2024 or 2025, but his 3.78 ERA and 185 strikeouts in 162 innings is far from terrible.
Sure, Skenes only ranks 32nd among all starting pitchers in total fantasy points entering Friday. He is right around Tarik Skubal, Jacob deGrom and Nolan McLean.
This has been a strange season for many pitchers. Not many people would have guessed in April that Jesús Luzardo, Drew Rasmussen and Parker Messick were going to be top-eight fantasy starters.

item.content:encoded:
The Angels announced that the MRI on the injured pitching arm of left-hander Samy Natera Jr. revealed no structural damage and that he will not require surgery.

He’s still looking at a six-week recovery window, but he’ll be able to complete his normal offseason routine without issue and should be ready to go for the start of spring training. He finished the 2025 campaign with a solid 3.13 ERA, 1.11 WHIP and a 48/13 K/BB ratio over 31 2/3 innings out of the Angels’ bullpen.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are out West on Friday night to begin a weekend series with the Arizona Diamondbacks.
Ahead of the matchup, New York received some bad news as superstar Aaron Judge heads back to the IL with a calf strain. Yankees manager Aaron Boone also made a few notable changes to his starting lineup for the series opener.
Yankees Announce Paul Goldschmidt Decision
After spending pretty much the entire season in a platoon role and not starting the last time the Yankees played on Wednesday, veteran slugger Paul Goldschmidt is in the lineup Friday, starting at first base and batting leadoff.
He’ll bat in front of Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, and Ben Rice, who will move into the cleanup spot.
Here’s the full Yankees lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Yankees 9/18 P. Goldschmidt 1B C. Bellinger LF H. Ramos RF B. Rice DH A. Rosario 3B S. Jones CF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B G. Cole SP.”
Yankees 9/18
P. Goldschmidt 1B
C. Bellinger LF
H. Ramos RF
B. Rice DH
A. Rosario 3B
S. Jones CF
G. Lombard Jr. SS
A. Wells C
A. Volpe 2B
G. Cole SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 18, 2026
Goldschmidt’s 2026 Season
In his 16th MLB season and his second as a member of the Yankees, Goldschmidt has appeared in 101 games for New York, and across 332 at-bats, he’s hitting .253 with 42 runs, 84 hits, 18 home runs, and 50 RBIs while slugging .458 and maintaining a .773 OPS.
Looking at the Yankees
New York enters Friday’s contest with the D-backs holding an 88-64 overall record. They sit 5.0 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for the AL East division lead and the No. 1 overall seed in the American League.
Currently, the Yankees hold the top Wild Card spot, and if the season ended today, they’d host a best-of-three series at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx against, coincidentally enough, the Boston Red Sox in what would mark a rematch of the 2025 postseason.

item.content:encoded:
This is the second-to-last MLB Friday if the 2026 regular season, meaning this is my penultimate home run picks post this year. Philadelphia's Kyle Schwarber has hit 45 homers this year and likely will win his first MLB home run crown and third in the NL. It is worth noting that likely NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs has 44 homers now, but Schwarber is the -400 overall favorite to lead the league, though he was -1800 a couple of days ago.
Regarding MLB tonight, I will say the Rockies are home at hitter-happy Coors Field and starting one of the worst pitchers in the majors in Gabriel Hughes (0-8, 6.37 ERA). But he's facing Seattle, and I don't much like any of the disappointing Mariners to go yard -- plus none have faced Hughes previously. Cincinnati is also home at hitter-friendly Great American Ball Park against the Cubs, but there are two good starting pitchers in that one: Clay Holmes and Chase Burns.
Those who want to get into , particularly home run prop betting, need to take a look at what I'm playing for Friday's games. Over the past four MLB seasons, I'm up $1,681 on MLB picks. You can find more of my picks at SportsLine, and in the member-exclusive SportsLine Discord server, a community of sports betting enthusiasts and SportsLine experts.
Last Friday, my home run picks were Austin Riley at +490 and Brewers' Jackson Chourio at +398. Riley went yard in the bottom of the seventh against the Phillies, so that was nice. Milwaukee scored 20 runs against Cincinnati and Chourio had four hits, but none were homers. Remember, all my HR plays mean I like Over 1.5 total bases even better at the .
Top MLB home run picks for Friday, Sept. 18
- Nolan Arenado, Diamondbacks (+630, DraftKings)
- Mike Yastrzemski, Braves (+630, FanDuel)
Nolan Arenado, Diamondbacks (+630, DraftKings)
An important series in the desert opens tonight, and I'm sure there will be sellouts all weekend as the New York Yankees make a rare visit to Phoenix with a 9:40 ET first pitch. There are no weather concerns as Chase Field has a usually-closed retractable roof. It's not out of the question this could be a World Series preview. New York will be in the AL playoffs, most likely as the AL's top wild card team. Arizona has work to do to earn the NL's last wild card spot over San Diego.
And we get a Hall-of-Fame-caliber matchup in the bottom of the first in Yankees right-hander Gerrit Cole facing Diamondbacks third baseman Nolan Arenado. The one reason Cole might not get to Cooperstown is because his career is cut a bit short after injuries cost the 2023 Cy Young winner a chunk of the 2024 season and all of 2025. The 36-year-old righty has been moderately back in form this year at 8-9 with a 3.67 ERA. but has also allowed 20 homers in 20 starts.
Perhaps Cole is tiring as he has been ravaged for seven homers in back-to-back losses, allowing nine runs and 15 hits over 11 1/3 innings. In his most recent start against the Mets, Cole managed only three swings and misses, none generated by Cole's 38 fastballs.
There is no doubt Arenado will be headed to Cooperstown as arguably a top-10 third baseman in MLB history as a 10-time All-Star, eight-time Gold Glover, five-time Silver Slugger Award winner and three-time NL home run leader. The 35-year-old has one year left on that eight-year, $260 million contract originally signed with the Rockies in 2019. Arenado's 26 homers this season, his first with Arizona, are his most since 26 in 2023 with the Cardinals. He has hit 15 of those 26 at home and is 10-for-22 in his career off Cole with three homers and two doubles, good for a slugging percentage of .955.
Perhaps also consider a longshot flier on Snakes catcher James McCann, even though he only has five homers and doesn't play all the time. McCann is 6-for-14 with three doubles and a homer career off Cole.
Mike Yastrzemski, Braves (+630, FanDuel)
It's a matchup of division leaders tonight to open a series as Atlanta visits Houston with an 8:10 ET first pitch, and the Daikin Park retractable roof is usually closed. These clubs are division leaders in very different senses. The Braves will win the NL East, while the Astros are neck-and-neck with the Rangers in the AL West and could miss the postseason entirely.
The Braves already did the Astros a solid for this series by opting to skip ace Chris Sale in it. That somewhat hints to me what Atlanta's motivation is the rest of the way as it apparently will not push overly hard to try and earn the NL's No. 2 seed and that first-round bye.
Atlanta outfielder Mike Yastrzemski is not having a good first year with the Braves, hitting .228 with 10 homers and a slugging percentage of .377. He has slipped into a platoon role, pretty much only starting against right-handers as a lefty hitter; all 10 homers are against right-handers.
But Yastrzemski homered Monday to snap a power drought (23 games) and is 4-for-10 career with a double, triple and homer (1.000 slugging) in his career off Houston starting pitcher Peter Lambert (8-9, 3.71 ERA). The righty has surrendered 14 dingers.

item.content:encoded:
He's back, Chicago Cubs fans. According to the Chicago Tribune's Meghan Montemurro, the Cubs activated shortstop Dansby Swanson from the injured list before Friday night's game against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park in Cincinnati, Ohio.
The Cubs optioned infielder BJ Murray Jr. as a corresponding move.
Via Montemurro on X:
Dansby Swanson has been activated from the IL.
BJ Murray Jr. optioned to Triple-A Iowa.
Chicago Cubs Activate SS Dansby Swanson Before Reds Series
Swanson had been on the injured list since Aug. 17 with a left oblique strain.
Before landing on the IL, Swanson posted 3.1 bWAR and a .216/.300/.404 slash line with 18 home runs and 66 RBI over 119 games this season.
Looking at Chicago Cubs SS Dansby Swanson
The Cubs signed Swanson to a seven-year, $177 million contract in Dec. 2022 after he spent seven seasons with the Atlanta Braves.
Since joining the Cubs, Swanson has posted 16.9 bWAR and a .238/.310/.407 slash line with 80 home runs and 289 RBI.
In his 11-year MLB career, Swanson has posted 31.7 bWAR and a .248/.317/.413 slash line with 182 home runs, 253 doubles, 24 triples and 700 RBI.
Chicago Cubs Right Now
The Cubs are the first NL Wild Card team with an 85-68 record. They are tied for the top spot with the Philadelphia Phillies.
Chicago lost six of its last 10 games. The Cubs are coming off a 2-1 series win over the Atlanta Braves.
Friday's game between the Cubs and Reds is scheduled to begin at 5:40 p.m. CDT.

item.title: [CBS Sports] Ups and Downs: Alex Bregman's big second half includes celebrating his horse's win with Cubs teammates

The timing was perfect with the off day lining up just before a three-game series in Cincinnati, roughly a 90-minute drive from Louisville, h
item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman has been one of the best hitters in baseball in the second half of the 2026 season, and his hot streak extended from the field to the track. Bregman's horse won a race at Churchill Downs Thursday night, giving him and the Cubs reason to celebrate on a day off. Bregman had his entire team with him on a bus trip. The timing was perfect with the off day lining up just before a three-game series in Cincinnati, roughly a 90-minute drive from Louisville, home of Churchill Downs.
"It helps build the camaraderie, and it's fun," Bregman said. "I just think it's good to get the whole group together and having fun. That's what it's all about. Building that team chemistry, and it was a great time.
"That was probably a core memory for me right there. We've won probably 25 or 30 races, but that was the most meaningful. In terms of the size of the race, that was probably the smallest one we've ever won, but it was probably the most memorable because of all the guys being there."
Bregman's horse, Act of Parliament, was a winner with jockey Axel Concepcion. The Cubs' instagram account shared an 11-slide update of all the fun, which included second-year reliever Ryan Rolison dressed up in a horse costume, which he estimated felt like 100 degrees.
"Everyone was just going crazy watching the videos," said Rolison, who noted he would reuse the costume for Halloween. "We put the jockey up on our shoulders and I think he enjoyed that. Pedro [Ramírez] was walking me around by my ear. That was quite the experience. It was a great time. It was awesome."
Bregman isn't alone in his love for the horse track, as Cubs manager Craig Counsell also loved it.
"We just had a fun day, that's the big thing," Counsell said "Churchill Downs is a historic place, like Wrigley Field. It's like a Wrigley Field for horse racing. It was fun to introduce a bunch of guys on the team to a different world that they don't get to see and we got to hang out outside of baseball."
"It was cool to see, Breggy and Counsell love their horse races," said utility man Matt Shaw. "And for us to see and experience that. The horses were beautiful, the place was beautiful, it was really cool."
As noted, Bregman's hot streak is happening on and off the field.
Heading into Friday, Bregman in the second half of the season is hitting .305/.384/.623 with 17 homers and 47 RBI. He trails only his teammate and NL MVP favorite Pete Crow-Armstrong in second-half WAR in all of baseball. He's second in slugging (again, to PCA), fourth in home runs and second (again, to PCA) in RBI.
All this came after a very disappointing first half, but Bregman puts in the work.
"He's just a relentless competitor," Counsell said. "We throw around the term 'baseball junkie' but that's just what he is. I joked the other day that he doesn't sleep, but I don't know if he sleeps. He's always looking for ways to get an advantage. It's more hours of the day than I have. That's just who he is. He's great at it. He loves doing it and it's fun to see."
The Cubs, who entered the weekend in possession of the National League's top wild-card spot with nine games remaining, hope to add a lot more fun and core memories in the 2026 postseason.

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- Two days after completing simulated game-like activities at Wrigley Field, Cubs shortstop Dansby Swanson was activated from the 10-day injured list and started ninth in the lineup against the Reds on Friday night at Great American Ball Park.
Swanson missed 28 games because of a left oblique strain. At the time of the injury, Swanson was slashing .216/.300/.404 with 18 homers and 66 RBIs. Since June 17, he has a .270 batting average (47-for-174) with 38 RBIs and an .860 OPS.
“Since that time frame, I felt really good and figured some things out as far as what is going to work for me offensively -- hopefully for the rest of my career,” he said.
Swanson’s return means Nico Hoerner goes from shortstop to his original position at second base, while Pedro Ramírez -- who played regularly at second during Swanson’s absence -- returns to the bench.
“It’s been a long time, so I’m really grateful to be back and contribute to this team and to achieve, obviously, something special [like winning the World Series],” Swanson said. “The medical staff and everyone involved with this entire process did all they can to get me back as soon as possible, which I’m grateful for.”

item.content:encoded:
Andres Gimenez Injury: Working through hamstring injury
Gimenez is not in the Blue Jays' starting lineup against the Rangers on Friday due to a hamstring injury, Arden Zwelling of Sportsnet.ca reports.
Gimenez has been working through hamstring soreness for the past couple of days, and while he could be available off the bench Friday, the Blue Jays would prefer for him to rest up and be cleared to return for Saturday's contest. In Gimenez's absence, Ernie Clement will start at shortstop while Josh Smith gets the draw at second base.

item.title: [nbcsports.com] Two-start pitchers: Logan Gilbert fronts a small list of quality options for the season’s final week
item.dc:creator: David Shovein
item.description: Hello and welcome to the final installment of our weekly two-start pitcher article for the 2026 MLB season. If your fantasy league is still playing this week, then every inning matters. You know where you stand in each and every category, and grinding out every additional win or strikeout could be the difference between winning and losing at this stage. item.content:encoded:
Hello and welcome to the final installment of our weekly two-start pitcher article for the 2026 MLB season.
If your fantasy league is still playing this week, then every inning matters. You know where you stand in each and every category, and grinding out every additional win or strikeout could be the difference between winning and losing at this stage. The pickups that are made this week could be what sets you apart from your competition.
This is a living document, so we’ll update the options below as the weekend moves along.
Before we get into it, we’ll start with a couple of notes on situations that may be unresolved or teams that may not have a two-start pitcher lined up for the upcoming week. With teams setting their rotations for the postseason, there are also pitchers who may be held back from making their projected second start, which is definitely something to keep in mind.
⚾️ Baseball is back! MLB returns to NBC and Peacock in 2026! In addition to becoming the exclusive home of Sunday Night Baseball, NBC Sports will broadcast MLB Sunday Leadoff, “Opening Day” and Labor Day primetime games, the first round of the MLB Draft, the entire Wild Card round of the postseason, and much more.
The Dodgers continue to roll with a six-man rotation and will also be interested in setting up their rotation for the postseason, so with only six games on the schedule it’s highly unlikely that any of their starters are going to pitch twice. Yoshinobu Yamamoto will take the ball on Monday and it’s possible that he may get an inning or two on Sunday if someone else (Blake Snell maybe) gets skipped during the week, but he should be locked into lineups regardless of whether it’s one start or two, so there’s no actionable takeaways there.
The Brewers have also been utilizing a six-man rotation for most of the second half and with six games on their docket, it’s unlikely that any of their starters get a two-start week. Jacob Misiorowski is scheduled to start on Monday against the Phillies and it’s possible he could throw a few innings on Sunday as well if the Brewers want him to get the work in. He’s in all fantasy lineups no matter what though, so that wouldn’t change anything.
The Twins have been utilizing a six-man alignment as well down the stretch, so with six games on their schedule that means that everyone will just take the ball once. Bailey Ober is pitching on Monday and would be the beneficiary if any of their other starters were to get skipped during the week, but as of now that seems unlikely. He would make for a decent streaming option though with matchups against the Giants in San Francisco and against the Rangers at home.
The Mets are also rolling with a six-man rotation to end the season, so there are no two-start pitchers there either. Sean Manaea pitches on Tuesday (at Rangers) and could conceivably pitch on Sunday as well (at Nationals) if anyone gets skipped during the week. We’ll update here if anything happens to change.
Someone on the Yankees is likely to make two starts next week, we just aren’t sure whether it’ll be Gerrit Cole or Carlos Rodon. Both are scheduled to pitch in Tuesday’s doubleheader against the Rays and both would be on regular rest for the regular season finale against the Orioles on Sunday. It’s also possible that the Yankees mix in a bullpen game there and no one winds up with the two-start week. If we gain any clarity from Yankees’ skipper Aaron Boone over the weekend, we’ll update here.
Very similar to the Yankees’ situation, we don’t have a clear picture on what the Rays will do with their rotation next week. It looks like Nick Martinez and Drew Rasmussen are lined up for the two games of Tuesday’s doubleheader against the Yankees. One of them could end up pitching again on Sunday and give them a two-start week, but that’ll all depend on how the club plans to structure its rotation for the postseason. Rasmussen should be locked into lineups regardless and Martinez is still a decent option even if it’s just a single-start week.
The Blue Jays’ rotation is extremely short-handed at the moment, leading to much uncertainty on what they will do over the final week of the season. My best guess would be another bullpen day on Monday, and then if the team is still in the mix for a wild card on Sunday, you could see Max Scherzer draw a second start for the week. It’s a gamble for sure if you want to chance that he makes two starts, but it’s one that could wind up paying off.
The Nationals also plan to utilize a six-man rotation over the final week of the season, so none of their underwhelming options are going to wind up making two starts. Unless it was Cade Cavalli though, fantasy managers shouldn’t have interest anyways.
Going Twice…
Note: Probable pitchers as of September 18 and are subject to change.
American League
▶ Strong Plays
Logan Gilbert, Mariners, RHP (vs. Astros, vs. Angels)
While it has been a disappointing season overall for the Mariners in 2026, Gilbert has certainly done his job, posting a 3.69 ERA, 1.06 WHIP and a 194/46 K/BB ratio over 178 innings through his first 30 starts. That’s right in line with what expectations were for the right-hander coming into the season. He’ll look to finish the year strong with a pair of home matchups against familiar divisional foes that he has had all sorts of success against. In a week where the quality two-start options are quite limited, Gilbert represents one of the best overall plays on the board.
Drew Anderson, Tigers, RHP (vs. Nationals, vs. Pirates)
Drew Anderson has pitched very well since joining the Tigers’ rotation in early August, registering a 2.58 ERA, 1.28 WHIP and a 31/19 K/BB ratio over 38 1/3 innings. He draws a pair of really nice matchups to finish the season with both starts coming in the spacious confines of Comerica Park. I know that he’s hard to trust given the limited track record stateside, but Anderson actually makes for a very strong play this week and is someone that I’d start in all formats.
Jake Bennett, Red Sox, LHP (vs. Guardians, vs. Cubs)
Bennett has done a really nice job in his rookie campaign for the Red Sox, compiling a 3.78 ERA, 1.10 WHIP and a 90/20 K/BB ratio across 109 2/3 innings in his 19 starts. His performance has dropped off considerably in the second half though as he seems to be hitting a bit of a wall from a workload perspective. Since July 22 he holds a 5.14 ERA and a 1.32 WHIP over 56 frames. What has still been there is the strikeouts. He has punched out six or more batters in five of his last six starts. If you’re able to absorb the ratio risk and need to make up ground in strikeouts, he’s a strong option this week.
▶ Decent Plays
Cristian Javier, Astros, RHP (at Mariners, at Athletics)
As you can expect after such a long layoff, we have seen plenty of inconsistency in Javier’s performance this season. He appears to have shaken off the rust though and is rounding into form now. Over his last three starts, the 29-year-old hurler holds a 2.20 ERA, 0.98 WHIP and a 15/7 K/BB ratio over 16 1/3 innings of work. That’s enough for me to give him a shot in a two-start week against two familiar divisional foes. Having to pitch at Sutter Health Park to finish the week isn’t ideal, but the A’s offense is limping to the finish line and there aren’t any left-handed bats there that we should be worried about. I’d feel comfortable streaming him in all league sizes.
Daniel Lynch IV, Royals, LHP (vs. White Sox, vs. Guardians)
Lynch has struggled with the transition back to being a full-time starter after spending most of the season in the bullpen. In his first eight starts he holds an uninspiring 5.28 ERA and a 17/11 K/BB ratio over 30 2/3 innings. That’s not helpful at all for fantasy purposes. He has pitched better lately though, allowing just two runs over 10 innings in his last two starts while notching victories in both of them. He gets the opportunity to play spoiler against a pair of divisional rivals this week and the added intensity of those games should lead to quality results. I’d definitely be streaming him in 15-teamers and I may even take the plunge in 12’s if I needed another viable arm.
Shane Baz, Orioles, RHP (vs. Blue Jays, at Yankees)
Baz’s first season with the Orioles can definitely be characterized as a disappointment. He enters the final week of the season with an atrocious 6-15 record, 4.11 ERA and a 1.35 WHIP over 173 innings with just 152 strikeouts along the way. He has been way more hurtful than helpful for fantasy purposes. You should expect more of the same over his final two starts. He could give you 8-10 strikeouts with a chance at a victory, but it’ll likely come at the expense of a poor WHIP and an ERA that isn’t going to be helpful. If that still sounds appealing to you, go ahead and roll the dice.
MacKenzie Gore, Rangers, LHP (vs. Mets, at Twins)
Gore has had another extremely inconsistent season, leading to a disappointing 4.67 ERA, 1.3 WHIP and a 172/69 K/BB ratio over 165 2/3 innings in 32 starts. Even the strikeouts have disappeared lately, with just three in total over 11 innings in his last three starts. It’s possible that the dropoff in production has been due to the heavy workload, in which case, there’s no real reason to expect him to bounce back in a two-start week here. The matchups are good though and in some leagues the 6-8 strikeouts that he’s able to provide here could wind up being the difference at the end of the season.
▶ At Your Own Risk
Foster Griffin, Guardians, LHP (at Red Sox, at Royals)
While Griffin has been a breakout star in 2026 and one of the best waiver wire finds of the season, he has not been the same pitcher since joining the Guardians at the trade deadline and shouldn’t be blindly started in the final week of the season. Over eight starts since the trade he holds a miserable 5.79 ERA, 1.61 WHIP and a 35/15 K/BB ratio across 37 1/3 innings of work. It’s possible that he fixes whatever has been ailing him and gets back on track this week, but the more likely scenario is continued ratio damage. Perhaps the strikeouts and the shot at a victory are worth the trade off, but think twice before locking him into lineups this week.
Yusei Kikuchi, Angels, LHP (at Athletics, at Mariners)
Kikuchi has had a rough season overall, registering a 5.02 ERA and 1.55 WHIP across 57 1/3 innings through his first 12 starts sandwiched around a trip to the injured list. He has also notched just one victory on the year. His performance has been slightly improved since returning from the injured list and he’ll try to finish the season on a high note against two divisional foes. I’m not thrilled about the prospects of using him at Sutter Health Park in West Sacramento, as his long balls woes could lead to a disastrous outing there. I’d only start Kikuchi if I was desperate to make up ground in strikeouts and could afford the hit to my ratios.
Anthony Kay, White Sox, LHP (at Royals, vs. Rockies)
On the surface, a pair of matchups at the Royals and against the Rockies would normally make anyone a strong streaming candidate – especially in the final week of the season. There are some serious red flags to consider here though. Kay has really struggled down the stretch, with a 7.06 ERA over 21 2/3 innings in his last five starts. He also hasn’t completed five innings in any of those outings, and with there being a strong chance that the White Sox will need Sunday’s game to keep their playoff hopes alive, they won’t hesitate to go to the bullpen in that one either. He’s an extremely volatile play this week. He could wind up delivering eight strikeouts and a victory with solid ratios. He could wind up giving you six innings total with three strikeouts and awful ratios. It’s up to your risk tolerance whether you want to take the chance or not.
Brady Basso, Athletics, LHP (vs. Angels, vs. Astros)
Basso has been transitioning to the Athletics’ starting rotation down the stretch, but he has yet to work deeper than four innings in any game so far and is very unlikely to pitch deep enough to earn a victory in either of these starts. The overall results on the season have been mediocre at best and his limited strikeout ability isn’t attractive for streaming purposes. Unless your ratios can’t be impacted by poor performance and you’re desperate for a live body to try to pick up a couple of strikeouts, Basso is best left on the waiver wire.
National League
▶ Strong Plays
Jared Jones, Pirates, RHP (vs. Cardinals, at Tigers)
After shaking off a bit of rust in his return from the injured list, Jones has been terrific for the Pirates and for fantasy managers. Over his last 13 starts, he holds a 3.56 ERA, 1.10 WHIP and an 84/22 K/BB ratio over 65 2/3 innings – and that includes an eight-run debacle against the Mets. He has allowed three earned runs or fewer in each of those 12 other starts. He gets a nice draw for the final week and represents one of the stronger overall options on the board. He should be started in all leagues without question.
Zack Wheeler, Phillies, RHP (vs. Brewers, vs. Rays)
Wheeler is tentatively lined up to start twice next week, though if seeding for the Wild Card is already decided by Sunday, it’s very likely that he’ll get skipped or work in a very limited capacity as the Phillies structure their rotation how they want to for the postseason. That means it’s probable that he’ll only get a single start against the Brewers this week. He’s a strong option and should be started for fantasy leagues regardless, just be aware that he’s probably not going to end up making two starts.
Kevin Gausman, Cubs, RHP (vs. Marlins, at Red Sox)
The Cubs may wind up needing Sunday’s game for seeding purposes, but they’ll have already clinched a postseason berth and will want to align their rotation for the Wild Card series, so it’s possible that Gausman doesn’t wind up making that second start or is limited if he does. He’s still a quality option for the week as he starts off with a strong matchup at home against the Marlins and would be in most fantasy lineups regardless. Just understand that he may not end up making two starts.
▶ Decent Plays
Michael Soroka, Diamondbacks, RHP (at Rockies, at Padres)
If anyone is going to make two starts for the Diamondbacks in the final week of the season, it looks like it’s going to be Soroka. It’s not an easy draw though, as he has to battle the Rockies at Coors Field to start the week before finishing up with the Padres in San Diego. He has pitched well overall on the season and is coming off of a strong start against the Marlins his last time out. You can’t count on the ratios being as strong as they have been given the matchups, but the strikeouts and chances of earning a victory are still there. He makes for a solid streaming option in the season’s final week.
Robbie Ray, Padres, LHP (at Dodgers, vs. Diamondbacks)
As of now, Ray is lined up to make two starts next week, though his availability on Sunday will ultimately be determined by how the Padres choose to line up their rotation for the Wild Card series. Meaning he may end up with just a one-start week against the Dodgers in Los Angeles which is far from ideal. He’s probably still worth using, just understand that he probably doesn’t get two starts and his overall ceiling for the week is greatly diminished.
Andre Pallante, Cardinals, RHP (at Pirates, vs. Brewers)
To the shock and dismay of most fantasy prognosticators, Pallante has actually had himself a nice season in the Cardinals’ rotation, posting a 3.70 ERA, 1.26 WHIP and a 104/47 K/BB ratio over 151 innings while picking up 12 victories. He’s coming off of a brutal start against the Giants though where he was rocked for six runs on eight hits over his five frames. The matchup against the Pirates to start the week looks strong and he could be facing a Brewers’ squad missing most of its regulars on the final day of the season. As long as you keep your expectations in check, he’s a fine streaming option.
Janson Junk, Marlins, RHP (at Cubs, vs. Braves)
Junk has done a nice job logging innings for the Marlins this season, but he hasn’t been very helpful for fantasy purposes, registering a mediocre 4.50 ERA, 1.34 WHIP and a 78/31 K/BB ratio over 114 innings of work. He now has to finish the season battling two of the stronger offenses in the National League, which is most definitely not a recipe for success. He’s also not a big strikeout guy, so if you’re trying to climb in that category, there are probably better options on the board for the ratio hit you could take here. He has a higher floor than most doubles available on the waiver wire if you just need a handful of strikeouts and an outside shot at a win.
Blade Tidwell, Giants, RHP (vs. Twins, vs. Dodgers)
Tidwell has made 16 appearances (eight starts) for the Giants this season, logging a 4.56 ERA, 1.20 WHIP and a 42/21 K/BB ratio over 53 1/3 innings. What he has on his side this week is the strong likelihood that he’ll actually make two starts, and the second one against the Dodgers could come against a bunch of backups on the final day of the season. If you need seven strikeouts, decent ratios and an outside shot at a win, he’s probably worth a shot in deeper mixed and NL-only formats.
▶ At Your Own Risk
Andrew Abbott, Reds, LHP (at Braves, at Blue Jays)
Abbott has really struggled down the stretch for the Reds, compiling a 9.15 ERA over 19 2/3 innings in his last five starts. When he’s on his game, he is able to pile up strikeouts and is a threat to win, but he has not been in that form consistently in quite some time. The matchups are also tough, batting two potential playoff teams on the road. Once again, if your only concern is strikeouts and wins and you are alright taking on the ratio risk, you can fire away. If you care about your ratios at all though, I’d sit this one out.
JR Ritchie, Braves, RHP (vs. Reds, at Marlins)
With AJ Smith-Shawver getting moved back to the bullpen, it looks like JR Ritchie gets an opportunity to close out the season in the Braves’ rotation. His first start back did not go well, giving up six runs over 4 2/3 innings against the Cubs at Wrigley Field. The matchups are a bit better this week, but it’s not enough to trust him if you still have to protect your ratios. If all you’re trying to do is gain ground in wins and strikeouts and you need the volume, go ahead.
Mason Adams, Rockies, RHP (vs. Diamondbacks, at White Sox)
Never Rockies. There’s just no reason to do it, especially in a split week. Adams also hasn’t pitched well this season, posting a 5.09 ERA and 1.65 WHIP over 23 innings in his five starts. The only part that’s mildly appealing is the 23 punchouts. If you are unable to gain or lose ground in ratios and only care about moving up in strikeouts and wins (unlikely here), then you could look to him as a streaming option.

item.content:encoded:
The MLB regular season is rapidly winding down, as there are 9-10 games left on the schedule for all teams.
For the Atlanta Braves, they are opening a new series with the Houston Astros (on the road) this weekend.
If Atlanta wins on Friday, it will clinch a postseason berth. The Braves are still a handful of games back on the Los Angeles Dodgers for the No. 2 seed, but they also have a sizeable lead in the NL East, and barring an epic collapse, should win the division.
Before game one of the Braves-Astros series, Atlanta revealed a small lineup change regarding Ronald Acuña Jr.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Announce Austin Riley Demotion Before Astros Series
Ronald Acuña Jr./Drake Baldwin Flip Spots in Braves Order
In a non-shocking lineup change, Ronald Acuña Jr. will bat second on Friday evening.
Houston is rolling with RHP Peter Lambert, so perhaps manager Walt Weiss liked Drake Baldwin as the leadoff batter, but Ronald and Baldwin steadily flip-flop between the one and two spots.
Courtesy of @UnderdogMLB, here is the full Braves order for 9/18:
Braves 9/18 D. Baldwin DH R. Acuña Jr. RF M. Olson 1B M. Harris II CF M. Dubón SS O. Albies 2B M. Yastrzemski LF A. Riley 3B S. Murphy C T. Mahle SP
Other lineup notes include Sean Murphy forming a batter with starter Tyler Mahle, Austin Riley dropping to 8th in the batting order, and Ozzie Albies also getting a lineup demotion.
For his Houston Astros homecoming, Mauricio Dubon is batting 5th and playing SS.
More MLB on Heavy: Tarik Skubal Shares Eyebrow Raising Comment After Los Angeles Dodgers Clinching Moment

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Pirates' Nick Gonzales Facing Stiff Competition for NL Batting Title

item.content:encoded:
PITTSBURGH — Nick Gonzales has been one of the Pittsburgh Pirates' best hitters, and he could finish as one of the best in baseball.
Gonzales has hit .304/.367/.392 for an OPS of .759 in 141 games for the Pirates, giving him the best batting average and the fourth-best in the National League, with nine games left in the 2026 season.
The Pirates have Gonzales starting at third base in the series opener against the Kansas City Royals at PNC Park on Sept. 18, and it's another chance for him to finish his season strong.
Gonzales also has a realistic chance of winning the NL Batting Title, with Freddy Sanchez the last Pirates player to do so in 2006, batting .344.
Who Gonzales Faces in the NL Batting Title
NL Batting Title Leaders
| Player | Batting Average | Team |
|---|---|---|
| Luis Arraez | .315 | Philadelphia Phillies |
| Gabriel Moreno | .307 | Arizona Diamondbacks |
| Otto Lopez | .306 | Miami Marlins |
| Nick Gonzales | .304 | Pittsburgh Pirates |
| TJ Rumfield | .301 | Colorado Rockies |
Gonzales ranks fourth in the NL and is nine points behind Philadelphia Phillies second baseman Luis Arraez, who leads with a .315 batting average.
Arraez is always towards the top of the batting average leaderboards, winning three straight batting titles from 2022 to 2024, .316 with the Minnesota Twins in 2022, .354 with the Miami Marlins in 2023 and then .314 with both the Marlins and the Padres in 2024.
Moreno is having a career year, like Gonzales, and has never hit above .300 before. He's been excellent in September, batting .333/.410/.611 for a 1.021 OPS.
Lopez is also putting up his best season yet, and has bounced back from a poor August by hitting .316/.418/.404 for an OPS of .822 in September.
Rumfield has been great in his rookie season and at his very best this month, batting .408/.491/.633 for an OPS of 1.124.
Why Gonzales Winning Batting Title Means to Pirates
Gonzales has been a constant for the Pirates on the basepaths and someone they can rely on to get a rally going.
He hit his best in July, .388/.438/.544 for an OPS of .982, but has hit just .260/.352/.323 for an OPS of .675 since the start of August.
Gonzales needs to put up some great numbers to overtake Arraez and the other competition, but it's not impossible.
He's gotten more time at designated hitter than at third base, with his defensive struggles, but he's absolutely been an important part of the Pirates' offense.
"I hope he gets there and I hope he does it," Pirates manager Don Kelly said about Gonzales. "Awesome for him to be in the top of the batting order in the National League, and I hope that he can get up there and win it. He should take pride in that in how he's been able to swing the bat for us. He's had some huge at-bats, and swung the bat well and been a big part of our offensive success this year."
Dominic writes for Pittsburgh Pirates On SI, Pittsburgh Panthers Pn SI and also, Pittsburgh Steelers On SI. A Pittsburgh native, Dominic grew up watching Pittsburgh Sports and wrote for The Pitt News as an undergraduate at the University of Pittsburgh, covering Pitt Athletics. He would write for Pittsburgh Sports Now after college and has years of experience covering sports across Pittsburgh.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yordan Alvarez vs. Junior Caminero for AL MVP: Can a designated hitter win the award?
